notes.facet: Blinn-Phong / specular on a 2D droplet — the warm-cream glint, the highlight that reads as wet glass (AX goo-blob W08 un-flood + W15 lit contained-droplet + W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: IQ 4-tap TETRAHEDRON SDF normal (iquilezles.org/articles/normalsSDF) — derive the surface normal from 4 evaluations of the composite distance field via the k=vec2(1,-1) swizzle pattern (k.xyy·f(p+k.xyy·h)+...), normalize. Half the cost of 6-tap central differences. OUR SHADER ALREADY DOES THIS (surfaceNormal() in metaball.frag.ts) — validation, not a change.

DOME-Z LIFT (height-from-distance) — pseudo-3D normal for a flat 2D blob: interior=clamp(-d/bodyR), z=sqrt(max(0,1-(1-interior)^2)) gives a unit half-sphere profile (flat centre, steep rim); n3=normalize(vec3(grad2d*(1-z), z)) tilts outward at the rim and faces the viewer in the core. This is THE canonical 'make a 2D sticker read as a rounded bead' move. OUR SHADER ALREADY DOES THIS — the warm-cream glint and Fresnel rim ride this normal.

Linear-space Blinn-Phong with HALF-VECTOR — spec=pow(max(dot(N,H),0),shininess)·strength where H=normalize(L+V); compute and ADD the highlight in LINEAR sRGB BEFORE the OETF (linearToSrgb) and before the alpha premultiply, or the highlight double-gammas and fringes the edge. OUR SHADER ALREADY DOES THIS CORRECTLY (the named A5/A2 trap is closed).

NORMALIZED (energy-conserving) Blinn-Phong (interplayoflight.wordpress.com) — multiply the specular term by (shininess+2)/8 (or (n+8)/8π full form) so a tighter highlight (higher shininess) stays equally bright overall instead of dimming. GAP IN OUR SHADER: uSpecShininess is a free knob with no normalization, so tuning shininess silently changes perceived glint brightness and forces re-tuning uSpecStrength. Folding the (n+2)/8 factor decouples the two knobs.

Fresnel-Schlick RIM (inspirnathan part-12, Schlick approximation) — rim=pow(1-max(dot(N,V),0), power); power~5 is a thin sharp rim, ~2-3 a broad halo. Tint by a color (rim·rimColor) and ADD. Grazing-angle edge light = the 'wet meniscus' read. OUR SHADER ALREADY DOES THIS (uRimPower/uRimStrength, fed --foreground via the ColorResolver, attenuated by (1-0.6·thickness) so it rides the rim not the core).

WARM-CREAM specular TINT (not pure white) — physically the highlight reflects the LIGHT color, not the object; a near-white-but-WARM tint reads as a real warm light source, pure-white sRGB reads cheap-CG (Apple Liquid Glass uses warm specular catch-lights). OUR SHADER ALREADY DOES THIS — warmCream = oklabToLinearSrgb(oklchToOklab(vec3(0.97,0.03,radians(85°)))), routed through the same spliced OKLCh matrices.

IQ NORMALIZED smin (iquilezles.org/articles/smin, 2024 rewrite) — k is a TRUE blend-band in DISTANCE units after the kernel-normalization pre-scale (quadratic: k*=4.0; circular: k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5))). Same k → same meniscus width across variants. CRITICAL for W08: a too-large k floods the field negative everywhere. The article also warns the smin'd field is NOT a true SDF — gradient length drops below 1.0 in the blend zone (under-estimates distance), which is EXACTLY why the normal needs a screen-space epsilon, not a fixed one (our shader uses 1.5px/uResolution.y).

SPECULAR ANTIALIASING / roughness-clamp (Toksvig, Tokuyoshi geometric specular AA) — a tight specular power over a high-frequency animated normal (our FBM-displaced membrane) sparkles/strobes frame-to-frame; the fix is to widen the effective highlight where the normal varies (clamp shininess, or fwidth-widen the spec lobe). GAP: our glint rides the time-scrolling fbmWarped normal at shininess 16-64 with no AA — a flicker hazard on the contained droplet, especially when small in a dock grid.

ANIMATED / motion-reactive specular (Apple Liquid Glass; caustics literature) — the highlight that MOVES sells 'liquid'. Apple drives icon specular off the gyroscope; the UI analog is a time/pointer-driven light direction so the glint slides as the blob breathes/leans. This is the bridge to the MOOD MODEL: arousal can scroll the light or specStrength, valence can warm the cream tint.

CIRCULAR vs QUADRATIC smin merge (IQ) — circular smin gives a true quarter-circle fillet (rounder, wetter meniscus) at slightly more cost; quadratic is cheaper but slightly creased. Both already shipped (uMerge dispatch) and BOTH normalized to the same k-band so swapping does not re-tune the seam — the premium-droplet read is the circular variant.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD. The blob's lit-droplet shader is ALREADY SOTA-shaped — the W08/W15/W16 work is a SCALE re-derivation + a default flip + two robustness folds, NOT a shader rewrite. (1) W08 UN-FLOOD is a distance-regime fix grounded in the IQ smin article: k is a blend-band in DISTANCE units, so uSmoothK MUST ride POS_SCALE like every other length. Confirmed live — useMetaballRenderer.ts L437-440 uploads uSmoothK WITHOUT *POS_SCALE while uBodyRadius (L404), uSatRadius (L495), uPointer (L363) all carry it; live composed k≈0.21→effective≈0.84 in a 1.0 UV floods the field negative. Restore POS_SCALE on the upload + re-tune the composed band to ~0.03-0.08 effective. Keep mood.smoothK as a 1.0-centred MULTIPLIER (it already is, L439). The IQ caveat that smin under-estimates distance (gradient<1 in the blend zone) is WHY surfaceNormal() must use the screen-space epsilon it already has — preserve that through any re-derivation. (2) W15 LIT-DROPLET DEFAULT: flip BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.lit:false→true and turn on tasteful low iridescence+SSS; the warm-cream glint, dome-Z normal, and Fresnel rim ALL ALREADY PAINT CORRECTLY but are gated OFF for a 'zero-regression' instinct that the greenfield no-backwards-compat precept forbids. Once W08 contains the body inside ~70-80% of the footprint, thickness stops saturating flat and the rim lands on a CURVED rim INSIDE the clip — the glint resurfaces for free. Derive rimColor + the warm-cream tint from glass-ui warm tokens so the un-themed blob belongs to the cream-glass system. Two robustness folds the SOTA surfaces: (a) ADD the energy-conserving (uSpecShininess+2.0)/8.0 normalization to the Blinn-Phong so shininess and strength decouple (today tuning one re-tunes the other); (b) ADD specular antialiasing — widen the spec lobe where the FBM normal varies (a roughness/fwidth clamp) so the tight glint does not strobe on the animated membrane, critical for small dock-grid instances. (3) MOOD MODEL: the {valence, arousal} circumplex (useBlobMood.ts) already routes iridScale into the sheen; EXTEND it to the lit glint — arousal→specStrength/light-motion (excited sparkles, sleepy is a calm soft sheen), valence→warm-cream tint warmth/brightness. This makes the Apple-style motion-reactive specular emerge from the existing affect surface instead of a parallel system. The max(warmCream·spec, rimLin·rim) combine ALREADY prevents the glint stacking on the rim into a blown hotspot — preserve it. W16: the warmCream tint is a CONSTANT per frame — hoist it out of the per-pixel branch into a uniform (cheap perf trim alongside gating the 4-tap surfaceNormal behind the lit path).
pitfalls: DOUBLE-GAMMA / EDGE FRINGE: the spec+rim highlight MUST be added in LINEAR space before linearToSrgb AND before the *alpha premultiply. A post-OETF add double-gammas the highlight and fringes the premultiplied edge (the named A5/A2 trap, gated by proof:blob-space-gamma). Our shader is correct — do not let a refactor move the highlight after the OETF.

SPECULAR FLICKER/STROBE: a tight specular power (shininess 16-64) over the time-scrolling fbmWarped normal sparkles frame-to-frame — the classic specular-aliasing failure. No AA today. Worse when the blob is small (dock grid) where the normal varies more per pixel. Fix with a roughness/fwidth-based lobe widening; do NOT just crank shininess.

SMIN FIELD IS NOT A TRUE SDF: gradient length < 1.0 in the blend zone (IQ 2024), so a FIXED-epsilon normal shimmers and a constant-scale dome-Z reads wrong near the seam. The screen-space epsilon (1.5px/uResolution.y) and the +1e-6 normalize guard are load-bearing — preserve them through the W15 length-cohort re-derivation.

POS_SCALE PARTIAL MIGRATION RE-FLOODS: W08 restores POS_SCALE on uSmoothK as a MINIMAL fix; W15 must EITHER keep that regime OR re-derive the ENTIRE length cohort (body/sat/orbit/smin/noise) ATOMICALLY with proof:blob-render as the lock — never a partial migration that leaves the smin band in a different distance regime than the radii (that re-floods). §4 note 13 records this; respect the disposition lines.

PURE-WHITE SPECULAR reads cheap-CG: never hardcode sRGB white(1,1,1) for the glint; the warm-cream OKLCh tint (L~0.97,C~0.03,h~85°) is the identity. Equally, do NOT default rimColor to a cold-blue thin-film — the warm-cream-glass identity wants the --foreground warm rim. A var(--primary) blob in dark mode also needs a min-contrast rim floor or it washes out (W15 Slice-13 F3).

UN-NORMALIZED BLINN-PHONG couples the knobs: without the (n+2)/8 factor, raising uSpecShininess dims the glint, so a consumer who tightens the highlight then has to re-raise uSpecStrength — a hidden coupling. Add the energy-conservation factor so the two knobs are orthogonal.

PER-PIXEL CONSTANT WASTE: warmCream is recomputed (two matrix multiplies) every pixel inside the lit branch — hoist to a uniform. Gate the 4-tap surfaceNormal (4 full sceneDist evals = the dominant fragment cost) behind uLit so the flat path stays cheap (W16 perf trim).

LIT-DEFAULT REGRESSION RISK: flipping lit ON by default changes every existing consumer's render. This is CORRECT per the greenfield no-backwards-compat precept, but the proof:blob-render gate must assert luminance VARIANCE across the body (flat fill fails, lit dome passes) so the flip is locked, and a live light/dark side-by-side audit closes the PENDING W9 browserVerify.

sotaTechniques: ANALYTIC-GRADIENT NORMAL (IQ distgradfunctions2d) — a 2D SDF that returns distance in .x and its analytic gradient (∂/∂x,∂/∂y) in .yz gives a unit-length surface normal for free, with no finite-difference probe. The gradient of a true SDF has length 1 everywhere, so it IS the normal; reuses terms already computed in the distance eval so it is 'very cheap' vs a 4-tap or 6-tap central difference. Caveat IQ states explicitly: smin does NOT preserve unit-length gradient near the surface (only far away), but the gradient propagates THROUGH smin by interpolation and is smooth — good enough as a fake normal for rim/Fresnel shading.

SCHLICK FRESNEL = RIM (canonical, the blob already ships it) — rim = pow(1.0 - max(dot(N,V),0.0), p); Schlick's R0=0 approximation. Fresnel (reflection) and rim-light (additive glow) are the SAME shader term; the only difference is semantic — rim is added emissively, Fresnel gates a reflection mix. Exponent p controls falloff width: p~2-3 = broad force-field glow, p~5 = tight bright edge. Lower p = thicker, softer membrane band.

FRESNEL-GLOW TINT (Godot fresnel_glow) — rim contribution = pow(1-dot(N,V), amount) * rimColor * intensity, with the clamp REMOVED so HDR values >1 bloom. Warm-vs-cold is achieved purely by the rimColor RGB (no separate temperature param) — exactly the injected-ColorResolver seam glass-ui already has (uRimColor = var(--foreground) warm by default).

DIRECTIONAL / WRAPPED RIM (asymmetric edge temperature) — modulate the Fresnel rim by dot(N,L) (or a half-Lambert wrap (dot(N,L)*0.5+0.5)) so the rim is BRIGHT/WARM on the lit side and DIM/COOL on the shadow side. Mix two rim tints by the light-facing factor: rimTint = mix(coolRim, warmRim, dot(N,L)*0.5+0.5). This is the 'top-bright bottom-dark' liquid-glass tell — a real lit bead, not a uniform halo. The blob's rim is currently UNIFORM (V is a constant (0,0,1)), so this is a net-new axis.

PER-CHANNEL CHROMATIC DISPERSION AT THE RIM (Maxime Heckel / dispersion loop) — refract R/G/B with three slightly-different IOR ratios (red bends least, blue most) and offset the sampled color per channel; loop a few slides and average to spread the fringe. Dispersion is STRONGEST at grazing angle — i.e. it co-peaks with the Fresnel term, so a (fres-weighted) RGB split on the membrane edge is the single biggest 'thick real glass' vs 'flat glassmorphism' tell. The imadrahmoune liquid-glass piece confirms: offset the R and B sample coords for the aberration; Fresnel decides refract-vs-reflect mix (IOR 1.52 for glass).

FAST SUBSURFACE / TRANSLUCENT BACK-LIGHT (Barré-Brisebois GDC'11, via Alan Zucconi) — back = pow(saturate(dot(V, -(L + N*distortion))), power) * scale; a distortion param deflects the outgoing back-light along the normal so thin rims glow as light wraps THROUGH them. The blob already ships this (uSssScale/uSssPower); the SOTA refinement is the explicit DISTORTION knob deflecting -(L+N*thickness), and weighting it by (1-thickness) so it leaks only at the thin membrane edge.

ENVIRONMENT-REFLECTION COLORING (Codrops droplet, Yuki Kojima 2025) — instead of a flat tint, color the droplet by sampling noise/an env in reflect(rayDir,N) and crush with pow(color, vec3(7.0)) to suppress mids into glass highlights. An alternative to Fresnel-additive for a more 'wet/specular' read; the blob's warm-cream specular already approximates the highlight-crush.

IQ COSINE PALETTE FOR IRIDESCENCE (already shipped) — a+b*cos(2pi(c*t+d)) maps the Fresnel/edge angle onto a HUE offset; the blob biases it to a warm arc (uIridHue) and caps chroma to a pearl band. SOTA-correct; the refinement is driving t off the analytic-gradient normal + thickness rather than only fres+colorNoise.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for our blob (it ALREADY ships Fresnel rim + warm-cream specular + warm-iridescence cosine palette + fast-SSS in metaball.frag.ts — these are refinements, not a build). 1) THE W15/W16 KEYSTONE PERF+QUALITY WIN: surfaceNormal() in metaball.frag.ts does a SEPARATE 4-tap finite-difference probe of sceneDist (5 SDF evals/pixel) to get grad2d, while watercolor-edges.glsl ALREADY computes IQ analytic-gradient noise (noised() returns the exact gradient in .yz from ONE eval). Per IQ distgradfunctions2d, the SDF gradient IS the free unit-normal. W16 explicitly asks to 'gate the 4-tap surfaceNormal behind the lit path' for fragment cost — the deeper fix is to PROPAGATE the analytic gradient through the smin chain (smin interpolates the .yz gradient, IQ's vec2 material-blend smin variant the README already cites) so the rim normal rides the field the alpha is cut from with NO extra taps. This also fixes a latent bug-class: the 4-tap normal on the smin+domain-warped field is not unit-gradient so it shimmers (the code's own comment admits the screen-space epsilon hack). 2) WARM-vs-COLD RIM = the missing emotional axis tied to the mood model. Today uRimColor is one tint and V is constant (0,0,1), so the rim is a UNIFORM warm halo. Make it DIRECTIONAL: rim *= modulate by dot(N, uLightDir) (the lit-side warm, shadow-side cool) AND wire the rim TEMPERATURE to useBlobMood's valence axis — high valence (happy/excited) = warm rimColor toward --foreground/gold; low valence (sleepy/curious-cold) = cooler rim. The MoodParams already carries iridScale; add a rimWarmth/rimTemp scalar derived from valence (paramsFor already warms hue by valence — extend the same surface to the rim). This makes the rim the primary 'mood read' on the silhouette W15 wants. 3) W15 CONTAINED-DROPLET DEPENDENCY: the rim only reads correctly once W08 un-floods the SDF (k≈0.84 floods the field negative → thickness saturates flat → rim renders OUTSIDE the clip, the named slice-12 F0). The rim/normal must re-anchor on the contained body (thickness = -d/bodyR maps to a real curved dome inside the ~70-80% footprint). Ship lit+rim ON by default (W15 deletes the 'zero regression' flag-gating) with rimColor=var(--foreground) so the un-themed blob is warm-cream by identity and has a min-contrast rim in BOTH light/dark (slice-13 F3 dark-mode washout). 4) THE GENUINE NEW MATERIAL ATOM = per-channel chromatic dispersion ON the membrane edge, fres-weighted (it co-peaks with Fresnel). A cheap 3-tap RGB split of the color (or the iridescence hue) along the gradient direction, scaled by fres*dispersionAmount, is the 'thick glass' tell the AS visual audit named as the single biggest liquid-glass differentiator — and it lands as per-pixel ALU on the already-running fragment, no new pass (consistent with the README's 'no new pass/rAF' perf charter). Keep it a LOW taste-first default + opt-in knob, congruent with the warm-pearl-not-garish identity. 5) ColorResolver SEAM is already correct: uRimColor flows through the injected resolver (resolveRimColor → value.js var()-unwrap), so a warm/cool rim is fully token-authorable and value.js's fork repatriation (W16 close-criterion) inherits it for free. W16 should hoist the duplicated var()-unwrap into one resolveTokenColor leaf as flagged.
pitfalls: smin BREAKS the unit-gradient SDF near the surface (IQ explicit): an analytic-gradient normal taken straight from the smin output is only ~true far from the seam. Mitigate by using IQ's vec2 material/gradient-blend smin (interpolate the .yz gradient by the same h the distance uses) — do NOT just renormalize a garbage gradient at the meniscus or the rim creases at every satellite seam.

RIM/SPEC/SSS MUST stay in LINEAR before the OETF — the blob's metaball.frag already adds highlight in linear before linearToSrgb(); a post-OETF rim double-gammas and fringes the premultiplied edge (the named A5/A2 trap, proof:blob-space-gamma + proof:blob-color-equivalence lock it). Any new dispersion/directional-rim term must enter lin BEFORE the OETF and BEFORE the *alpha premultiply.

The rim is INVISIBLE until W08 un-floods the field. If uSmoothK floods k≈0.84 across a 1.0 UV, thickness saturates to 1 everywhere, fres→0, and the rim renders outside the clip — tuning rim params on a flooded field is wasted. W08 (POS_SCALE restore + ~0.03-0.08 effective band) is a hard prerequisite for any rim work; do not re-derive rim before the contained silhouette exists.

Chromatic dispersion is a banding/cost trap if over-looped. A multi-slide refract loop (Heckel uses ~LOOP iterations) is fine for a textured-backdrop refraction but the blob has NO backdrop texture to sample — it would dispersely offset its OWN color field. Keep it a cheap 2-3 tap fres-weighted hue/channel offset, not a full refraction loop; an IGN dither (the blob/aurora already ship one) kills the warm-cream rim banding the README flags.

Directional rim can over-darken the shadow side and break the min-contrast-rim requirement (slice-13 F3): a pure dot(N,L) modulation can zero the rim on the unlit half, leaving a half-blob with no edge in dark mode. Use a half-Lambert WRAP (dot*0.5+0.5) or a floor so the cool side still carries a minimum rim — the W15 'every grid blob paints visibly against light/dark' gate will catch a zeroed shadow rim.

Fresnel/rim attenuation by thickness is already (1 - 0.6*thickness); stacking a second thickness gate from a re-anchored normal can double-attenuate and kill the rim entirely on the small W15 body. Re-tune rimStrength against the NEW contained bodyRadius (W15 explicitly re-balances magnitudes against the smaller body), don't inherit the W9 values tuned on the oversize body.

max(warmCream*spec, rimLin*rim) is intentional (keeps the glint from stacking into a blown hotspot) — a naive additive combine of spec+rim+dispersion+SSS re-introduces the specular-blowout class W09 is separately fixing on .glass-material. Keep the max() ceiling discipline when adding the directional/dispersion terms.

Removing the 4-tap normal entirely is gated on the analytic gradient propagating through BOTH the smin loop AND the domain-warp (fbmWarped) displacement — the warp perturbs the body edge, so the body's effective normal is sdCircle's radial gradient PLUS the FBM gradient (noised().yz is already available). If you analytic-gradient the circle but ignore the FBM membrane gradient, the rim won't track the living-edge wobble W15 wants. Compose both gradients or keep a cheaper 2-tap on the composite.

notes.facet: Iridescence — thin-film interference, warm-biased (cream/gold not cold-blue), the soap-bubble sheen budget
sotaTechniques: PHYSICAL THIN-FILM OPD MODEL (Belcour-Barla 2017, the glTF KHR_materials_iridescence canon). The hue is NOT a free artistic choice — it is set by an Optical Path Difference OPD = 2 * filmIOR * thickness * cos(theta_refracted), converted to a per-channel phase 2*pi*OPD/lambda, then summed against pre-integrated SENSITIVITY basis functions (DC + harmonics m=1,2) to get an RGB reflectance. This is the analytic RGB approximation that replaced per-wavelength spectral sampling and is the industry default. Mechanism: thickness + view angle jointly pick which wavelengths constructively interfere, so the color shifts across the surface and with the camera.

SPECTRAL-ZUCCONI6 wavelength->RGB bump approximation (Alan Zucconi). A branchless sum of parabolic bumps (bump3y) maps a wavelength in [400,700]nm to an RGB triple, used inside a small loop over interference orders n: u = filmIOR*2*d*cos(thetaR); for n in 1..3 { color += spectral_zucconi6(u/n); }. Mechanism: gives a physically-plausible iridescent ramp without a LUT texture; the exact 6-parabola coefficient set is published GLSL (c1/x1/y1 + c2/x2/y2).

IQ COSINE PALETTE (a + b*cos(2*pi*(c*t+d))) as the cheap stylized iridescence — what the blob already uses. Mechanism: one cos evaluation maps a scalar t (here Fresnel + noise + animated thickness) onto a smooth color ramp. The SOTA refinement for a WARM, subtle sheen is to (1) drive it in a perceptual space (OKLCh hue, as the blob does) OR drive an RGB cosine with a narrow warm vec3 d-phase, (2) keep frequency c LOW (~0.2-0.5, well under 1.0) so t never wraps the full hue circle, and (3) cap chroma to a pale-pearl band.

FRESNEL/SCHLICK VIEW-ANGLE GATE (Schlick: F = pow(1 - dot(N,V), p)). Iridescence is fundamentally view-/angle-dependent — it must ride the grazing-angle rim, not the flat-facing core. Mechanism: weight the iridescent term by a Fresnel factor (p~2-3) so the sheen concentrates where the dome curves away from the viewer (the rim), exactly the soap-bubble read. The blob already computes this (fres = pow(1-dot(N,V),2.5)).

WARM-RESTRICTED SPECTRUM / COLOR-TEMPERATURE BIAS. To get cream/gold/peach not cold-blue: clamp the effective wavelength band to the warm arc (~560-620nm, gold->peach) OR center the OKLCh hue on a warm anchor (~85deg, the blob's uIridHue) and let the cosine sweep only +/- a narrow arc (the blob's 0.18*PI ~ 32deg). Mechanism: thicker films and longer-wavelength bias push toward warm reds/golds; thinner films/short wavelengths give cold blue/violet — so a warm identity = a thicker-film, long-wavelength-weighted, narrow-arc choice.

ANIMATED FILM THICKNESS as the living-shimmer driver. Scroll the thickness term (or the cosine t) slowly over time + over the FBM noise field so the sheen drifts like a real soap film thinning/thickening, rather than a static decal. The blob does this via uIridSpeed and +0.3*colorNoise into t. Mechanism: a per-pixel time/noise offset on the interference phase makes the bands crawl.

PRE-INTEGRATION-TO-NEUTRAL / GAUSSIAN SPECTRAL FILTER (Belcour-Barla anti-aliasing). For thick or noisy films the physical model converges to neutral gray and the fixed-RGB-wavelength approach produces high-frequency color banding; Belcour pre-integrates interference with Fourier/Gaussian filtering so thick films go gray and bands don't alias. Mechanism: convolve the spectral response so sub-pixel thickness variation averages out instead of sparkling.

OUTPUT DITHER (1-LSB Interleaved Gradient Noise on gl_FragCoord). The standard fix for 8-bit banding on a low-chroma smooth ramp — aurora already ships exactly this. Mechanism: add a +/-0.5/255 IGN-keyed jitter before the 8-bit quantization so a slow low-contrast warm gradient (the iridescent rim + the warm-cream dome) reads as smooth, not stepped.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for OUR blob (metaball.frag.ts:303-321 is the existing iridescence block). (1) KEEP the IQ-cosine-in-OKLCh-hue approach — it is the correct cheap choice for a sub-2415-module per-pixel UI substrate; a full Belcour OPD model is overkill for a decorative droplet and would fight the OKLCh round-trip already in place. The current block is already SOTA-shaped: warm hue center (uIridHue~85deg), narrow arc (0.18*PI), Fresnel-weighted (fres*uIridescence), chroma-capped, animated (uIridSpeed). (2) W15 BUDGET FLIP is the real headline: the iridescence already executes correctly but is DEFAULT-OFF (types.ts:185 iridescence:0.0) and swamped by the oversize field — W15 ships a LOW warm-pearl FLOOR on by default (~0.06-0.12), and W08/W15 containment resurfaces it onto the now-curved contained rim where Fresnel actually has a gradient to ride. (3) MOOD MODEL: iridScale (useBlobMood.ts:51, lerp 0.4->1.8 by arousal) is the correct circumplex hook — excited shimmers, sleepy goes flat; after the default-on flip, re-check the excited ceiling so 1.8*floor does not over-saturate into garish thin-film (the W15 FileBounds already flags this in useBlobMood). (4) ADOPT a thin physical tilt WITHOUT a rewrite: feed the cosine t a thickness-from-(-d) term (thickness already computed at frag:300) so the sheen tracks real film-thickness (thicker core->warmer, thin rim->slightly cooler-within-warm) — this is the cheapest borrow from the OPD model and reads more like glass. (5) BORROW spectral_zucconi6 ONLY if a future preset wants a richer oil-slick look — keep it behind a preset, never the warm-cream default (presets-in-consumers). (6) SHIP THE DITHER: add the aurora IGN 1-LSB dither (the blob README flags it planned/unshipped) before the OETF output — this is the single highest-value missing piece for the warm-pearl sheen because a low-chroma warm ramp on a near-flat dome is the textbook banding case.
pitfalls: BANDING is the #1 hazard for THIS facet. A warm-pearl sheen is low-chroma + low-contrast over a near-flat warm-cream dome — exactly the 8-bit gradient case that steps visibly. The blob has NO output dither (aurora does, via IGN). Ship the 1-LSB IGN dither before linearToSrgb or the subtle sheen will look stepped on real 8-bit displays.

COLD-BLUE DRIFT. A naive cosine palette or a full spectral_zucconi6 sweep wraps through blue/violet and breaks the warm-cream identity. Must center on a warm hue and clamp the sweep arc narrow (the blob's 0.18*PI is right); a high cosine frequency c>=1.0 re-introduces the cold arc. Watch any t that can grow unbounded (fres+noise+time) from pushing the hue past the warm band.

GARISH/RAINBOW over-saturation. Iridescence reads cheap-CG the moment chroma goes high. Keep the warm-pearl chroma cap (blob caps at +0.08 OKLCh C) and keep the default weight LOW. The mood iridScale up to 1.8x can blow the cap on the now-default-on floor — re-tune after the W15 default flip.

DOUBLE-GAMMA / WRONG-SPACE trap (the named A5/A2). Iridescence must be mixed in OKLCh BEFORE gamutClampOklch and BEFORE the mandatory linearToSrgb OETF (the blob does this correctly). Adding a thin-film RGB term post-OETF, or skipping the OETF, ships ~2.2x too dark and fringes the premultiplied edge. Any new thin-film color must enter the existing linear/OKLCh pipeline, not as a tacked-on sRGB add.

FILL-RATE. The fragment already runs FBM x2 + a full OKLCh round-trip per pixel; a per-wavelength spectral_zucconi6 loop over interference orders adds real ALU. For the default warm-pearl sheen the single-cos OKLCh-hue path is cheaper and sufficient — do NOT swap to the loop-over-orders model for the default. Gate any spectral upgrade behind a preset + the planned quality:half axis.

FRESNEL ON A NON-UNIT-GRADIENT SDF. The iridescence rides the surface normal from the 4-tap tetrahedron gradient of a smin+domain-warped field, which is NOT a unit-gradient SDF — a too-small epsilon shimmers (the blob already uses a screen-space ~1.5px eps + 1e-6 guard). If the sheen sparkles at the rim, the normal eps is the cause, not the palette.

VIEW-ANGLE STATICITY. A 2D billboard blob has a FIXED view vector V=(0,0,1); real iridescence shifts with camera. The only motion sources are the animated thickness + the FBM field + the breath/wobble. Without animating thickness the sheen reads as a static decal (a dead arc), which is the same dead-membrane failure W15 fixes for geometry — keep uIridSpeed non-zero and tie it to the de-synced breath, not the mechanical sin pulse.

CONTRAST-IN-DARK-MODE. The warm-pearl lift brightens the rim; on a var(--primary) blob in dark mode the whole dome can wash toward the sheen. W15 already mandates a foreground-aware min-contrast rim guard — verify the iridescence lift does not defeat it (the sheen must stay legible without blowing the rim into the page).

notes.facet: Fake subsurface-scattering — thickness-driven inner glow, the translucent-pigment look (for glass-ui's WebGL2 metaball goo-blob, W08 un-flood + W15 lit contained-droplet + W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: FROSTBITE/ZUCCONI WRAP-BACKLIGHT (the canonical fast-SSS term, GDC 2011 Barre-Brisebois). Mechanism: a half-vector H=normalize(L + N*distortion) bent backward by the normal, then I=pow(saturate(dot(V,-H)), power)*scale gives a soft glow where the camera looks toward a light hiding BEHIND the thin part of the body — translucency on the cheap. OUR BLOB ALREADY SHIPS A VARIANT of this (metaball.frag.ts:332-336, `back = pow(clamp(dot(V,-(L+N*thickness)),0,1), uSssPower)`), but it (a) reuses `thickness` as the distortion delta instead of a dedicated `uSssDistortion` knob, and (b) is missing the canonical *ambient* SSS floor term. Full-screen cost on a 2011 console was ~0.6-1.0ms; in our single-droplet 2D case it is a handful of ALU ops.

THICKNESS-AS-INVERSE-AO, COMPUTED ANALYTICALLY FROM THE SDF (the headline win for a 2D blob). Mechanism: thickness is the inverse of ambient occlusion — AO fires rays OUTWARD and measures emptiness, thickness fires rays INWARD and measures how much body is behind a point. In 3D you bake a thickness texture or render back-face depth; in OUR 2D SDF the interior distance `-d` IS the thickness, FOR FREE — `thickness = clamp(-d/bodyR, 0, 1)` (already in metaball.frag.ts:300). This is the cheap structural advantage the W08/W15 waves should lean into: no thickness pass, no second render target, the field already hands us a per-pixel volume estimate. The two consumers are the inner-glow lift (bright where thick) and the backlight gate (light leaks where THIN), which is exactly the (1.0 - thickness) attenuation in the modern Alisavakis form.

BEER-LAMBERT INNER GLOW (physically-grounded replacement for the current linear `oklch.x += coreGlow*thickness`). Mechanism: real translucent pigment attenuates light exponentially with path length — transmitted = exp(-absorption * thickness). For the inner-luminosity lift this means the core should ride a `1 - exp(-k*thickness)` saturating curve (or the glow color = bodyColor * exp(-absorptionRGB * (1-thickness)) for a tinted leak), NOT a linear ramp. The exponential curve reads as real pigment density (a flat plateau in the thick core, a fast warm falloff near the rim) where the current linear lift reads as a uniform brightening. This is a one-line swap of the falloff function on the SAME free `-d` thickness scalar.

WAVELENGTH-DEPENDENT WARM SHIFT IN THIN AREAS (the physically-correct route to the warm-cream identity — GPU Gems 16 / pre-integrated skin). Mechanism: scattering is broadest in RED, then green, almost none in blue, so light exiting a THIN edge shifts warm/red (the lit-to-shadow color bleed you see in ears, nostrils, a hand over a flashlight). For our blob this means the SSS/backlight term should not just lift LIGHTNESS — it should bias HUE warm proportional to (1-thickness), so the thin rim glows cream/gold and the thick core stays the base color. Our shader already nods at this (`oklch.z += sss*0.1`) but the warm shift is a fixed tiny constant; the SOTA move is to make the hue bias scale with thinness and route through OKLCh so it stays perceptually warm, not garish. This is the single most identity-aligned technique: it makes the translucency itself carry the warm-cream signature rather than a separately-tuned iridescence layer.

CURVATURE-DRIVEN SSS WIDTH (pre-integrated SSS, the modern dome-aware refinement). Mechanism: subsurface glow is wider where the surface curves more gently and tighter where it curves sharply — the scatter radius tracks local curvature. We already compute a surface normal via the IQ 4-tap tetrahedron gradient (surfaceNormal, metaball.frag.ts:221); the rate-of-change of that normal (or simply the Fresnel `fres` we already have) is a free curvature proxy. Modulating the SSS/inner-glow falloff by curvature makes the highlight roll across a believable sphere (exactly W15's stated goal: 'the dome highlight rolls across a believable sphere instead of saturating flat') rather than reading as a flat radial vignette keyed only off `-d`.

INTERLEAVED GRADIENT NOISE (IGN) DITHER ON THE GLOW (banding antidote — mandatory for smooth low-contrast inner gradients on an 8-bit canvas). Mechanism: a thickness-driven glow is a wide, low-contrast luminance ramp — the exact signal that bands on an 8-bit framebuffer. IGN (`fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(gl_FragCoord.xy, vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715))))`) adds a sub-LSB ordered-noise offset before quantization and beats plain hash/Bayer dithering at hiding the steps. The README claims an IGN dither already exists (README.md:260) — W15/W16 must VERIFY it actually rides the new lit/SSS terms (the lit block was default-OFF, so the dither may never have been exercised on the glow it is meant to smooth) and that it is applied post-OETF in display space, where banding is visible.

AMBIENT/HALF-LAMBERT TRANSLUCENCY FLOOR (the missing term that keeps the dark side from going dead). Mechanism: the canonical Frostbite form adds an ambient SSS term `+ ambient` so the body retains a soft translucent base-glow even where no backlight reaches — a paper-lantern floor. Without it, the un-lit hemisphere of the droplet reads opaque/dead. A small constant `uSssAmbient` added into the backlight intensity (and ideally tinted toward the warm subsurface color) gives the whole droplet the 'lit from within' read the W15 lit-warm-glass identity is after, not just a rim sheen.

pitfalls: WASH-OUT / blown core: a linear `oklch.x += coreGlow*thickness` saturates lightness to 1.0 in the thick center and reads as a flat white blob, killing the base color and the dome read. The Beer-Lambert saturating curve fixes this, but ALSO clamp/cap the total L lift — the current code does three independent `min(oklch.x + X, 1.0)` lifts (coreGlow, sss, iridescence, lit-spec) that STACK and can collectively blow the core. Budget the combined lightness lift, don't add four uncapped terms.

THICKNESS PINS TO 1.0 ON THE FLOODED/OVERSIZE FIELD: because thickness = -d/bodyR and the W08 flood makes -d huge everywhere, the SSS gradient is invisible pre-W08 (uniform glow). This is the exact 'executes but paints nothing' trap — verify the SSS visually AFTER un-flood + containment, never trust that the term 'is wired.'

NON-UNIT-GRADIENT SDF breaks thickness magnitude: smin + domain-warped FBM is NOT a unit-gradient SDF, so `-d` is only approximately proportional to true interior distance — thickness is a heuristic, not metric. Fine for a look, but don't build physically-exact Beer-Lambert absorption coefficients on it; tune by eye. The `/bodyR` normalize already papers over most of the scale drift.

BANDING on the low-contrast glow: a wide thickness ramp on an 8-bit canvas bands hard, especially in dark mode where the luminance steps are most visible. The IGN dither must actually be applied to the glow in display space (post-OETF) and must be re-verified now that the lit/SSS path is default-ON (it may have been dead code while lit:false).

WARM SHIFT GOING GARISH: routing the SSS hue warm-shift through raw RGB (not OKLCh) or with too large a magnitude tips cream-gold into orange/sickly. Keep the hue bias in OKLCh, clamp chroma to a pale-pearl band (the shader already does this for iridescence — reuse the cap), and scale by (1-thickness) so only the thin rim warms.

DOUBLE-COUNTING SSS vs IRIDESCENCE vs FRESNEL RIM: the shader has THREE rim-weighted warm terms (iridescence cosine palette, fake-SSS backlight, Blinn-Phong/Fresnel lit rim) that all brighten+warm the edge. Turned on together at floor levels they can stack into a blown halo. Use max() not + between competing highlights (the lit block already does `max(warmCream*spec, rimLin*rim)`) and keep the SSS as the INTERIOR-glow specialist (thick→core) while Fresnel owns the rim, so they occupy different spatial regions instead of fighting.

OVERLOADING `thickness` AS THE BACKLIGHT DISTORTION DELTA (current bug-smell): metaball.frag.ts:333 uses `N*thickness` as the half-vector bend, coupling the SSS spread to body depth in a way the canonical formula doesn't intend (distortion is a material constant ~0.1-0.5). It happens to look okay but is non-canonical and hard to tune; give it a dedicated `uSssDistortion` so the spread and the depth-attenuation are independent knobs.

PERF: the SSS/lit path needs the surfaceNormal 4-tap (4 extra sceneDist evaluations = 4x the FBM cost per pixel). W16 explicitly gates this behind the lit path — but since W15 makes lit the DEFAULT, that gate no longer saves anything on the common case. Pair with W16's pre-FBM bounding discard (skip transparent pixels before any FBM) and the half-res quality axis so the now-default lit droplet doesn't tax weak GPUs.

sotaTechniques: IQ NORMALIZED QUADRATIC SMOOTH-MIN (W08 un-flood keystone): smin k*=4.0 then min(a,b)-h*h*k*0.25 — the 4.0 multiply and 1/4=g(0) coefficient are the NORMALIZATION making k a literal blend-band WIDTH in distance units (= max shape inflation = bbox expansion). Blending only where |a-b|<k; a k too large for the field keeps that true everywhere so the whole canvas merges negative (the 84.1% flood). Our sdf-body.glsl already has k*=4.0; the flood was the MISSING POS_SCALE on uSmoothK plus composed k~0.84 in a 1.0 UV. Confirms W08 verbatim: k is a length, must ride POS_SCALE, retune to ~0.03-0.08 effective.

IQ CIRCULAR SMOOTH-MIN (our merge:circular variant): kernel g(x)=1+0.5(x-sqrt(2-x^2)), normalize by 1/(1-sqrt(0.5)). Produces an exact circular-arc meniscus vs the quadratic's parabolic approximation — a wetter, more liquid body/satellite join, the right default for a contained droplet. Same normalized-k contract, so switching variant does not re-flood.

IQ COSINE PALETTE color(t)=a+b*cos(2pi(c*t+d)) (our iridescence sheen + a candidate ramp engine): a=bias, b=amplitude/contrast, c=frequency, d=per-channel phase=hue. Low b and a narrow c keeps it IN-FAMILY (warm gold->peach, never cold blue). metaball.frag already does this in HUE space for the rim sheen (uIridHue + 0.18*PI*cos) — textbook-correct. The same form could drive the body ramp continuously.

OKLCh PERCEPTUALLY-UNIFORM RAMP, equal-chroma/varying-L (the in-family backbone): equal numeric steps = equal perceived steps; holding C and the hue band while marching L gives stops of EQUAL VISUAL WEIGHT that read as one family — exactly deriveBlobPalette's L-spread-shared-hue structure. SOTA refinement: ease the L ramp (lame/sine/power), bell the C across the ramp (peak mid) — our chromaBump*sin(PI*t) IS that bell.

OKLCh HUE-ARC SELECTION to dodge the grey dead-zone (our HARMONY_METHOD map): the short arc can cut through the achromatic axis (muddy grey midpoint on a warm<->cool pair); the long arc stays saturated. Our map routes complementary/split-complementary to longer, analogous/monochrome to shorter, triad/tetradic to increasing — canonical CSS-Color-4 hue-interpolation-method strategy applied correctly.

OKLab MIDPOINT-GREY COMPENSATION (the chroma-bump): a linear OKLab mix of two vivid stops dips chroma through grey at the midpoint (rectangular a/b passes near neutral); the fix is a midpoint chroma LIFT. deriveBlobPalette does it in JS and samplePaletteOklch redoes it in GLSL (0.03*sin) — correct but DUPLICATED with a hardcoded 0.03.

CSS-COLOR-4 GAMUT MAPPING via hue-preserving chroma reduction (our gamutMapStop + in-shader gamutClampOklch): pull an out-of-gamut OKLCh stop inward on chroma holding L and h, so hue never shifts on clamp. gamutMapStop runs value.js Ottosson gamutMapOKLab then a 6-iter 0.999 chroma-shrink; the shader mirrors it. W3C-recommended; the extreme-corner caveat is why the bounded nudge + linear re-check exist.

RUSSELL CIRCUMPLEX AFFECT + VALDEZ-MEHRABIAN color-emotion mapping (our useBlobMood): a 2-axis valence/arousal core, named moods as points; saturation and brightness drive pleasure/arousal MORE than hue (warm/high-brightness=high-valence, low-saturation/cool=calm). useBlobMood already derives all MoodParams from one valence/arousal surface — strongly SOTA-aligned. Underused leg: valence should also warm/cool the palette ANCHOR HUE, not just the perturbation amplitudes.

FRESNEL-WEIGHTED FAKE-SSS + THICKNESS WRAP-LIGHTING for the lit gel droplet (our W9.b lit block): thickness from -d/bodyR (the SDF interior depth) drives core glow; a wrap/back-light term fakes light leaking through the thin rim; a Schlick Fresnel concentrates sheen on the curved rim. The SDF IS the free thickness oracle — the cheap-SSS substitute for UV-blur summation. Our shader does all three in LINEAR before the OETF (correct). Only PAINTS once the body is CONTAINED so thickness doesn't saturate flat.

notes.facet: Mood / expression model — the {valence, arousal} 2-axis mapping to motion energy + sheen (excited / sleepy / curious) for the WebGL2 metaball goo-blob
sotaTechniques: Russell's Circumplex Model of Affect (the V/A 2-axis core): emotions are POINTS in a continuous {valence (pleasant -1..+1), arousal (calm 0..1)} plane rather than a discrete enum; the 5 named moods are samples of ONE principled surface, not 5 hand-tuned param sets. This is exactly what our useBlobMood.ts MOOD_AVA + paramsFor() already does, and it is the academically-canonical model for affect-driven animation (dancers/mocap span the V/A axes; facial-expression engines compute V/A coordinates). KEEP this as the spine.

Laban Movement Analysis (LMA) Effort factors as the V/A->motion bridge: the four Effort dimensions Weight (Strong<->Light force), Time (Sudden<->Sustained acceleration), Space (Direct<->Indirect path), Flow (Bound<->Free control). The validated finding is that motion FACTORS (stiffness/speed/spatial-extent) modulate the felt valence+arousal. This gives a NAMED rubric for which uniform each axis drives: arousal -> Time (pulseFreq/orbitSpeed = Sudden when high) + Weight (pulseAmp/wobble = Strong/bouncy when high); valence -> Flow (Free/smooth-eased vs Bound/jittery) + the lean-in/shy pointer (Space-Direct toward cursor when pleasant). Our model already does arousal->energy and valence->palette+lean; LMA says ALSO route valence onto FLOW (easing smoothness / jitter) not only color.

PAD model's third axis — Dominance: the games/affective-agent literature (OCC, PAD pleasure-arousal-dominance, GAMYGDALA) adds a Dominance/control axis beyond V/A. For the blob this is exactly the pointer lean-IN (dominant/confident, reaches toward cursor) vs shy-AWAY (submissive, recoils) behaviour we already derive from valence*arousal in paramsFor's pointerAttraction. Worth naming it explicitly as the latent 3rd axis so the lean-in is principled, not ad-hoc — but DO NOT add a full 3rd config axis (KISS / no-overfit): keep it derived from V/A as today.

Mood-vs-Emotion temporal split (homeostatic baseline + decaying event spikes): affective-computing dynamics research is unanimous that emotion states DECAY toward a homeostatic baseline (set-point) over time, and that MOOD (slow baseline) is distinct from EMOTION (fast event-triggered spike). The SOTA shape: a slow-drifting baseline mood + transient emotion impulses that elicit fast then regress to baseline. Our `excitedHoldMs` latch (click -> excited held ~0.9s then relaxes) + the 6s idle drift-to-sleepy is precisely this homeostasis pattern. The refinement SOTA suggests: make the return-to-baseline a continuous exponential decay (a spring/critically-damped relax to the idle set-point) rather than the current hard hold-then-snap, so excitement bleeds off smoothly — and let arousal itself decay toward an idle set-point when no interaction sustains it.

Expressive-vs-Productive easing duality (motion-design canon, LottieFiles/design-systems): functional motion uses linear/productive easing; emotion-driven motion uses EXPRESSIVE easing (anticipation + overshoot + settle). For the blob the arousal axis should pick the easing CURVE, not just the speed: high arousal -> springy overshoot easing on the mood cross-fade + bouncier pulse (Disney squash-stretch/overshoot); low arousal -> long ease-out, no overshoot. Today useBlobMood uses one fixed easeInOut for every transition; SOTA = let the target mood's arousal select the transition easing (excited=overshoot spring, sleepy=slow ease-out).

Energy->motion AND energy->sheen co-modulation (the headline coupling): the premium-organic-UI idiom couples a single 'energy/liveliness' scalar to BOTH kinetics and surface optics so excitement reads on the silhouette AND the material. Our paramsFor already does this (arousal drives orbitSpeed/wobble/pulse/noise AND iridScale for the iridescence+SSS sheen). SOTA validation: liveliness in the Codrops droplet comes from constant surface shimmer + trail-responsive geometry TOGETHER, not motion alone. So the excited blob should shimmer MORE (iridescence up, faster iridSpeed scroll, brighter coreGlow) while it also moves more — a unified energy term, which is the correct architecture.

Normalized quadratic smin as the contained-merge primitive (IQ 2024 rewrite) — the un-flood math: smin(a,b,k){ k*=4.0; h=max(k-abs(a-b),0)/k; return min(a,b)-h*h*k*0.25; }. After the k*=4.0 normalization, k IS the blend-band thickness in FIELD units. Our flood was composed uSmoothK~0.21 -> effective k~0.84 in a 1.0-wide UV (~6x the working band) -> the merge field goes negative across the whole canvas = the color slab. The mood model is COUPLED to this: paramsFor lerps smoothK 0.16..0.32 as an ABSOLUTE distance, but the renderer re-normalizes it as a multiplier (`params.smoothK / BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.smoothK`). SOTA fix (W08): store the mood smoothK as a UNITLESS 1.0-centred multiplier in MoodParams (excited gooier ~1.4x, sleepy crisper ~0.8x), not an absolute distance — kills the magic re-normalization divisor and lets W08's POS_SCALE'd absolute band stay the single source of length.

2D-SDF fake-normal lit droplet (IQ distance+gradient functions; imadrahmoune liquid-glass grammar) for the contained-droplet read: the SDF gradient (analytic or 4-tap) is a FREE fake surface normal; feed it Blinn-Phong specular + Schlick Fresnel rim + a thickness-from(-d) fake-SSS back-light to make a flat fill read as a lit gel dome. This is W9/W15's surface, and the mood model SCALES it: arousal/iridScale modulates spec/rim/SSS intensity so an excited droplet is glossier+more iridescent and a sleepy one is matte. Keep the sheen WARM-biased (toward --foreground), never clinical white, to stay in the cream-glass identity.

Trail-of-merged-spheres pseudopod (Codrops droplet) as the 'curious/reaching' expression: a short decaying-radius queue of pointer positions smin-merged into the body so the blob stretches an elastic pseudopod toward the cursor and snaps back — pure positional lag, NO spring constants needed (the queue's inherent latency + metaball blend IS the elasticity). This is the kinetic vocabulary of the 'curious' mood (pointer-active) and reuses the existing satellite plumbing. Couple its reach length to valence*arousal (a pleasant+aroused blob reaches FARTHER/more directly = LMA Space-Direct; an unpleasant one barely reaches = Indirect/recoil).

pitfalls: DO NOT add a discrete mood enum-switch or per-mood hand-tuned param tables as the primary model — that is the pre-circumplex anti-pattern the SOTA (and our own paramsFor) explicitly rejects. The 5 named moods MUST stay as SAMPLES of the continuous V/A surface, or they drift out of family and the 'one principled surface' invariant breaks. proof:blob-mood-resolved already guards against dead sub-orphans; keep the derivation single-source.

DO NOT let mood `smoothK` ship as an absolute distance — this is the EXACT coupling that contributed to the W08 flood. An absolute mood smoothK that lerps INDEPENDENTLY of the config/POS_SCALE length regime re-introduces the multi-source-of-length bug. It MUST be a unitless multiplier so there is ONE length authority (the POS_SCALE'd config band). The magic re-normalization divisors (`/0.015`, `/0.025`, `/BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.smoothK`) in the renderer are the smell — they prove the regime is split.

DO NOT overcouple arousal so the excited blob becomes a vestibular trigger or reads cheap. The README's own guidance: premium ambient is slow-and-breathing; fast motion reads cheap AND is a prefers-reduced-motion hazard. The excited END of the arousal range must stay tasteful — cap orbitSpeed/pulseAmp so even max-excited is lively-not-frantic. Do NOT add a parallel matchMedia in useBlobMood — proof:blob-tempo-suppression guards that the tempo×dt freeze (not ×uTime) is substrate-owned. The mood system must read the substrate's frozen dt (dt->0 freezes mood drift automatically); never a second PRM path. The composed rest pose under PRM should be a DESIGNED poster (peak roundness, idle mood), not a random freeze.

PERF: the mood model adds zero new passes (it's per-frame TS lerps + uniform uploads), so it is NOT the perf cost — but the iridescence/SSS it scales via iridScale IS per-pixel ALU and the 4-tap surfaceNormal is 4x field cost. W16 gates the 4-tap behind the lit path; make sure a sleepy/low-iridScale blob does not still pay full 4-tap cost if the sheen is scaled to ~0 (consider a min-iridScale threshold below which the lit branch is skipped, mirroring the lit gate).

DO NOT let the excited 'hold' latch or the homeostatic decay defeat W16's quiescence gate by making the blob NEVER settle. If mood perpetually micro-drifts it will burn full fps forever (the exact RED witness 2 the wave fixes). The decay must REACH a steady set-point within eps and STAY there so shouldContinue can park — a settled-detection (|d(params)/dt| < eps for the mood AND pointer AND no satellite mid-merge). An always-jittering mood is a demand-gate violation.

DO NOT widen the model to a full PAD 3-axis config surface or add per-mood Dominance/Flow knobs as new BlobConfig fields — that is overfit substrate with no consumer (the library's no-overfitting + substrate-with-consumer precepts). Dominance stays DERIVED from V/A (the pointer lean); Flow stays DERIVED from valence (the jitter/easing). The public surface is setMood(named) + the V/A points are internal — keep it.

The OKLCh in-family perturbation + warm-biased iridescence (iridHue~85) is the guard; verify the excited extreme stays warm, not neon, and the sheen stays toward --foreground.

sotaTechniques: IQ-2024 NORMALIZED smooth-minimum (smin): the modern smin pre-scales k by the kernel's g(0) so k is a TRUE blend-band in distance units (quadratic: `k *= 4.0`; circular: `k *= 1.0/(1.0-sqrt(0.5))`). Our sdf-body.glsl.ts ALREADY ships both normalized variants — so the W08 flood is NOT a smin-math bug, it is a UNIT-REGIME bug: the band k is a length and must ride the same POS_SCALE compression every other length-uniform carries, and the composed value must land ~0.03-0.08 effective. This is exactly what W08 specs. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/smin.

IQ smin MATERIAL/COLOR-BLEND trick: the SAME h interpolation factor that blends the two SDF distances also blends the two shapes' colors/materials (`vec2 smin(a,b,k){ h=1-min(|a-b|/(4k),1); w=h*h; s=w*k; return (a<b)?vec2(a-s,w*0.5):vec2(b-s,1-w*0.5);}` returns .x=distance, .y=mix factor). Our smin throws away h and the body/satellite color is decided by a global FBM `colorNoise` field, so a merging satellite does NOT carry its own palette stop INTO the neck — the gel seam reads uniform. Reusing h lets each metaball own a palette stop and the meniscus inherit a true gradient. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/smin.

Circumplex model of affect (Russell): emotions are a POINT in a 2-axis {valence, arousal} plane — excited = high-valence/high-arousal, sleepy = low-arousal, curious = mid-valence/mid-arousal. Our useBlobMood.ts ALREADY implements this canonically (MOOD_AVA table → paramsFor() derives all 12 MoodParams off one principled surface). This is the SOTA-correct framing; the gap is that the derived arousal/valence outputs are under-used downstream (orbitSpeedScale + wobbleScale are derived but the satellite tick ignores them — confirmed in the README W11 note). Source: arxiv 2307.10031 (EM-otion En-gine NPC believability), psychologyfanatic circumplex.

Anticipation + overshoot + follow-through (Disney 12 principles, the game-feel 'juice' canon): a believable state change is NOT a symmetric crossfade — it leads with a tiny ANTICIPATORY counter-move, OVERSHOOTS the target, then settles, and SECONDARY masses (satellites = the blob's 'floppy ears/tail') LAG the body and overshoot when it stops. Our click→excited path already has the right physics primitive (underdamped PULSE_OMEGA=18/PULSE_ZETA=0.35 oscillator), but the MOOD crossfade itself is a plain symmetric easeInOut with no anticipation and no secondary lag. Source: gameanim.com 12-principles, gamedevacademy game-feel.

Asymmetric attack/decay envelopes for state transitions: arousal should rise FAST and decay SLOW (excited snaps on in ~150-300ms, relaxes over seconds), the way an ADSR envelope or a real creature startles-then-calms. Our TRANSITION_MS table encodes some of this (excited 600ms in, sleepy 2500ms in) but the same duration is used for BOTH entering and leaving every mood — the snap-in/melt-out asymmetry is the missing realism axis. Idle-life via layered low-frequency noise ('breathing'): a creature is NEVER perfectly still at rest — a slow Perlin/sine breath on body radius + a slower wander on satellites keeps it alive without reading as twitchy. Our blob has pulseFreq/pulseAmp (the breath) and FBM membrane scroll (the living edge) — SOTA-correct. For the MOOD arc specifically the highest-leverage upgrades are: (1) adopt the IQ material-blend smin so each satellite/palette stop carries its color INTO the neck (the living-gel seam) instead of the flat global colorNoise field; (2) split TRANSITION_MS into asymmetric attack/decay so excited snaps in fast and melts out slow (arousal rises fast, decays slow); (3) add a tiny ANTICIPATION counter-move + body OVERSHOOT on a mood step (reuse the existing underdamped pulse channel — fire a small impulse on every setMood, not just click) so the creature 'reacts' rather than crossfades; (4) wire the derived orbitSpeedScale/wobbleScale/mergeRate into the satellite tick (currently derived-but-ignored — README W11 confirms) so excited visibly speeds the orbit + merge cycle and sleepy droops it; (5) keep sleepy ALIVE — slow the breath/orbit, do not freeze. notes.facet: Master tempo scalar — tempo*dt (never *uTime) so PRM/pause freezes EVERY axis deterministically, no FBM jump
sotaTechniques: INTEGRATE-THE-STEP, NEVER SCALE-THE-CLOCK (the canonical tempo seam). Maintain ONE accumulated motion clock `simTime += tempo*dt` and feed THAT to every time-driven term; never compute a frame value from `tempo*wallClock`. Mechanism: a noise field sampled as `fbm(p + uTime*speed)` is a continuous TRANSLATION of the sample domain, so the field's appearance is a pure function of uTime's VALUE — multiply uTime by a tempo that just changed and the whole field teleports by `(tempo_new - tempo_old)*wallClock`, a one-frame jump that grows without bound over a session. Integrating a tempo-scaled step keeps uTime monotonic and Lipschitz-continuous (it resumes from the accumulated value), so tempo→0 freezes the field in place and tempo→1 resumes seamlessly. This is exactly what the blob already does for FBM at useMetaballRenderer.ts:303-304/341 (`stepMs = tempo*dtMs; simTimeMs += stepMs; uTime = simTimeMs/1000`).

DELTA-TIME DRIVEN ANIMATION with a SCRIPT-OWNED custom time (Unity Shader Graph `_CustomTime`/`Time.deltatime` canon). SOTA engines deprecate the engine-global clock for any pausable/deterministic effect and inject a host-accumulated time uniform instead — the engine's built-in Time node 'freezes' in non-play contexts and cannot be paused deterministically, so production shaders expose a custom time property set from script. Mechanism: the shader becomes a pure function of an externally-owned scalar; pause/seek/slow-mo are host-side arithmetic on the accumulator, the shader is unchanged. Maps 1:1 onto the blob's injected `simTimeMs` (the renderer owns the clock, the shader reads `uTime` as data).

PHASE ACCUMULATOR for periodic motion (Direct Digital Synthesis canon — `phase += 2π*freq*dt; out = sin(phase)`, NOT `sin(time*freq)`). The textbook result: `sin(t*f)` emits an audible/visible 'click/pop' EVERY time the frequency f changes, because the argument jumps by `t*(f_new - f_old)`; accumulating instantaneous phase makes a frequency change phase-CONTINUOUS (the wave continues from where it left off). This is the SAME discontinuity class as the clock-scaling bug, applied to oscillators. DIRECTLY EXPOSES A LIVE BUG in the blob: the breath pulse `uPulsePhase = timeSec * config.pulseFreq * params.pulseFreq * 2π` (renderer:407) uses the RAW substrate `timeSec` (not `simTimeMs`) AND a mood-varying `params.pulseFreq` — so the breath pulse both (a) JUMPS on a tempo change (it is the one motion axis NOT on the integrated clock) and (b) POPS on a mood transition (frequency-keying without phase continuity). It must become an accumulated phase: `pulsePhase += 2π * pulseFreq_effective * (stepMs/1000)`.

FIXED-TIMESTEP ACCUMULATOR + dt CLAMP (Gaffer-on-Games 'Fix Your Timestep!' + the rAF tab-resume clamp). Accumulate frame time and advance the simulation in bounded steps; clamp the first post-resume dt (`Math.min(dt, MAX)`) so a backgrounded-tab rAF that delivers a multi-second dt cannot teleport the simulation ('spiral of death' / tunneling avoidance). Mechanism: bounding dt bounds the per-frame integration step, so no single frame can jump the accumulator arbitrarily far. The blob already implements the clamp (`Math.min(rawDtMs, 50)`, renderer:289-291) on EVERY integrated axis — the W11 extension of the W10 spring-only clamp — which is precisely correct; the SOTA refinement is to ensure the clamp sits BEFORE the tempo multiply (it does) and that the FIRST frame seeds dt to a nominal 16ms (it does: `lastTimeSec ? ... : 16`).

SINGLE-OWNER FREEZE SOURCE (one writer drives tempo→0; the substrate owns PRM, the seam reads it). SOTA pause/reduced-motion design collapses ALL motion-suppression onto ONE scalar gate rather than scattering `if(paused)` and `matchMedia` checks across systems. Mechanism: `tempo = (reducedMotion || paused) ? 0 : config.tempo` (renderer:301-302) makes a single multiply the ONLY place motion can be suppressed, so PRM, the WCAG-2.2.2 pause button, and a future slow-mo all route through one arithmetic node and provably freeze EVERY integrated axis at once. The blob reads the substrate's live `reducedMotion` (a `matchMedia change` listener owned by `useWebGLCanvas`) rather than adding a second PRM path — the AV.W7-removed anti-pattern that `proof:blob-tempo-suppression` machine-locks (no `matchMedia` anywhere in the blob tree).

DETERMINISTIC, SEEDED, CLOCK-DECOUPLED STATE MACHINE (the satellite phase system reads the integrated clock). SOTA procedural-creature systems drive event timers off the SAME accumulated sim-clock the visuals use, so the entire creature shares one tempo. The blob's satellite orbit/merge/absorb/emerge machine takes `now = simTimeMs` (useBlobSatellites.ts:30-32, renderer:329), so pausing the tempo freezes satellite phase WITH the FBM and the mood — the whole creature breathes as one organism, and a resume continues the phase rather than snapping to a wall-clock-derived position.
notes.applicability: The blob's master tempo seam (W11.c) is ALREADY ~90% SOTA-correct and the existing `proof:blob-tempo-suppression` gate is well-designed: it asserts `stepMs = tempo*dtMs`, `simTimeMs += stepMs`, `uTime = simTimeMs/1000`, the no-clock-scaling bite, `tempo=0` on freeze, the no-parallel-matchMedia rule, and the first-dt clamp — plus a runtime continuity witness (integrated jump <0.02 vs clock jump >0.1). The research VALIDATES every one of these against the canon (IQ domain-warp = continuous-translation, DDS phase accumulator, Gaffer fixed-timestep, Unity custom-time). THE PATH FORWARD has one concrete, load-bearing fix the gate does NOT currently catch: the breath-pulse axis is the LAST un-integrated axis. At renderer:407 `uPulsePhase` is computed from the raw substrate `timeSec` (NOT `simTimeMs`) and multiplies the mood-varying `params.pulseFreq`, so under the DDS phase-accumulator analysis it (a) JUMPS on a tempo change like the forbidden clock-scaling form, and (b) POPS on every mood transition (frequency-keying without phase continuity — the audible-click class). Because the shader reads it as `bodyR = uBodyRadius + sin(uPulsePhase)*uPulseAmp` (frag:166,270), the body's radius will visibly hitch on pause/PRM and on mood drift. THE FIX (routes naturally into W16's quiescence/integration work, or as a W11.c follow-on since it is a pure time-seam correction, NOT a length/geometry edit owned by W08/W15): replace the absolute-time pulse with an ACCUMULATED PHASE — carry a `pulsePhase` accumulator advanced by `pulsePhase += 2π * (config.pulseFreq * params.pulseFreq) * (stepMs/1000)` and upload `sin(pulsePhase)`-ready phase. This (1) puts the pulse on the tempo-integrated clock so tempo=0 freezes it with the rest, and (2) makes mood-driven frequency changes phase-continuous (no pop). The gate should be EXTENDED with a clause asserting `uPulsePhase` is NOT computed from `timeSec` (mirror the existing `clockScaled` bite for the pulse axis) and that a `pulsePhase +=` accumulator exists. For the W16 README rewrite, document the tempo seam as the canonical 'one accumulated clock, every axis reads it' contract with the IQ-translation + DDS-phase-accumulator rationale, and note that PRM/pause is a single `tempo→0` multiply (the WCAG-2.2.2 freeze is a freeze of the SAME scalar the DockBackgroundToggle pause sets). For the mood model: the `MOOD_AVA` valence/arousal core is already textbook Russell circumplex affect (excited=high-arousal/high-valence, sleepy=low-arousal) — SOTA-aligned; the only tempo-relevant note is that arousal currently drives `pulseFreq`/`orbitSpeedScale` as a FREQUENCY multiplier, which is exactly why the phase-accumulator fix matters (mood = a live frequency change, the DDS pop trigger).
pitfalls: THE PULSE-PHASE LEAK (live, confirmed). renderer:407 `uPulsePhase = timeSec * config.pulseFreq * params.pulseFreq * Math.PI*2` reads the RAW `timeSec`, bypassing the integrated `simTimeMs`. This is the exact clock-scaling discontinuity the gate forbids for uTime — but applied to the pulse axis, which the gate does NOT check. Result: the breath pulse JUMPS on tempo change and POPS on mood transition (frequency-keying). It is the single un-converted motion axis; the W11.c 'every axis reads simTimeMs' claim is not yet fully true.

MOOD-AS-FREQUENCY-CHANGE is a phase-pop trigger even on the FBM axis if naively done. `params.pulseFreq`/`noiseSpeed`/`orbitSpeedScale` are frequency multipliers that change continuously as mood eases (useBlobMood lerp). For terms folded into the accumulator (`simTimeMs += tempo*dt`, then `uTime*speed`), a changing `speed` re-scales an EXISTING large `uTime` — so even the FBM scroll can micro-jump if `speed` is applied as `uTime*speed` rather than integrated into the accumulator as `phase += speed*dt`. The blob currently multiplies `uTime*uNoiseSpeed` in-shader (frag:182) with a CONSTANT config noiseSpeed (not mood-varying), so it is safe TODAY — but if a future wave makes `noiseSpeed` mood-driven, it inherits the same pop class. Rule: any per-frame-varying frequency must be integrated as `phase += freq*dt`, never multiplied against an accumulated time.

CLAMP ORDERING. The dt clamp MUST sit before the tempo multiply (it does: clamp at :291, tempo at :303). If a refactor moved the clamp after `tempo*dt` it would clamp the SCALED step, letting a slow tempo silently widen the effective dt window — a subtle frame-rate-dependence regression.

FLOAT32 PRECISION DRIFT on a long-lived accumulator. `simTimeMs` and any `pulsePhase` accumulator grow unbounded; uploaded to a `float` uniform (32-bit), `sin(pulsePhase)` loses angular precision after ~hours of runtime (mantissa exhaustion) and the FBM scroll quantizes. SOTA mitigation: wrap the phase accumulator modulo 2π (`pulsePhase = mod(pulsePhase, 2π)` — sin is periodic so this is exact) and, for FBM, periodically wrap `simTimeMs` by a large period or keep the uTime upload as a wrapped/offset value. Low-priority for a UI accent (sessions are short) but a documented hazard for the README.

GATE IS STATIC-SOURCE, NOT RENDERED-PIXEL. `proof:blob-tempo-suppression` greps source patterns (`stepMs = tempo*dtMs`, `simTimeMs += stepMs`). It cannot catch the pulse-phase leak because it only checks the uTime upload, not uPulsePhase — and it asserts nothing about the rendered field's continuity across an ACTUAL pause. The AX cardinal lesson (static-green-while-visually-broken) applies: the live VISUAL-TRUTH audit must include a pause-mid-pulse / mood-transition-under-pause screenshot pair to catch a phase hitch the grep gate is blind to.

DON'T ADD A SECOND PAUSE/PRM PATH. The temptation when wiring W16's `v-model:paused` is to gate motion in the SFC as well as the renderer. Motion suppression must remain the ONE `tempo = (reduced||paused)?0` multiply; a parallel `if(paused) return` in the frame callback would freeze the loop but leave `lastTimeSec` stale, so the FIRST resume frame delivers a huge dt — re-introducing the jump the clamp exists to prevent. The clamp + single-tempo-gate is the correct, sufficient design; preserve it.

notes.facet: Goo / liquid aesthetics references — the SVG feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix goo, the modern WebGL/SDF metaball successor, and the IQ smin/normalization frontier — as it applies to glass-ui's WebGL2 goo-blob (AX.W08 un-flood · W15 contained lit droplet · W16 integration+mood)
sotaTechniques: IQ-2024 NORMALIZED smin (the un-flood key) — multiply k by a per-variant normalization factor so k is a literal blend-thickness in DISTANCE units, not a magic-scaled blob. Quadratic: `k *= 4.0; h = max(k-|a-b|,0)/k; min(a,b) - h*h*k*0.25` (factor g(0)=1/4). Circular: `k *= 1/(1-sqrt(0.5))` (factor ~0.293). The blob's sdf-body.glsl.ts ALREADY ships both verbatim-correct — so the W08 flood is NOT a formula bug.

The smin FLOOD mechanism (the W08 root cause, now precisely diagnosable) — IQ: smin influence extends wherever `|a-b| < k`, and an over-large k makes the blend band span GLOBALLY rather than confining to the seam (CD-family smins under-estimate distance over infinitely-large regions). At composed uSmoothK~0.21 the effective k~0.84 in a 1.0-wide UV is ~6x the working band, so |a-b|<k holds across the whole canvas → field pushed negative everywhere → opaque slab. Fix is a SCALE re-derivation (re-tune composed k to ~0.03-0.08 effective + restore POS_SCALE so the smin length rides the same 0.625 compression as bodyRadius/satRadius/noiseAmp/pointer), NOT a shader rewrite.

Codrops droplet pattern (Yuki Kojima 2025) — the canonical premium-metaball reference: smin-blended SDF spheres + surface noise for an organic skin + a mouse-trail of spheres arranged along the cursor path so the body stretches a stretchy pseudopod and snaps back. The blob ALREADY implements this (uTrail compile-time array, smin-merged, tapering radius). SOTA-confirmed it is the right interaction architecture.

2D-SDF fake-normal lighting (the lit-droplet substrate) — derive a pseudo-3D normal from the SDF gradient (IQ distgradfunctions2d / the 4-tap tetrahedron) + a dome Z-lift (z=sqrt(1-(1-interior)^2)), then Blinn-Phong glint + Schlick/Fresnel rim. The blob ALREADY ships this (surfaceNormal() + the uLit block). SOTA-current and correct.

2D-SDF REFRACTION/LENSING via screen-space derivatives (the ONE frontier technique the blob does NOT yet have) — the 2025 liquid-glass shaders compute a refractive UV offset from the SDF gradient using dFdx/dFdy of the distance value (`computeRefractOffset`), bending whatever is behind the droplet like a real lens, plus Schlick Fresnel + wavelength-dependent IOR chromatic aberration at the rim. This is the genuine 'liquid glass' read beyond a flat lit fill. A backdrop-sampling lens is heavier (needs a backdrop texture) — a CHEAP fold is a subtle rim chromatic-fringe + an edge UV nudge without a full backdrop pass.

Fast subsurface scattering (Alan Zucconi) — a thickness-driven back-light term: light wrapping through the thin rim plus an inner-luminosity ramp from `-d`, giving a translucent-gel core glow. The blob ALREADY ships this (uSssScale/uCoreGlow block). The W15 move is to turn it ON at a low default, not invent it.

IQ cosine procedural palette for iridescence — `a + b*cos(2pi(c*t+d))` mapping the Fresnel/edge angle + a time-scrolled thickness onto a HUE offset, biased to a WARM arc (clamped chroma → cream/gold pearl, never cold rainbow). The blob ALREADY ships this warm-biased variant (uIridescence block). SOTA-current; W15 just enables a subtle default.

OKLCh perturbation + hue-preserving gamut clamp + mandatory sRGB OETF — work the color in OKLab/OKLCh (Ottosson exact matrices), perturb L/C/h perceptually, chroma-bisect to gamut without shifting hue, then linearToSrgb on output. This is why the blob stays in-family vs reference blobs that band in raw sRGB/HSV. ALREADY shipped + machine-locked (proof:blob-color-equivalence, proof:blob-space-gamma).

Interleaved Gradient Noise dither (Jimenez, CoD:AW) — a single-pass per-fragment dither (`fract(52.9829*fract(dot(pos,vec2(0.06711,0.00583))))`) that breaks 8-bit banding on smooth low-contrast gradients with zero texture taps. The warm-cream droplet's soft fill IS the banding-prone case; aurora already ships an IGN dither — the W15/W11 finish should splice the SAME dither so the cream fill doesn't band.

Volume-preserving velocity squash-and-stretch — stretch along the motion axis by `sa = 1 + |v|*k`, squash the perpendicular axis by EXACTLY `1/sa` (reciprocal, NOT 1-amt which shrinks area), applied as an anisotropic UV basis. Literature confirms UI deformations should be ~2-5% and cap LOW. The blob ALREADY ships the exact reciprocal form in sceneDist(). SOTA-confirmed; the W15 job is to re-balance the magnitude against the smaller contained body.

Circumplex affect (valence/arousal) mood model — the two-axis psychological model where each named mood is a POINT in {valence,arousal} space and the per-mood params are DERIVED from one principled surface (arousal→motion energy, valence→warmth/lean). The blob ALREADY ships this (useBlobMood paramsFor). SOTA-grounded; W16's job is the wire-or-cut hygiene (setMood has no caller; orbitSpeedScale/wobbleScale are lerped-but-unread sub-orphans — wire them into the satellite tick or record a MIGRATION collapse to one `energy` scalar), NOT a redesign.

SVG feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix goo (the LEGACY reference, deliberately NOT the path) — the classic gooey look: blur a group then crank alpha contrast with a color matrix so elements melt together. It is resource-heavy on large areas, Safari-flaky on DOM elements, and cannot light/refract/color-manage per-pixel. The blob's single-pass WebGL2 SDF is the correct modern successor — the README should keep this contrast as the 'why WebGL not SVG-goo' rationale.
notes.applicability:
THE HEADLINE: glass-ui's blob is already at or beyond the public web frontier (IQ-2024 normalized smin both variants, SDF tetrahedron normal, Blinn-Phong+Fresnel, warm iridescence, fake-SSS, multi-stop OKLCh, circumplex mood, reciprocal squash, Codrops pointer-trail). W08 (un-flood) — research VINDICATES the spec's diagnosis exactly. The smin formula is correct; the flood is purely (a) composed uSmoothK magnitude too large (effective k~0.84 floods because IQ's |a-b|<k band spans the whole 1.0-wide UV) and (b) the missing POS_SCALE on the smin upload (it IS a length and must ride the 0.625 compression every other length-uniform carries). Re-balance pointer-lean/pseudopod/squash magnitudes against the new smaller body so the already-wired interaction becomes legible.

pitfalls: The flood recurs if the un-flood is PARTIAL — IQ's |a-b|<k band is global when k is large, so any wave that compresses the smin band while leaving body/sat/orbit at a different scale re-floods. W08 and W15 MUST keep the POS_SCALE disposition coherent: W08 restores POS_SCALE minimally; W15 re-derives the ENTIRE length cohort ATOMICALLY (never a half-migration). proof:blob-render is the regression-lock on both.

Smin k is a LENGTH — uploading uSmoothK without POS_SCALE while every other length-uniform carries the 0.625 compression is the exact bug that floods. The smin band must ride the same compression as bodyRadius/satRadius/noiseAmp/uPointer or the merge thickness desyncs from the geometry it merges.
