sotaTechniques: PREMULTIPLIED SOURCE-OVER (the canonical pair). Output vec4(rgb*alpha, alpha) from the fragment shader, request the context premultipliedAlpha:true, and set blendFunc(ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA). This is the ONE correct combination for a transparent-background canvas the browser composites over the page. The blob ALREADY does exactly this (useMetaballRenderer.ts:198/266, metaball.frag.ts:379) — SOTA-correct, no change needed; the README should document it as the canonical recipe.

PREMULTIPLY AFTER THE OETF, NOT IN LINEAR. The order must be: compute color in linear -> add lit/SSS/spec highlights in linear -> linearToSrgb() OETF -> THEN rgb*alpha. The blob does this correctly (metaball.frag.ts:376 OETF then :379 premultiply). Premultiplying in linear then OETF-ing the premultiplied value double-darkens the edge band (the named A5/A2 trap the proof:blob-space-gamma gate guards). Because the browser composites the 8-bit canvas as already-encoded sRGB premultiplied values, gamma-space premultiply IS the matching convention here — do NOT 'fix' it to linear-space premultiply.

ADDITIVE GLOW VIA rgb>alpha (the premultiplied glow trick — the headline for W15's lit droplet). In premultiplied output a pixel may carry rgb GREATER than its alpha; such a pixel reads as EMISSIVE/additive when composited (ONE*src adds full color, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA*dst barely darkens because alpha is low). This is precisely how a glow rim/core-glow should be authored: the lit Fresnel rim + coreGlow + fast-SSS lift the LINEAR rgb above what alpha alone would carry, so after premultiply the rim glows over the page instead of just being a more-opaque edge. W15 should AUTHOR the lit highlights to deliberately exceed alpha at the rim (the highlight += in metaball.frag.ts:373 already adds in linear pre-premultiply — keep it un-clamped-against-alpha so the glow is additive, only clamp[0,1] against the channel ceiling).

fwidth-BASED ANALYTICAL EDGE with antialias:false (the reason MSAA is off). The droplet edge is anti-aliased ANALYTICALLY in-shader: aa = fwidth(d); alpha = 1 - smoothstep(-aa, aa, d). This gives a per-pixel ~1px gradient at any zoom/DPR and is strictly better than MSAA for an SDF (MSAA only AAs polygon edges, not the in-fragment alpha cut). So antialias:false is CORRECT and intentional — the analytical edge + premultiplied output is the SOTA pairing. The blob has this (metaball.frag.ts:277-278).

IQ QUADRATIC smin WITH k-NORMALIZATION (the W08 un-flood mechanism, confirmed against the source). smin: k*=4.0; h=max(k-abs(a-b),0)/k; return min(a,b)-h*h*k*0.25. The k*=4.0 makes k EXACTLY the maximum surface inflation in true distance units (kernel g(0)=1/4). IQ's explicit warning IS the W08 flood: 'when k is too large relative to shapes, over-merging occurs — the blended region floods and destroys geometric definition.' The fix is to treat k as a LENGTH on the same coordinate system as every other length (the POS_SCALE compression) and size it to the shapes — exactly W08's restore-POS_SCALE-on-uSmoothK + re-derive-the-composed-band-to-~0.03-0.08-effective.

CIRCULAR smin FOR ROUNDER MENISCI. smin_circular: k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5)); h=max(k-abs(a-b),0)/k; return min(a,b)-k*0.5*(1+h-sqrt(1-h*(h-2))). Produces mathematically-perfect circular blend profiles (wetter, rounder seam) vs quadratic's polynomial approximation. The blob already exposes merge:'quadratic'|'circular' (types.ts BlobMerge) — this is the SOTA variant pair; circular reads as a wetter liquid meniscus for the contained-droplet identity.

FAST SUBSURFACE SCATTERING (Alan Zucconi / translucent-gel read for W15's living warm-glass). I_back = saturate(V . -normalize(L + N*delta))^p * scale, thickness-modulated. The blob's metaball.frag.ts:332-335 IS this formula (back = pow(clamp(dot(V, -(L + N*thickness)),0,1), uSssPower); sss = back*uSssScale*(1-thickness)) — SOTA-correct, just defaulted OFF (sssScale:0). W15 turns it ON at a LOW floor; combined with the premultiplied additive-glow trick it gives the translucent-gel core-glow that reads as warm glass, not a flat sticker.

FRESNEL/SCHLICK RIM as the curvature read (lit dome for W15). rimFres = pow(1 - max(dot(N,V),0), rimPower), attenuated by (1 - k*thickness) so the sheen rides the rim not the core. The blob has this (metaball.frag.ts:366-367) fed by an IQ-tetrahedron normal off the COMPOSITE SDF (surfaceNormal samples sceneDist at a screen-space epsilon). This is the SOTA way to make a flat SDF read as a rounded bead; W15 flips lit:true so it paints.

PREMULTIPLIED canvas FEEDS CSS filter:drop-shadow (the glass-ui-specific compositing chain). Because the canvas is premultiplied-alpha with a transparent clear (clearColor(0,0,0,0)), CSS filter:drop-shadow() traces the canvas ALPHA channel (not the bounding box) to cast the blob's soft shadow — GooBlob.vue wraps the canvas in exactly this. The premultiplied output is what makes the drop-shadow trace clean; a straight-alpha or opaque-cleared canvas would shadow a rectangle. This is the load-bearing reason the premultiplied pipeline is correct for THIS component.

WebGPU FORWARD PARITY (alphaMode:'premultiplied'). The WebGPU canvas equivalent is configure({alphaMode:'premultiplied'}) + blend {srcFactor:'one', dstFactor:'one-minus-src-alpha'} (the 'premultiplied source-over' preset) — identical math. If the blob ever ports to WebGPU (aurora's WGSL path), the premultiplied convention carries over 1:1; the additive-glow trick and the OETF-then-premultiply order are unchanged.
notes.applicability: The glass-ui blob's compositing pipeline is ALREADY SOTA-correct in its bones — this facet is mostly a CONFIRMATION + a README-grounding, not a rewrite. Concrete path forward by wave: (W08 un-flood) The premultiplied edge is fine; the flood is purely geometric (smin k too large), exactly as IQ's smin article predicts. W08's restore-POS_SCALE-on-uSmoothK + re-derive-the-composed-band-to-~0.03-0.08-effective is the textbook fix — k must be a LENGTH on the same coordinate system as every other length. The analytical fwidth edge will then resolve a clean ~1px premultiplied band on the now-bounded field; no compositing change. (W15 contained-lit-droplet) THIS is where premultiplied alpha becomes the load-bearing glow mechanism. Turn lit:true + low iridescence/SSS/coreGlow floors and AUTHOR the highlights to push LINEAR rgb above alpha at the rim/core so that after the OETF-then-premultiply, the rim/core reads ADDITIVE (glows over the page) — that is the premultiplied-glow trick and the difference between 'a more-opaque edge' and 'a glowing wet bead.' Keep the highlight add in linear BEFORE the OETF (metaball.frag.ts:373) and only clamp[0,1] per channel, never clamp rgb<=alpha. Verify with proof:blob-render that the contained droplet shows a center-vs-corner gradient AND a bright rim band (a glow signature), and that the CSS drop-shadow still traces a clean alpha silhouette. (W16 integration/README) The research-backed README must document the canonical recipe as ONE coherent contract: premultipliedAlpha:true + antialias:false (analytical fwidth edge, not MSAA) + blendFunc(ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) + clearColor(0,0,0,0) + shader outputs vec4(rgb*alpha, alpha) AFTER the OETF + premultiplied-rgb>alpha = additive glow + CSS drop-shadow traces the alpha. Cross-link IQ smin for the merge band and Zucconi fast-SSS for the gel read. The mood model: mood drives the GLOW intensity (iridScale/sssScale multipliers) and the smin band (mood smoothK as a 1.0-centred multiplier per W08), so 'excited' = brighter additive rim glow + wetter merge, 'sleepy' = dimmer + tighter — all riding the SAME premultiplied output, never a second blend path.
pitfalls: DO NOT premultiply in linear space then OETF. rgb*alpha must come AFTER linearToSrgb(). A linear-premultiply-then-OETF darkens the edge band (double-gamma the partial-coverage pixels) — the proof:blob-space-gamma A5/A2 trap. The blob is correct today; W15/W16 must not reorder it when adding the lit highlights.

DO NOT clamp the lit highlight to rgb<=alpha. That kills the additive-glow trick — a rim with rgb>alpha is the WHOLE POINT (it reads emissive). Clamp each channel to [0,1] (the display ceiling), never against alpha. If a future 'fix' clamps premultiplied rgb to alpha to 'avoid >1 premultiplied values,' the glow flattens to a plain opaque edge.

antialias:true (MSAA) is the WRONG instinct for an SDF. MSAA only AAs geometric/polygon edges and does nothing for the in-fragment smoothstep alpha cut — it would cost fill for zero benefit AND can introduce its own premultiplied-resolve darkening at the quad's own edges. Keep antialias:false; the fwidth analytical edge is the AA. Resist any audit that flags antialias:false as a defect.

STRAIGHT-ALPHA blendFunc(SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) with a premultiplied context = double-darkened, fringed edges. The two MUST agree: premultipliedAlpha:true pairs ONLY with blendFunc(ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA). A mismatch is the classic dark-halo fringe. (The blob agrees today — a regression here is silent: it still renders, just with a darker rim.)

clearColor must be (0,0,0,0) with the premultiplied convention. A non-zero-alpha clear or an opaque clear breaks the transparent compositing (the CSS background/drop-shadow no longer show through) — the canvas would composite a rectangle. The blob clears (0,0,0,0) correctly; keep it.

PERF: the surfaceNormal IQ 4-tap calls sceneDist 4x per pixel (each with FBM x3 octaves x2) — quadrupling field cost. W16 already routes this to gate the 4-tap behind the lit/iridescence/SSS path ONLY. Turning lit:true ON by default (W15) makes this the DEFAULT cost — so the W16 pre-FBM bounding discard (length(uv)>maxReach -> return transparent BEFORE the FBM) and the quality:half axis are NOT optional once the lit glow ships by default; they are the cost-recovery for the glow.

8-bit precision loss in premultiplied storage is destructive — you cannot un-associate alpha later. Irrelevant for direct-to-canvas display (the blob's case), but matters if the blob is ever rendered to an intermediate texture/FBO and re-composited (e.g. a future half-res quality path that upsamples). A half-res premultiplied intermediate then bilinear-upsampled is CORRECT (premultiplied is exactly what makes filtering fringe-free) — but do the upsample on the premultiplied values, never un-premultiply mid-pipeline.

Mood/glow must ride ONE output path. The glow intensity is a per-fragment scalar (sssScale/iridScale/coreGlow multipliers), NOT a second additive blend pass or a second draw. Adding a separate additive-blend glow pass (blendFunc ONE,ONE) would be a parallel compositing path — forbidden by the one-path precept and would not trace the drop-shadow alpha correctly. Keep the glow IN the single premultiplied fragment.

notes.facet: WebGL2 metaball performance — ALU budget, full-screen pass cost, FP16, early-out outside the bounding field (glass-ui goo-blob W08 un-flood / W15 contained-droplet / W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: IQ smin CD-Family early-out (the headline lever for W16). Inigo Quilez's 2024 smin rewrite formalizes the Clamped-Differences (CD) family: g(-1)=g'(-1)=0, g(1)=g'(1)=1, so 'the smooth-minimum doesn't have any effect on the SDF shapes a nor b once they are sufficiently far apart, i.e. k units apart or further.' MECHANISM: when |a-b| > k the smin collapses to a plain min — the blend term is identically zero. APPLIES: our smin already has this (h = max(k-|a-b|,0)/k goes to 0), but we still evaluate every satellite/trail sdCircle. The real lever is a CHEAP PRE-FIELD BOUNDING TEST: max metaball reach = max(satPos+satRadius, trailPos+trailRadius, bodyR) + smin band + noiseAmp; a fragment with length(uv) beyond that reach is guaranteed transparent and can skip the entire field+FBM+OKLCh block. This is the W16 'pre-FBM bounding discard' done with the correct math (the smin band must be added to the reach so the meniscus is not clipped).

Pre-FBM early-out via transparent WRITE, not GLSL discard (correctness-critical for W16). The single largest waste today: ~60% of the 1.6x-oversize canvas (2.56x the fragments) is transparent border that runs BOTH 3-octave FBM calls + the OKLCh round-trip before alpha<0.001 returns. MECHANISM: a coarse bounding test (length(uv) > maxReach, or a cheap body-only sdCircle > band) BEFORE fbmWarped()/fbm() returns a transparent fragment, skipping ~all the per-pixel ALU on dead pixels. CRITICAL NUANCE the W16 spec gets subtly wrong: it says 'discard' — but our pass is a pure premultiplied blend (gl.BLEND ONE/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA), NO depth buffer, NO depth test. The shader ALREADY uses `fragColor = vec4(0.0); return;` not `discard` (metaball.frag.ts:280-283). KEEP that form: GLSL `discard` defeats early-Z / Hi-Z and on TILED MOBILE GPUs can disable the tiled-renderer fast path for every subsequent draw to the render target — a write of vec4(0) has none of that hazard and is the correct early-out on a blending-only transparent canvas.

Half-resolution internal render + free bilinear upsample (the ~4x fill-rate lever; the W16 quality:'full'|'half' axis). MECHANISM: render the metaball pass into a half-size FBO color texture, then blit/upsample to the visible canvas using the GPU's free GL_LINEAR bilinear filter — 1/4 the fragments run the expensive shader. APPLIES: blobs are the IDEAL half-res candidate because the soft FBM/AA edge HIDES the bilinear interpolation (a hard-edged UI element would not). It must be ONE extra blit, never a Kawase/multi-pass blur chain (the 'no multi-pass blur on mobile' rule). Wire it behind the never-shipped quality axis: a hero blob opts into 'full', weak-GPU/ambient blobs default 'half'. Note the substrate already clamps DPR<=2 (AV_DPR_MAX); half-res composes with that for a DPR-1+half-res weak-mobile tier.

FP16 / mediump split: keep the SDF/positions highp, drop color+lighting+normals to mediump. MECHANISM: on mobile GPUs that genuinely implement 16-bit (Mali/Adreno/Apple), mediump (FP16) ALU is 'usually faster than highp, often significantly faster' via 2x arithmetic throughput AND lower register pressure -> higher occupancy/latency-hiding. APPLIES: our frag is `precision highp float` globally. The SDF field math (sdCircle length(), smin, the screen-space gradient, FBM lattice coordinates) MUST stay highp — distance fields band and the gradient shimmers under FP16, and the W08/W15 sub-0.08 seam-pull lives in a precision-sensitive regime. But the OKLCh perturb, the Blinn-Phong/Fresnel/iridescence/SSS lighting (all dot products bounded [-1,1]) and the normal vectors are mediump-safe (colors are already 0-1, lighting is range-bounded). HAZARD: too many FP16<->FP32 casts cost cycles, and desktop GPUs run mediump as FP32 anyway (zero desktop win) — so this is a mobile-only, measure-first lever, lower priority than half-res and the bounding early-out.

Gate the surfaceNormal 4-tap behind the lit/iridescence/SSS path ONLY (the second-biggest ALU lever; W16 arm 5). MECHANISM: surfaceNormal() calls sceneDist() FOUR more times per pixel (the IQ tetrahedron gradient) — and sceneDist itself runs the satellite loop + trail loop + a full fbmWarped (which is itself 2x fbm = up to 6 noised() evals under domain-warp). So the normal QUADRUPLES the field cost per lit pixel. Today N is computed unconditionally in main() (metaball.frag.ts:298) even though it is only consumed when uLit/uIridescence/uCoreGlow/uSssScale are active. APPLIES: compute N (and thickness/fres) only inside an `if (uLit>0.5 || uIridescence>0.0 || ...)` guard; the flat-fill fast path skips 4 field evals. CONTEXT-SHIFT for W15: W15 ships lit:true as the DEFAULT identity, so the lit path becomes the common case — which makes it ESSENTIAL that the 4-tap rides a CHEAP field. Pairs with: under the lit default, evaluate the 4 normal taps against a CHEAPER body-only field (skip the satellite/trail loops in the gradient taps if the rim normal only needs the body curvature), or reuse the analytic FBM gradient (noised() already returns the gradient in .yz from ONE eval) instead of 4 finite-difference taps — the watercolor-edges noised() machinery exists precisely so the surface CAN consume the analytic derivative rather than re-sampling.

Single-pass per-pixel SDF is the architecturally-correct choice for <=4 nuclei (the explicit anti-pattern guard). MECHANISM/RATIONALE: compute-shader particle accumulation is SOTA for thousands-to-millions of bodies; the blob has MAX_SATS=4 (body + <=3 satellites + a <=15-sample trail), CPU-simulated and uploaded as ~12 uniforms — there is NO accumulation bottleneck. Per-pixel field is free relative to marching-squares (which is a smoothness DOWNGRADE on the GPU) and the SVG feGaussianBlur goo-filter is strictly inferior (Safari/Firefox feColorMatrix breakage, blur-radius cost, alpha-contrast crush). APPLIES: do NOT migrate to WebGPU compute or a particle swarm — keep single-pass WebGL2 SDF. WebGPU is Baseline-2026 'newly available' (~70-95% coverage) and a decorative background cannot carry a hard WebGPU dependency; if ever adopted it is a SUBSTRATE-WIDE decision, never blob-local WGSL. This is the perf-architecture invariant the README should state as load-bearing.

Quiescence / event-scheduled rAF (the biggest battery/fill lever after offscreen-park; W16 arm 2). MECHANISM: replace the perpetual shouldContinue(){return !paused} with a real at-rest predicate — park when mood settled AND pointer spring at rest (|v|<eps) AND trail collapsed AND click-pulse 0 AND no satellite mid-merge — and wake() from the satellite scheduler when the next orbit/merge phase is due. An idle ambient blob renders ZERO frames between phase transitions instead of burning 60fps of FBMx2 + OKLCh. APPLIES: this is the W16 headline perf arm; it composes with the substrate's existing offscreen/tab-hidden/PRM park (a parked rAF runs zero work). The perf story is layered: offscreen=0 frames, idle-onscreen=event-scheduled, visible-animating=half-res-able + bounded + FP16-able.

Once the composed uSmoothK lands the ~0.03-0.08 effective seam-pull (tight wet meniscus) with POS_SCALE restored, the smin band becomes a SMALL, KNOWN distance — which is exactly what makes the CD-family early-out tight: maxReach = bodyR + orbitRadius + satRadius + smin_band + noiseAmp, and a small smin_band keeps that bounding circle tight (a flooded 0.864 band would have made any bounding test useless). (b) lit:true makes the surfaceNormal 4-tap the COMMON path, not the exception — so the W16 'gate the 4-tap behind lit' arm must be paired with making the lit field CHEAP (body-only normal taps, or consume the analytic noised() gradient). README perf section should document: fill-rate is quadratic in DPR (DPR<=2 clamp is load-bearing), the bounding early-out + quality axis, and the single-pass-SDF-is-correct-for-<=4-nuclei invariant.", "MOOD MODEL note (perf framing): the 5-mood cross-fade is a CPU-side parameter lerp feeding ~6 uniforms (smoothK multiplier, iridScale, edge amp, tempo). It costs nothing per-pixel beyond the uniform values it sets, so the mood model is perf-neutral — the cost is entirely in the shared frag ALU those uniforms drive. The quiescence predicate (W16) reads 'mood settled / not transitioning' as one of its at-rest conditions; that read is the only perf-load-bearing mood seam. Keep mood a uniform swing, never a branch that changes the field topology per-mood (a per-mood #define would force shader recompile)."]
pitfalls: DISCARD vs transparent-write (the W16 spec wording trap). The W16 spec text says 'length(uv) > maxReach -> discard' (W16 arm 5, line 147; PATH-FORWARD §5 also says 'discard'). GLSL `discard` defeats early-Z/Hi-Z and on TILED MOBILE GPUs can disable the tiled-renderer fast path for every subsequent draw to that render target. The shader ALREADY correctly uses `fragColor = vec4(0.0); return;` (metaball.frag.ts:281). The implementer must use the transparent-write form for the new bounding early-out too — NOT GLSL discard. On this blend-only/no-depth canvas the early-Z argument is moot, but the mobile-tiler hazard makes discard strictly worse than a transparent write. Flag this so the literal 'discard' in the spec is not copied into the shader.

Bounding-reach math must include the smin band + noise amp or it clips the meniscus. A naive `length(uv) > maxBodyReach` test that uses only body+orbit+satRadius will cut the smooth-min meniscus and the FBM edge wobble, producing a hard clip exactly at the boundary the un-flood (W08) was meant to fix. maxReach MUST = furthest(metaball center + its radius) + smin_band + noiseAmp + a small AA epsilon. Conservative is safe (a slightly loose bound just runs a few extra transparent pixels); too-tight re-introduces a clip artifact.

FP16/mediump on the SDF banding the field + shimmering the gradient. Dropping the distance field, the screen-space gradient (surfaceNormal eps ~1.5px), or FBM lattice coordinates to mediump will band the silhouette and shimmer the normal — the seam-pull lives at ~0.03-0.08 distance units, a precision-sensitive regime, and mediump's ~128 distinct values across 0-1 is far too coarse. Only color (already 0-1) and bounded lighting dot-products are mediump-safe. Also: desktop GPUs run mediump AS FP32 (zero desktop win) and excessive FP16<->FP32 casts cost cycles — so FP16 is a measure-first, mobile-only lever, lowest priority of the set.

Half-res hides soft edges but would soften the lit specular glint. The half-res FBO + bilinear upsample is near-lossless on the soft FBM watercolor edge, BUT the W9.b Blinn-Phong specular is a TIGHT glint (shininess 16-64) — at half-res the glint can lose its punch / sub-pixel position. If half-res visibly dulls the highlight, either render the specular at full-res in a cheap second term or accept it as the 'half' quality tradeoff (the hero blob uses 'full'). Validate the lit-default droplet at half-res specifically, not just the flat fill.

Gating the 4-tap normal without re-checking the lit DEFAULT. W16 arm 5 says 'gate surfaceNormal behind the lit path ONLY' as a perf win — but W15 ships lit:true as DEFAULT, so the lit path is the COMMON path and the gate saves nothing for the default blob. The gate still helps a consumer who sets lit:false, but the real default-case win must come from making the lit normal CHEAP (body-only taps or the analytic noised() gradient), not from gating. Do not declare the 4-tap gate a sufficient perf win for the default droplet.

Quiescence false-park freezing a blob that should animate. The at-rest predicate must AND together every motion source (mood transition, pointer spring |v|, trail collapse, click pulse, mid-merge satellite) and wake() from the satellite scheduler's known phase timers — miss one and the blob freezes mid-gesture or never resumes its orbit (the adversarial-verify lane explicitly tests no-false-park). This is a correctness hazard wearing a perf hat.

Trusting readPixels against the live demand loop. preserveDrawingBuffer:false + the parking demand-loop means naive readback returns 0 — any perf/visual gate must use a preserveDrawingBuffer:true test context or screenshot. This is inherited from W08/W15/W16 method caveats and bites any new perf measurement (e.g. confirming the bounding early-out shrinks opaque-fraction correctly).

notes.facet: WebGPU compute metaballs — when a compute pass beats the fragment field; storage-buffer satellite arrays (the W07 lesson)
sotaTechniques: VERDICT: for THIS blob the fragment field IS the SOTA architecture; compute is a net loss. A compute pass beats a fragment field only when (a) ball count is large (hundreds-thousands) and the O(balls x pixels) accumulation is the bottleneck, OR (b) you need GEOMETRY out: marching-cubes/Surface-Nets writing a vertex+index storage buffer for a re-lit 3D mesh (deferred PBR + shadow maps, as in gnikoloff/webgpu-compute-metaballs). Our blob is a 2D screen-space SDF with <=4 satellites + <=15 trail points + <=4 stops merged per-pixel in one full-screen quad; the per-pixel smin loop is trivially cheap and a compute pre-pass only adds a buffer round-trip + sync barrier with zero field-eval savings. The README verdict (line 280: single-pass WebGL2 SDF is SOTA-correct for this body count) is research-validated. Keep it; cite IQ + the compute-metaballs repo as the boundary where it flips.

IQ NORMALIZED smin taxonomy (iquilezles.org/articles/smin): the keystone for W08 un-flood. The k *= N pre-scale makes k a TRUE distance-unit blend band, identical max-inflation across variants so they are interchangeable: quadratic k*=4.0 (g0=1/4), circular k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5))~=3.41 (g0~=0.293), root k*=2.0, exponential k*=1.0. Our sdf-body.glsl.ts already uses the EXACT normalized quadratic (k*=4.0, h*h*k*0.25) and circular forms. The normalization is correct; the flood is a SCALE-composition bug upstream, not a formula bug.

FIELD FLOODING is a NAMED IQ failure mode (the W08 root). The CD-family (quadratic/circular/root) smins are NON-LOCAL: their blend region where |a-b|<k spans to infinity, so every pixel where two distances are within k of each other gets pulled negative. IQ's mitigation is literally W08's prescription: keep k SMALL relative to inter-object spacing; the composed band must be ~0.03-0.08 of a 1.0-wide UV, not the ~0.84 the un-reconciled k*=4.0 produced. Optionally adopt the LOCAL circular-geometric smin (finite support) to cap flood radius structurally rather than only tuning k down (it over-estimates distance, harmless for a 2D direct cut).

SMIN MATERIAL/COLOR BLEND via the blend factor h: directly applicable to W15. IQ's vec2 smin returns the blended distance AND a material weight m in [0,1]; mix(materialB, materialA, m) blends each surface's COLOR/lit-params across the meniscus, not just alpha. Today the blob perturbs one global OKLCh field by FBM noise; the smin-h material channel is the SOTA way to give each satellite its own palette-stop tint bleeding across the neck, a free upgrade to the W11.b multi-stop palette that already ships.

Storage-buffer satellite array (the W07 lesson, generalized). The CONFIRMED Metal defect (AX.md note 1): dynamically-indexed arrays in the WGSL var<uniform> address space return [0,0,0,0] on Apple/Metal; fix is a single var<storage, read> Field buffer, which ALSO lifts the compile-time count cap (storage arrays are runtime-sized). Now WebGPU spec-canon (gpuweb #2559: uniform buffers do not support dynamic indexing, switch to read-only storage). The in-repo pattern is aurora.wgsl.ts: array<vec4f, N> packing (palette .xyz=stop; nucleiPos .xy=pos/.z=radius/.w=bias). The blob's hypothetical WGSL twin packs satellites EXACTLY this way (vec4 xy=pos/z=radius/w=opacity), trail + palette as further arrays, never as dynamically-indexed uniform-struct arrays.

The WebGL2-equivalent hazard already lives in our renderer and is FINE, but flag it. useMetaballRenderer.ts pre-locates every array ELEMENT (uSatPos[0..3], uTrailPos[0..14], uPalette[0..3] via getUniformLocation) and uploads per-element in a fixed loop with a dynamic break: the correct WebGL2 pattern (GLSL ES 300 forbids a uniform-sized array; a #define-sized array + dynamic break is standard) and it does NOT hit the Metal miscompile (WebGL2 over ANGLE handles indexed-uniform reads). Carry the lesson forward: do NOT collapse this into a single packed uniform-array that gets dynamically indexed in a way a WGSL twin would inherit; keep the compile-time-sized + dynamic-break shape on both paths.

Lit-droplet read (W15) from the Codrops/Shadertoy 2D-droplet SOTA our blob descends from (TRAIL_N=15 is literally the Codrops uPointerTrail[15]). The glossy-liquid read is THREE cheap moves we already have machinery for: (1) an SDF-gradient pseudo-3D normal (our IQ tetrahedron surfaceNormal + half-sphere z-lift) feeding Blinn-Phong glint + Fresnel/Schlick rim, wired behind uLit; (2) a power-curve tone lift (Codrops pow(color,7.0)) crushing darks and popping highlights for translucency, of which our core-glow/SSS L-lift in OKLCh is the perceptual-space equivalent; (3) value-noise surface detail driving the reflection coordinate, our FBM-warped membrane. W15's job: turn these ON BY DEFAULT (delete the zero-regression uLit=false gate per slice-13 F3) and re-anchor thickness on the contained body so the rim lives on a curved edge inside the footprint.

3-tap vs 4-tap normal: a real W16 perf lever. The poniesandlight 2D-SDF-blobs research names the 3-tap (not 4-tap) normal as a top single perf win. Our surfaceNormal does 4 sceneDist taps (each a full FBM + smin-loop eval) PER PIXEL. W16 already plans to gate the 4-tap behind the lit path; the refinement is a 3-tap gradient + compute-once-reuse (main() already reuses). With the bounding early-out below, this is the bulk of the oversize-canvas trim.

Bounding-volume early-out (IQ sdfbounding): the concrete mechanism for W16's planned pre-FBM bounding discard. Before the expensive composite (FBM + smin loop + 4-tap normal) test the pixel against a cheap conservative bound: max reach = max(bodyR + maxDisplacement + smoothK, maxSatOrbit + maxSatRadius + smoothK). If sdCircle(uv, 0, boundR) > epsilon the pixel is provably outside the field: early-return transparent, skip everything. On a 160%-overflow canvas where the blob is <40% of pixels this discards the majority of fragments before any FBM/normal cost. Conservative (overestimate) so zero false negatives, exactly IQ's bounding-sphere skip.

Mood model (W16) grounded in procedural-emotive-animation literature. The load-bearing distinction (Evaluating Emotive Character Animations; robot-mood parameterization): EMOTION is explicit behavior that INTERRUPTS ongoing functional behavior; MOOD is integrated WITHOUT interrupting. This says NOT to merge our two channels: the continuous MoodParams set (pulse/noise/irid/smoothK multipliers from valence-arousal) is the MOOD layer (always-on, cross-faded); the one-shot click impulse + pointer pseudopod are the EMOTION layer (transient interrupts). Keep them additive on the same tempo clock (simTimeMs already is). The SOTA web transition pattern is a critically-damped spring per parameter (Rive blend-state ethos: interpolate, never snap); our useBlobMood cross-fade + keyframes.js spring already do this. README should frame it as valence/arousal -> spring-interpolated parameter vector, not an ad-hoc 5-mood lerp.

(2) W15 lit contained-droplet: turn the already-wired uLit/iridescence/SSS ON by default, re-anchor thickness on the contained body, and adopt the IQ smin-h MATERIAL channel so satellite palette-stops bleed across the neck. (3) W16 perf: IQ bounding-sphere early-out (the planned pre-FBM discard) + 3-tap surfaceNormal gated behind lit; together the oversize-canvas trim. (4) W16 mood: frame as the mood(continuous, non-interrupting)-vs-emotion(transient interrupt) split; keep MoodParams and click-impulse as separate additive spring-interpolated channels. The W07 storage-buffer lesson is preserved as a FORWARD constraint: the WebGL2 indexed-uniform-array + dynamic-break pattern is correct and must NOT collapse into a dynamically-indexed packed array; any WGSL twin packs satellites as array<vec4f, N> in var<storage, read> (the aurora.wgsl.ts pattern), never var<uniform>. pitfalls: DO NOT migrate the blob to WebGPU compute: a net loss at <=4 satellites + 15 trail + 4 stops. A compute pre-pass adds a buffer round-trip + sync barrier with zero field-eval savings (the O(balls x pixels) accumulation only bottlenecks at hundreds-thousands of balls). The README already says this (line 280); the only error is relitigating it. Compute wins ONLY for a 3D marching-cubes mesh-extraction path, which the blob is not.

The flood is a SCALE-composition bug, NOT a smin-formula bug: do not rewrite the smin. sdf-body.glsl.ts already carries the exact IQ-normalized quadratic (k*=4.0) and circular forms. AX.md note 13: the missing POS_SCALE on the uSmoothK upload + the un-retuned 0.21-composed band is the root (uSmoothK uploads WITHOUT *POS_SCALE while bodyRadius/satRadius/pointer/noiseAmp all carry it). A shader rewrite would re-flood.

POS_SCALE disposition hazard (AX.md note 13): W08 takes the MINIMAL un-flood (restore POS_SCALE on uSmoothK + retune) and does NOT excise POS_SCALE; W15 either KEEPS that regime or re-derives the ENTIRE length cohort (body/sat/orbit/smin/noise) ATOMICALLY with proof:blob-render as the lock. A PARTIAL migration that deletes POS_SCALE while leaving the smin band W08 just compressed RE-FLOODS. Never half-migrate.

Non-local smin: tuning k down is necessary but the CD-family blend region still extends globally; two distances within k anywhere on the canvas pull negative. A satellite at a wide orbit within k of the body field far from the seam can still form an unwanted neck. Tight k is the practical fix; the circular-geometric LOCAL smin is the structural fix if tuning is fragile, at the cost of a distance over-estimate (harmless for a 2D direct cut, fatal for raymarching).

The 4-tap surfaceNormal evaluates the FULL composite field (FBM + smin loop) 4x PER PIXEL: the single most expensive per-fragment cost on the oversize 160% canvas. Turning lit ON by default (W15) WITHOUT also landing the bounding early-out + 3-tap normal (W16) spikes fragment cost on every visible blob. The two waves are coupled; do not ship W15 default-lit without W16's trim.

OffscreenCanvas/worker is NOT the multi-instance fix W16 needs. The WebGL-context-cap (one context per GooBlob, the prior context-cap incident, slice-13 F2) is solved by ROUTING static/ambient instances to WatercolorDot or a single shared scissored context (AX.md W16), reserving GooBlob for the interactive hero, NOT by moving each instance to a worker (still consumes a context, adds transfer overhead). Worker/OffscreenCanvas helps main-thread jank for ONE heavy canvas, a different problem.

value.js var()-token trap (already patched, keep patched): value.js parseCSSColor THROWS once per frame on a var(--token) color; both GooBlob.vue and the renderer carry the cascade-unwrap workaround (paint onto an element, read back the resolved rgb). W16 plans to hoist ONE resolveTokenColor(css,el) leaf so the renderer stays DOM-free; do not leave the var()-unwrap duplicated in two places.

Do not conflate mood and emotion into one channel. The literature is explicit that mood (continuous, non-interrupting) and emotion (transient, interrupting) are different layers; merging the click-impulse into the MoodParams set would make a click permanently retune the creature's resting personality. Keep them additive on the shared tempo clock.

notes.facet: prefers-reduced-motion rest pose — one composed still frame (peak roundness, trail collapsed, zero stretch)
sotaTechniques: DESIGNED-POSTER over ARBITRARY-FREEZE (the cardinal principle). Apple's Liquid Glass HIG / web.dev / Pope-Tech all converge: a continuously-animating decorative element under reduce must collapse to a DELIBERATE composed frame, not whatever frame the rAF happened to park on. Apple ships this as a 'Default' vs 'Fallback' variant pair bound to the reduce token — the fallback is authored, not a snapshot. Mechanism for us: a restPose() that DRIVES every motion axis to a chosen target value before the one static frame, rather than letting tempo=0 freeze the clock at an arbitrary simTimeMs.

IQ smin band==0 peak-roundness target (the composed-merge geometry). Inigo Quilez's rewritten smin article (the keystone) confirms the quadratic normalization is `k *= 4.0` (g(0)=1/4, so k matches the max inflation exactly) and a CIRCULAR smin `k *= 1.0/(1.0-sqrt(0.5))` that gives 'mathematically perfect circular profiles' (rounder menisci than the quadratic polynomial). For the rest pose 'peak roundness' is NOT a magic optimal-k from IQ (k is user-controlled) — it is a DESIGN target: pose the satellites at their absorbed/inner arrangement so the composite reads as ONE round body, and the smin band is the same un-flooded W08 band, so the still frame is a single clean dome, not a lumpy multi-nucleus freeze.

FROZEN-PHASE-AT-EXTREMUM (the pulse/breath). The body radius is `bodyR = uBodyRadius + sin(uPulsePhase)*uPulseAmp`. A naive freeze paints sin(arbitrary). The SOTA move: pin uPulsePhase to the value that yields PEAK radius (sin = +1, i.e. phase = PI/2) so the breath freezes at its fullest, roundest extent — the 'inhale held' pose reads as alive-at-rest, not caught mid-deflate. Zero uPulseAmp is the alternative (no pulse contribution); peak-radius is the more characterful choice and matches the 'peak roundness' brief verbatim.

ZERO-VELOCITY ELASTIC COLLAPSE (Apple 'disable elastic properties'). Apple's reduce spec literally says 'disables any elastic properties for the material' and caps specular amplitude ≤ 6px. Maps 1:1 to our blob: uStretch contribution → 0 (zero squash-and-stretch — the velocity term `length(uVelocity)` must read 0, which the existing pointer.rest() already guarantees via springX/Y.reset(0,0)), trail collapsed (uTrailCount → 0), click pulse → 0. The stretch is the most vestibular-hostile axis (anisotropic scale = parallax-class motion), so its removal is the highest-priority a11y win.

LIT-SURFACE PRESERVED, MOTION-SURFACE ZEROED (separate the two axes). The reduce obligation is about MOTION, not about flattening the look. The lit dome / Fresnel rim / iridescence are STATIC per-pixel shading on a still field — they paint correctly on a frozen frame and SHOULD be kept (a flattened gray poster is a worse, not better, fallback). Only the TIME-DRIVEN inputs (uTime-scrolled FBM, iridSpeed shimmer, orbit/pulse phase, velocity, trail) freeze. This is the W15 lit-droplet identity surviving into the rest pose: a still, fully-lit, peak-round warm-glass bead.

IGN DITHER ON THE STILL FRAME (banding mitigation specific to freezing). Interleaved Gradient Noise (Jimenez 2014, `dot+fract`, ~half the ALU of white noise, low-frequency-free) breaks 8-bit gradient banding. This matters MORE for the rest pose than the animated state: motion temporally dithers banding so it hides in the churn, but a FROZEN warm-cream dome with a smooth OKLCh lightness roll will show visible banding on the static frame. The README already notes 'an IGN dither to kill the warm-cream banding (the same dither aurora already ships)' is planned — the rest pose is exactly where it earns its keep.

MOOD-NEUTRAL CANONICAL POSE (the mood model at rest). The circumplex {valence, arousal} mood model means the frozen frame inherits whatever mood was live (sleepy = under-merged/flat, excited = over-energized smoothK/iridScale). SOTA character-animation idle practice: the rest pose is the NEUTRAL canonical pose, not the last emotional state. Map: restPose() should snap mood to a designed neutral target (idle, or a bespoke 'rest' affect point at moderate roundness) so the poster is consistent regardless of when reduce flips — a deterministic, bit-stable frame.

Any blob-local matchMedia or a parallel 'reduce' rAF is the SCC/one-path violation the codebase explicitly forbids (useBlobPointer.ts header: 'NO matchMedia here — the substrate owns PRM'). restPose() composes on the substrate's existing one-static-frame call."]

notes.facet: Offscreen / visibility / tab-hidden park — the shared useWebGLCanvas substrate contract for a continuous blob (W08 un-flood + W15 contained-droplet + W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: DEMAND-DRIVEN FRAMELOOP (the headline — render-on-demand). The animation loop runs ONLY while something is changing; when the scene quiesces, the rAF is cancelled (zero frames attached) and a setter that re-introduces motion calls invalidate()/wake() to re-arm. This is the React-Three-Fiber `frameloop="demand"` + `invalidate()` model and it is the single biggest fill/battery lever after the offscreen park. OUR MAP: this IS W16 arm-2 — the substrate ALREADY built the gate (createCanvasLifecycle.tick reschedules IFF `shouldContinue()` is true, line 106-109) and the blob deliberately defeats it (`shouldContinue(){return !paused}`, useMetaballRenderer.ts:518). The fix is to make shouldContinue a real at-rest predicate (mood settled AND pointer spring |v|<eps AND trail collapsed AND click pulse 0 AND no satellite mid-merge) and call canvasHandle.wake() from the satellite phase scheduler — wake() is glass-ui's invalidate(). The plumbing exists: useMetaballRenderer.ts:551 already calls wake() on a color change while parked; the satellite scheduler must do the same on the next orbit/merge phase boundary.

CONTENT-VISIBILITY OFFSCREEN-PARK via contentvisibilityautostatechange + event.skipped. `content-visibility:auto` lets the browser content-skip an offscreen subtree; the element fires `contentvisibilityautostatechange` with `event.skipped===true` (skipped/offscreen) or `false` (rendered), the canonical MDN pattern for stop/startCanvasUpdates. OUR MAP: the substrate implements this EXACTLY (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:154-168 → suspend/resume('off-screen')), and GooBlob.vue:185 sets `content-visibility:auto` + `contain:layout style` + `contain-intrinsic-size:auto none`. This is SOTA and already shipped — PRESERVE it. The README's 'parks aggressively' claim is true for this path.

PAGE-VISIBILITY EXPLICIT PARK (document.hidden + visibilitychange) — belt-AND-suspenders over the browser's automatic background-tab rAF stall. The browser DOES auto-stop rAF in hidden tabs, but timers (the mood/satellite phase clocks), audio, and network keep running; an app must still explicitly stop its own non-rAF work + its GL state machine. OUR MAP: the substrate owns ONE writer of the 'tab-hidden' reason (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:145-150) — correct: it parks the rAF deterministically rather than trusting the engine's throttle, which is the right call because the renderer's startTime/elapsed math (line 103) and the mood `tick(dt)` would otherwise accumulate a huge dt on tab-return (the resume() at line 138 already guards this with `startTime = performance.now() - 1000`). Keep it.

THREE-REASON SUSPEND SET — one-writer-per-reason ORed park. The loop runs IFF a `Set<reason>` is empty; each reason ('tab-hidden'|'off-screen'|'manual') is cleared ONLY by its owner, so a tab-show can never lift a legitimately-skipped offscreen suspend. This is the principled generalization of the three independent levers above into one gate. OUR MAP: the substrate's model (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:83-150) is the textbook implementation and W16 F6 names the ONE latent flaw — both the substrate's content-visibility path AND the consumer's IntersectionObserver fallback (useMetaballRenderer.ts:188-189) write the SAME 'off-screen' key, so an IO resume can lift a CV-legitimate skip. Fix: give the IO fallback its OWN 'off-screen-io' reason key so the loop runs only when BOTH agree (Set empty). This makes 'one writer per reason' literally true — the invariant the Set model promises.

INTERSECTIONOBSERVER rootMargin WARM-BAND FALLBACK. An IO with `rootMargin:200px` parks the loop when the surface scrolls past a warm band outside the viewport — the cross-engine fallback for browsers without contentvisibilityautostatechange (Safari historically lacked content-visibility events). OUR MAP: shipped (useIntersectionPause + useMetaballRenderer.ts:185-192, pauseWhenHidden:false so it owns ONLY off-screen, leaving tab-hidden to the substrate). The 200px warm band pre-warms the loop just before the blob scrolls in, avoiding a blank-then-pop. This composes WITH the CV path (both ORed) — the F6 reason-key split is exactly what keeps them from racing.

LIVE prefers-reduced-motion FREEZE (matchMedia change re-monitor → one static frame then park). PRM is monitored live (not read once); under reduce the loop paints ONE frame then parks, and a matchMedia `change` listener re-arms on un-reduce. A CSS reset cannot reach a WebGL rAF, so the JS substrate must own this. OUR MAP: shipped (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:93-123, gates the RESCHEDULE not the suspend Set — so an onscreen reduced surface never blanks, it just stops moving). This is the WCAG-aligned default; it is DISTINCT from the user-facing DockBackgroundToggle pause (WCAG 2.2.2), which must be reachable by ALL users, not gated behind PRM.

WEBGPU PARITY via a backend-agnostic lifecycle core. The exact same suspend-Set/tick/wake/visibility/content-visibility/PRM machinery is lifted out of the WebGL2 backend so the WebGPU sibling inherits the park gate for free — a parked compute dispatch attaches zero work on both backends. OUR MAP: already done (createCanvasLifecycle.ts is the agnostic core; useWebGLCanvas + createGPUCanvas are thin wrappers). The SOTA confirmation: WebGPU render loops use the identical rAF + document.hidden pattern, so no WebGPU-specific park is needed — proof:offscreen-pause extends to it. The quiescence predicate (arm 2) is backend-agnostic too: it reads mood/pointer/satellite state, not gl, so it lands in the consumer hook and benefits both backends.

QUALITY-AXIS DEGRADE (half-res metaball pass + bilinear upsample). Render the expensive fragment pass at half internal resolution and upsample — ~4x fragment savings for weak GPUs — as a complement to the park (you pay less PER visible frame, on top of paying for fewer frames). OUR MAP: W16 arm-2 wires the never-shipped `quality:'full'|'half'` axis (README marked 'Planned — AW'). This is the right SOTA companion to the demand-park: park handles WHEN to render, quality handles HOW MUCH per render. Pairs with the W16 arm-5 pre-FBM bounding discard (length(uv)>maxReach → return transparent BEFORE the two FBM calls) and the gated surfaceNormal 4-tap (only on the lit/iridescence/SSS path) — both reduce per-fragment ALU on the already-contained W15 field.
notes.applicability: THE SUBSTRATE IS THE MODEL — DO NOT REBUILD IT. The W08/W15/W16 facet is NOT 'add an offscreen-park' (the substrate already ships the three-reason Set + content-visibility + IntersectionObserver + live-PRM, and the AX docs explicitly call the F6 rootCause 'N/A — this is the well-designed substrate'). The facet is THREE precise integration fixes ON TOP of a correct substrate, all gated to W16 (W08/W15 touch NO lifecycle code — they own the smin distance regime and the contained-droplet geometry/identity respectively). PATH FORWARD: (1) W16 arm-2 — replace the perpetual `shouldContinue(){return !paused}` with a true quiescence predicate that reads the EXISTING at-rest state (useBlobMood must expose a 'transitioning' flag — it has `transitioning` as a private let at useBlobMood.ts:117, surface it read-only; useBlobPointer exposes spring-at-rest + trail-collapsed + pulse-0) AND call canvasHandle.wake() from the satellite scheduler on the next phase boundary. This converts a perpetual 60fps FBMx3 + OKLCh-per-fragment burn into an event-scheduled loop. This is the single biggest onscreen lever and only makes sense on W15's CONTAINED field (a flooded slab has nothing to quiesce). (2) W16 F6 — split the IO reason key to 'off-screen-io' (createCanvasLifecycle.ts + the useMetaballRenderer IO write) so CV and IO never race the shared 'off-screen' key; this is a ~2-line precision fix, not a redesign. (3) W16 arm-1 — the WCAG-2.2.2 pause seam: the renderer ALREADY returns {pause,resume} (which call suspend/resume('manual')) but GooBlob.vue:94 DISCARDS the return and :148 omits them from defineExpose — so DockBackgroundToggle's pause is a runtime no-op. Fix via the RATIFIED v-model:paused shape (structurally un-droppable, matches Aurora's useAurora pause/resume parity). The quiescence predicate is backend-agnostic (reads mood/pointer/satellite, never gl), so it benefits the WebGPU sibling for free. README: flip the 'Planned — AW' quality-axis + the defineExpose pause/resume table to landed; document the park taxonomy (manual/tab-hidden/off-screen-io/off-screen-cv/PRM) as five distinct levers, and that an idle ONSCREEN blob now quiesces (the README currently only claims offscreen/hidden/PRM park, never onscreen-idle — that gap is the W16 RED witness).
pitfalls: FALSE-PARK / FROZEN BLOB. The quiescence predicate must NOT park a blob that SHOULD be animating — mid-merge satellite, active pointer, in-flight mood transition, decaying trail, non-zero click pulse. If ANY of those is live the loop must run; the adversarial-verify lane (W16) explicitly tests this. The wake() from the satellite scheduler is the load-bearing half: if the scheduler forgets to wake on the next orbit/merge phase, the blob freezes then jerks (a worse artefact than a perpetual loop). useBlobMood currently has NO way to wake the loop from a queued setMood — the predicate parks while `transitioning` is false, but a pending auto-mood arc (e.g. idleMs crossing IDLE_SLEEP_MS=6000 → sleepy) has no timer-driven wake; that transition must be scheduled, not polled, or it never fires on a parked loop.

CONTENT-VISIBILITY FIRST-EVENT TIMING IS UNDERSPECIFIED (w3c/csswg-drafts #9803). The spec does NOT pin whether/when the FIRST contentvisibilityautostatechange fires relative to the 'close to viewport' computation — Chromium has shipped intermittent single-vs-double initial fires. Do NOT rely on the first event to establish initial park state; seed it explicitly. The substrate is robust here (it arms running and lets the event flip it), but a consumer reasoning 'I'll wait for the first skipped event' can mis-initialize. The IntersectionObserver fallback covers the gap, which is another reason the F6 reason-key split matters (the two must not race on init).

SHARED 'off-screen' REASON-KEY RACE (the W16 F6 root). Today BOTH the substrate's content-visibility path and the consumer's IntersectionObserver write suspended.add/delete('off-screen'). Scenario: CV legitimately skips (true offscreen) → adds 'off-screen'; an IO callback fires intersecting (within the 200px warm band but still CV-skipped) → deletes 'off-screen' → loop resumes on a content-skipped element. The Set-of-one-key promises one-writer-per-reason but two writers share the key. Fix is mandatory before the quiescence work or the demand-park can be silently un-parked by the fallback.

rAF startTime / dt ACCUMULATION ON RESUME. A long park (tab hidden for minutes) makes (performance.now()-startTime)/1000 huge; the first resumed frame would jump the animation forward by the full park duration, and useBlobMood.tick(dt) would fast-forward the mood arc. The substrate guards this (resume() resets startTime to now()-1000, createCanvasLifecycle.ts:138; onReducedMotionChange resets on un-reduce, :120) — but any NEW wake path (the satellite scheduler's wake) must NOT bypass this, and the mood/pointer tick(dt) must clamp dt (a huge dt would also overshoot springs). Verify the quiescence wake routes through the same startTime-reset discipline as resume().

DON'T FIGHT THE BROWSER'S AUTO-THROTTLE, BUT DON'T TRUST IT EITHER. The browser auto-stops rAF in hidden tabs, but the substrate's EXPLICIT tab-hidden park is still correct (it deterministically parks GL state + avoids the dt-accumulation, and timers/satellite clocks the browser does NOT stop). The pitfall is the inverse: a naive `if(document.hidden) setTimeout(loop,100)` fallback (seen in some WebGPU samples) would keep a 10Hz loop alive in a hidden tab — the OPPOSITE of the goal. The substrate's full-park is right; do not regress to a throttle-loop.

OFFSCREENCANVAS+WORKER IS A TRAP HERE (do not adopt). Moving the GL to a worker via transferControlToOffscreen frees the main thread but you lose direct canvas access (every pause/resume/color/pointer update becomes postMessage), and — critically — the worker would need its OWN visibility/content-visibility/PRM plumbing (those events fire on the main-thread DOM element, not in the worker). For a small decorative blob the main-thread cost is dominated by the fragment shader on the GPU, not JS; the worker adds message-passing latency to the pause seam for no win. The substrate's main-thread model is correct for this workload. Note this explicitly in the README so a future contributor doesn't 'optimize' into it.

MULTI-INSTANCE CONTEXT CAP IS ORTHOGONAL TO THE PARK (W16 F2). Parking the rAF does NOT release the WebGL2 context — an offscreen-but-mounted blob still holds a context slot (Chromium caps ~8-16/page; commit 9427536 hit this live). The IntersectionPause stops frames but the getContext slot persists until teardown (which forces WEBGL_lose_context, useWebGLCanvas.ts:124). So the park solves BATTERY/FILL, not the context cap; the cap needs the separate routing (static register → WatercolorDot; one shared scissored context for a true interactive grid). Don't conflate the two — a reviewer might think 'we park offscreen, so the cap is handled' (it is not).

MANUAL PAUSE vs PRM FREEZE MUST STAY DISTINCT (never collapse). The DockBackgroundToggle 'manual' pause is a WCAG-2.2.2 Level-A control reachable by ALL users; the PRM freeze is a befitting-silent browser-API degradation reachable only by reduced-motion users. They are two different reason owners ('manual' in the Set vs the reschedule-gate). Collapsing them (e.g. gating the pause button behind PRM, or making PRM throw) violates both the fail-explicit precept and WCAG. Keep manual on the suspend Set, PRM on the reschedule gate.

notes.facet: Blob as a UI affordance — loading/thinking/status indicator vs decorative backdrop; the intuitive interaction mapping (grounding the W08 un-flood + W15 lit contained droplet + the W16 integration/interaction/mood model)
sotaTechniques: IQ quadratic smooth-min with k-normalization (`k *= 4.0`) — the smin subtracts `h*h*k*0.25` from `min(a,b)` so the parameter k reads in TRUE distance units (the blend BAND width), making it interchangeable across variants. This is exactly W08's keystone: once the shader normalizes k, the COMPOSED uploaded value (config default x mood multiplier x POS_SCALE) must be re-solved as ONE budget against the new regime — Quilez's own recommendation is the quadratic ('fast, close enough to circular, never overestimates').

Smin NON-LOCALITY / 'lack of Rigidity' is the named root-cause of the flood — Quilez proves the polynomial smin is NOT local: its effect 'spans to infinity', underestimating the field along shape edges even for shapes far apart. With an over-large effective k (W08's measured ~0.864 in a 1.0-wide UV) `min(a,b) - 0.216` drives the whole composite field negative → alpha=1 everywhere → the canvas-flooding slab. The fix is a SMALL k (target effective seam-pull ~0.03-0.08), never a second normalizer.

Circular smooth-min (the CD/Clamped-Difference family, the NEW part of IQ's 2024 rewrite) — kernel constrained so g(-1)=g'(-1)=0, g(1)=g'(1)=1, giving rounder menisci and a HARD cutoff beyond k distance units (more 'rigid' than the quadratic, less flooding). Our `BlobMerge='quadratic'|'circular'` type ALREADY exposes this axis; the circular variant is the principled upgrade if the quadratic seam reads too creased on the contained droplet.

Distance-cutoff / bounding-discard for fragment cost — since each metaball only influences a ~k+radius neighborhood, a pre-pass `length(uv) > maxReach → return transparent` BEFORE the expensive FBM/OKLCh work skips dead border pixels. This is W16 arm-5 verbatim (the pre-FBM bounding discard + gating the 4-tap surfaceNormal behind the lit path).

Codrops 'spheres-along-the-mouse-trail' droplet pattern (Tympanus, Jun 2025) — the canonical INTERACTION mapping for a metaball: arrange a short decaying-radius chain of smin-merged spheres along the pointer trail so the blob stretches an elastic pseudopod toward the cursor and snaps back. This is precisely our `useBlobPointer` trail + `uTrail[TRAIL_N]` — the SOTA reach-toward affordance reuses the satellite plumbing, no new sim.

Volume-preserving squash-and-stretch (Disney principle #1, ported to UI) — a velocity-driven anisotropic UV warp where the perpendicular axis scales `1/sa` to preserve area. Gives ~80% of soft-body 'weight' with zero physics sim. Our `stretch` config + W10 squash is this; the SOTA framing is that squash-stretch + anticipation + follow-through are what make motion read as a LIVING creature vs a mechanical pulse.

Circumplex Affect Model (Russell's valence/arousal 2D plane) as the mood engine — every named mood is a POINT in {valence, arousal} space and the per-mood parameters are DERIVED from one principled surface, not hand-tuned in isolation. Our `useBlobMood` ALREADY implements this (MOOD_AVA + paramsFor): arousal drives motion energy (orbit/wobble/pulse/noise/iridescence), valence warms the palette + sets pointer lean (pleasant leans IN, unpleasant shies AWAY). This is the academically-grounded way to map an abstract 'mood' to concrete shader params.

Conversational-state avatar model (Microsoft Copilot 'Mico', Oct 2025) — a production blob-as-affordance: a compact animated blob whose color/shape/micro-expression signal listening / thinking / acknowledging / responding / idle. The canonical voice-assistant state vocabulary is Idle (soft glow) → Listening (waveform/expansion) → Thinking (slow rotation/churn) → Responding (pulsing waves). Maps DIRECTLY onto our mood states + tempo + merge-rate as a status/thinking indicator.

Deliberate non-photorealism to dodge the uncanny valley — Mico is intentionally non-human and blob-like specifically to avoid over-anthropomorphization and the uncanny valley, AND is user-disableable. The SOTA lesson for our blob: an abstract gooey creature is a FEATURE (warmth without the uncanny-valley risk of a face), and the affordance must always be optional/pausable (our WCAG-2.2.2 DockBackgroundToggle seam — W16).

Easing/velocity as emotional vocabulary (motion-design 2025/26 consensus) — the SAME transition reads premium, playful, or mechanical purely by easing curve + duration; a critically-damped spring (overshoot + settle) reads as 'weight/aliveness', a linear lerp reads dead. W10's frame-rate-independent spring pointer (`@mkbabb/keyframes.js`) and the de-synced breath pulse (W15 — break the single `sin` so the membrane never reads mechanical) are this principle applied.

Demand-scheduled / event-driven rendering for an idle affordance — a calm ambient blob should QUIESCE (park the rAF) at rest and WAKE on a state change or scheduled satellite phase, not burn 60fps perpetually. This is W16's quiescence signal feeding `shouldContinue` + the offscreen/PRM substrate park. SOTA for ambient WebGL: render only when something is actually changing.
notes.applicability: THE FACET SPLITS INTO TWO AFFORDANCE REGISTERS, AND THE WAVES SHOULD MAKE THE SPLIT EXPLICIT. (1) DECORATIVE BACKDROP / AMBIENT BRAND MARK — the blob conveys no information (aria-hidden), is calm/slow/on-palette, MUST carry a pause control if it auto-runs >5s, and should be cheap (WatercolorDot for the static register; reserve the GL GooBlob for the ONE interactive hero per W16 arm-3). (2) STATUS / THINKING / LIVING INDICATOR — the Mico model: the blob's mood + tempo + merge-rate ENCODE a state (idle/listening/thinking/responding). Our circumplex mood engine is already the right substrate for this — a consumer maps app-state → setMood (or arousal/valence) so 'thinking' = high arousal + churning merge, 'idle/sleepy' = low arousal + slow breath. PATH FORWARD PER WAVE: W08 (un-flood) — the smin re-derivation is the un-negotiable prerequisite: NEITHER affordance register is legible on a canvas-flooding slab. Re-solve config.smoothK + the mood smoothK MULTIPLIER (reframe as 1.0-centred, not absolute) + restore POS_SCALE as ONE budget against `k *= 4.0`, target effective seam-pull ~0.03-0.08 (the pre-AW working 0.034). Quilez's article is the authority that the quadratic is correct and that a small k is the only un-flood — do not add a second normalizer. W15 (lit contained droplet) — containment RESURFACES the affordance: the lit warm-cream dome, Fresnel rim, iridescence, and the wired interaction all already ship but paint nothing while the field is oversize. Ship lit:true + the low iridescence/SSS floor as the DEFAULT identity (delete the 'zero-regression' flag-gating — a greenfield product's canonical look IS the SOTA look). Derive the default palette from glass-ui warm tokens so the un-themed blob reads house-warm, not a cold liquid-glass bubble; cold/neon stay consumer presets. The Codrops droplet-trail pattern + volume-preserving squash become LEGIBLE once the body is contained and the magnitudes re-balanced against the smaller body. W16 (integration/interaction/mood/README) — make the affordance REAL and INTEGRATED: the v-model:paused seam actually parks the loop (the WCAG-2.2.2 obligation + the optional/disableable lesson from Mico); the quiescence signal makes the idle ambient register cheap; the mood model gets its README home framing the TWO registers explicitly (decorative vs status-indicator) with the circumplex/Mico/Codrops/IQ lineage as the research backing. The README should name the affordance contract: 'this is an ambient/expressive creature, NOT a determinate progress bar — for measurable progress use a Progress/Skeleton primitive' (the blob conveys MOOD/ALIVENESS, not a percentage).
pitfalls: smin FLOODING is the headline hazard and it is ALREADY the live W08 bug — an over-large effective k drives the whole composite SDF negative (alpha=1 everywhere = the slab). The non-locality is mathematical (IQ: the polynomial smin 'spans to infinity'), so the ONLY fix is a small k re-solved as one budget; a clamp or a second normalizer is a forbidden workaround.

The static-math gate trap — `proof:blob-smin-normalized` shipped GREEN while the blob was totally broken because it grep'd the fudge-deletion + ran an ISOLATED k-sweep, never composing config x mood x POS_SCALE against the body radius and never rendering a pixel. Any affordance/mood claim MUST be locked by a rendered-pixel gate (W08's proof:blob-render), never a source-string or pure-math gate. 'Runtime Truth Beats Source Claims.'

Mechanical motion kills the affordance — a single un-de-synced `sin` breath pulse and a linear pointer lerp read as a dead automaton, not a living creature. The emotional payload is entirely in the easing/velocity (spring overshoot + settle, de-synced FBM breath). This is the difference between a status-indicator that feels alive and one that feels like a spinner.

Over-anthropomorphization / uncanny valley — adding a face or photoreal detail backfires (the explicit Mico design rationale). The abstract gooey blob is the SAFE expressive register; resist the urge to add eyes/mouth. Keep it a creature, not a character.

Treating the blob as a determinate progress indicator — it conveys NO percentage and is aria-hidden/decorative. Using it where users expect measurable progress (a real loading bar) is a misuse; it signals 'alive/thinking/busy', not '47% done'. The README must draw this line.

Garish iridescence — the thin-film sheen must be clamped to the warm arc (~560-650nm, iridescenceAmt ~0.18, warm-cream tint in OKLCh not sRGB white) or it reads as a cheap rainbow bubble and leaves glass-ui's cream-glass identity (W9/W15 pitfall).

Perpetual-rAF battery/fill-rate burn for an idle ambient affordance — the demand gate the substrate built is defeated by `shouldContinue(){return !paused}` (W16 RED witness 2). An onscreen idle blob burning FBM x3 twice/pixel + an OKLCh round-trip per fragment forever is the opposite of 'premium ambient'. The affordance must quiesce at rest.

Multi-instance WebGL context-cap exhaustion (~8-16/page in Chromium) — a decorative grid of GooBlobs silently blanks the Nth instance (commit 9427536's prior live incident). notes.facet: Integration with glass-ui — the injected ColorResolver seam, token-driven palette, substrate sharing with aurora
sotaTechniques: ColorResolver as a dependency-injection seam (function-as-interface): the blob takes `colorResolver: (css)=>[r,g,b]` as a REQUIRED prop, never resolving color itself. This is the SOTA decoupling pattern (Mattia, the GLSL-design-tokens adapter, classic DI 'seam'): the shader depends only on the resolved gamma-sRGB triple, the resolution policy is the consumer's. value.js (the color source) injects its own; the demo uses `defaultBlobColorResolver`. The function-shaped seam is lighter than a service-locator/interface and is the right grain for one method.

Browser-cascade var()-unwrap (the canonical token->RGB resolution): a `var(--token)` cannot be parsed by value.js (or any JS color lib) and a direct `getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--token')` returns the token VERBATIM (still `var()`/oklch). The SOTA trick (Nicolas Mattia 2025, confirmed independently) is to PAINT the string onto a throwaway `el.style.color` and read back `getComputedStyle(el).color` — the browser resolves the cascade to a concrete `rgb(...)`. glass-ui already does exactly this in GooBlob.vue (`resolveColorString`) and the renderer (`resolveRimColor`); it is the correct pattern, and W16 hoists it to ONE `resolveTokenColor(css, el)` leaf.

Reactive theme re-resolution via MutationObserver on <html>.class: a token resolves to a DIFFERENT concrete color under `.dark`, so the unwrap must re-run on a theme flip. glass-ui uses a `MutationObserver` (attributeFilter:['class']) rather than `@vueuse` useDark — preserving the SCC-free discipline. Mattia's alternative (resolve per-frame, no listener) is rejected here: per-frame getComputedStyle is a forced sync layout reflow (~0.02ms each but a layout-thrash risk on a 60fps surface); the cache + observer is the better integration choice for a token that changes rarely.

Uniform-array palette swap (N in-family stops, NOT a LUT texture): the blob uploads `uPalette[MAX_BLOB_STOPS=4]` as a gamma-sRGB uniform array with `uStopCount<=1` falling back to `uBaseColor` (zero-regression single-color path). Palette-swap-in-shader theory (pvigier) says a uniform array is the right tool below ~16-256 stops; a 1D LUT texture only wins for large/interpolated palettes. For <=4 stops the uniform array is SOTA-correct: simpler, no texture bind, and the blob interpolates in OKLab in-shader (`samplePaletteOklch`) which a hardware-filtered 8-bit LUT could not do without banding.

Seed->harmony palette derivation sharing ONE vocabulary with aurora (`deriveBlobPalette` + `ColorHarmony` hoisted to `/color`): one seed color -> 2-4 gamut-mapped OKLCh stops via the SAME `deriveHue`/`gamutMapStop`/`ColorHarmony` primitives aurora's `deriveAurora` consumes (no forked deriver). This is the integration headline: token-driven palette + shared harmony math, value.js as the single color core (`proof:single-color-core`, `proof:color-acyclic` keep it a DAG). Midpoint chroma-bump (bell peaking at t=0.5) keeps a vivid pair off the grey OKLab midpoint.

Shared WebGL2 substrate, NOT a shared GL context: aurora and the blob both compose `useWebGLCanvas`/`createCanvasLifecycle` (one rAF demand-gate, three-reason suspend Set, content-visibility offscreen-park, live PRM monitor, context-loss self-heal). Each instance still owns ONE `getContext('webgl2')`. The substrate is shared CODE; the CONTEXT is per-instance. This is correct for 1-2 hero surfaces but hits the browser ~8-context cap (oldest-context-lost) when many blobs mount.

Shared procedural-color GLSL chunk (`procedural-color.glsl.ts`): the OETF + the four Ottosson OKLab/OKLCh mat3 literals (transposed column-major) + FBM_ROT are SPLICED into BOTH metaball.frag.ts and aurora.frag.ts so the color math can never diverge (AV.W2). Return-space is deliberately NOT unified — `oklchToLinear` (aurora bakes linear, ACES-tonemaps in linear) vs `oklchToGammaRgb` (the blob's DEC-AT-7 faithful gamma exit); forcing one re-introduces the ~2.2x-too-dark A5/A2 defect.

Circumplex (valence/arousal) affect model as ONE principled mood surface: the five named moods are POINTS in a 2-axis {valence, arousal} space and every per-mood param is DERIVED by `paramsFor` (arousal->motion energy: orbit/wobble/pulse/noise/sheen; valence->warmth: hue range/chroma/brightness/pointer-lean). Russell's circumplex is the canonical academic framework (arXiv:2502.16038: arousal modulates motion energy, valence determines color warmth) AND a named 2026 UI trend (mascots that change mood on interaction). glass-ui's mapping matches the literature exactly.

Master tempo scalar `tempo * dt` (never `* uTime`): ONE scalar multiplies every INTEGRATED dt (mood.tick, spring, orbit/phase, noise scroll) into an accumulated `simTimeMs`; the shader reads simTimeMs/1000, NOT the absolute clock. `tempo=0` (dock-pause/PRM) freezes motion WITHOUT a noise-scroll discontinuity (scaling the clock makes FBM jump). The substrate OWNS PRM + pause; the renderer only READS them to set tempo (no parallel matchMedia — the AV.W7-removed anti-pattern).
notes.applicability: "PATH FORWARD per wave. W08 (un-flood) is a SCALE re-derivation, not a shader rewrite or a seam change — the ColorResolver/palette/substrate integration is correct; the flood is purely that `uSmoothK` uploads WITHOUT `*POS_SCALE` while every other length carries it, so the composed `k~=0.84` floods the field negative across the whole 1.0-wide UV. Fix: restore `*POS_SCALE` on the uSmoothK upload + re-tune the config default/mood-lerp to land a ~0.03-0.08 effective seam band, store mood smoothK as a 1.0-centred MULTIPLIER. The integration facet's stake: the var()-unwrap + ColorResolver are confirmed-correct and untouched here (slice-11 proved the lit rim + iridescence paint correctly on the VISIBLE edge — only the field scale is wrong). W15 (lit contained-droplet): the integration deliverable is to make the warm-cream DEFAULT identity load-bearing — turn ON lit + low iridescence + low SSS in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, DELETE the 'zero regression' off-by-default flag-gating (a legacy instinct forbidden in greenfield), and DERIVE the default palette from glass-ui warm tokens through `deriveBlobPalette` so an un-themed `var(--primary)` blob belongs to the cream-glass system (cold/neon stays explicit opt-in). The seed->harmony deriver + the shared ColorHarmony vocabulary are the token-driven-palette mechanism that makes this one-line. Re-express the WHOLE length cohort (body/sat/orbit/smin/noise) in wrapper-normalized units ATOMICALLY (either KEEP W08's POS_SCALE regime or bake 0.625 into all constants in one wave — never a partial migration that re-floods); `proof:blob-render` is the regression-lock. W16 (integration): (1) FIX the runtime no-op — GooBlob.vue discards `useMetaballRenderer`'s return so `blob.value.pause()` is `undefined` and the documented DockBackgroundToggle wiring silently fails; capture `const {pause,resume}=useMetaballRenderer(...)` and re-expose, OR collapse to a `v-model:paused` prop. (2) HOIST one `resolveTokenColor(css,el)` leaf (the var()-unwrap is duplicated verbatim in GooBlob.vue + the renderer) so the renderer stays DOM-free. (3) MULTI-INSTANCE context cap: route static/ambient instances to WatercolorDot (the CSS/SVG sibling, zero GL context) and reserve GooBlob for the ONE interactive hero — the SOTA single-context-with-scissor multiplexing (webglfundamentals multiple-views) is the heavier alternative if multiple LIVE blobs are genuinely needed, but the WatercolorDot routing is the KISS answer for ambient marks. (4) the mood model: KEEP the exported `useBlobMood` (it is load-bearing — consumed by GooBlob.vue), wire the sub-orphans (`setMood` now has the internal `update()` caller; the previously-dead orbitSpeedScale/wobbleScale either wire into the satellite tick or collapse to one `energy` scalar) — no false 'excise for <2 consumers'. (5) the value.js consumer-fork repatriation is the named close-criterion: once W08/W15/W16 land the contained lit droplet, value.js DELETES its local goo-blob fork and consumes `@mkbabb/glass-ui/goo-blob`, injecting value.js's OWN color through the ColorResolver seam (value.js IS the color source — the seam was designed for exactly this clean consumer injection)."
pitfalls: Per-frame getComputedStyle for the token unwrap is a forced-synchronous-layout (reflow) trap. Mattia's article calls it ~0.02ms and 'run every frame' — that is fine for a tiny demo but on a 60fps full-surface blob it can thrash layout. glass-ui's cache + MutationObserver is the safer integration; do NOT regress to per-frame reads. The unwrap also paints onto `el.style.color` then restores it — a write/read/write on the live element; keep it cached so it runs once per unique string, not per frame.

oklch()/lab() base colors silently break a naive resolver. Mattia's appendix flags that newer color spaces need a slow ~3.3ms 2D-canvas workaround OR they don't resolve. glass-ui sidesteps this entirely by routing the CONCRETE string through value.js's parser (DOM-free, SSR-safe) AFTER the var()-unwrap reduces a token to a concrete rgb()/oklch() — but a consumer who injects a hand-rolled regex-rgb resolver will silently fail on an oklch() literal. The README must state the resolver contract: it receives a CONCRETE color string (post-unwrap) and must handle every CSS color form (hex/rgb/hsl/oklch/lab).

Forcing one return-space across aurora+blob re-introduces the ~2.2x-too-dark A5/A2 defect. The temptation in 'share the color core' is to make `oklchToLinear` the single exit. It is NOT — aurora bakes LINEAR (ACES in linear), the blob exits GAMMA (DEC-AT-7 faithful lift) and applies the OETF in-shader. The shared chunk is the MATRICES + OETF, not the return space. `proof:blob-space-gamma` + `proof:aurora-space-gamma` are born-RED to catch this.

The pause/resume seam is a typecheck-GREEN runtime no-op. GooBlob.vue throws away the renderer handle, so `blob.value.pause()` is `undefined` — vue-tsc passes because the methods exist on the DISCARDED return type. This is the exact binding-verification class (stale prop/emit/expose that no-ops; only e2e catches it). W16's gate must MOUNT a blob, wire DockBackgroundToggle, and assert the rAF actually parks — not just that the method typechecks.

Multi-instance context exhaustion: one `getContext('webgl2')` per GooBlob hits the browser ~8-context cap (Chromium loses the OLDEST context silently — the surface goes blank with no error). The substrate's shared CODE does not share the CONTEXT. Many ambient blobs MUST route to WatercolorDot (zero GL) or a single scissored context; do not mount N live GooBlobs.

uStopCount<=1 fallback must be honored at BOTH the JS upload and the GLSL sample. An empty `paletteStops[]` uploads uBaseColor into every uPalette slot AND sets uStopCount, and `samplePaletteOklch` early-returns uBaseColor when uStopCount<=1 — both halves are needed; a mismatch (e.g. count set but slots zero, or slots filled but count 0) paints black or a single wrong stop. This is the un-threaded-uniform class: a palette change must trace config->renderer upload->shader sample in one wave.

A new lit/iridescence/SSS uniform added to the shader WITHOUT threading it through `UNIFORM_NAMES` + the upload in useMetaballRenderer silently no-ops (vue-tsc + units miss it). Every new uniform must trace shader->renderer upload->config type atomically; W15 flipping defaults ON makes this live for the first time, so a previously-uploaded-but-dead uniform will suddenly matter — verify each paints.

Scaling the absolute clock instead of dt makes the FBM noise JUMP on a tempo/pause change. The master-tempo discipline is `simTimeMs += tempo*dt` then read simTimeMs — NOT `uTime *= tempo`. A naive 'multiply uTime by tempo' looks equivalent but discontinuously warps the noise scroll on every pause/PRM toggle. `proof:blob-tempo-suppression` guards it.
