notes.facet: Containment / clipping — the contained-droplet geometry (the blob stays in its box, satellites do not overflow wrongly)
sotaTechniques: IQ-NORMALIZED SMIN — k IS THE INFLATION (the un-flood keystone). IQ's 2024 smin rewrite normalizes k so it equals EXACTLY the maximum surface inflation (the 'pull-inward' the blend adds). For the quadratic polynomial the normalizer is k*=4.0 (already shipped in sdf-body.glsl.ts:29); circular is k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5)); the inward bias is k*g(0) (quadratic g(0)=1/4). MECHANISM: once normalized, an uploaded uSmoothK of 0.216 literally inflates every merged surface by ~0.216 distance units in a 0.5-half-extent UV — min(a,b)-0.216 drives the composite SDF negative across the whole canvas (the flood). The fix is arithmetic, not a shader edit: bring the COMPOSED upload (config.smoothK x mood-multiplier x POS_SCALE) back to the ~0.03-0.08 inflation band the pre-AW oracle ran at.

POS_SCALE LENGTH-COHERENCE — the smin band IS a length. Every length-like uniform (uBodyRadius:404, satRadius:495, uPointer:363, noiseAmp:423, pulseAmp:417) rides x POS_SCALE (=1/1.6=0.625, the inner-region compression); uSmoothK alone (:437-439) does NOT. MECHANISM: the smin inflation is measured in the SAME UV space as the radii, so it must carry the SAME compression or it is ~1.6x oversized relative to every other length — the second half of the flood. Restoring x POS_SCALE on the upload puts the merge band on one coordinate system (the W08 minimal un-flood).

SHARP-MIN FOR CONTAINMENT (the Codrops k=7 idiom). The canonical premium droplet reference (Codrops 2025 three.js droplet) uses k=7 — a TIGHT/sharp smin near a hard min — specifically because a higher k contains merged regions into a crisp meniscus instead of a diffuse low-threshold flood. MECHANISM: containment is a JOINT property of (smin inflation) AND (the alpha cutoff). glass-ui already cuts alpha at the d=0 isosurface with fwidth AA (metaball.frag.ts:277-278) — the correct sharp-cutoff equivalent — so the lever is the inflation magnitude, not the threshold. Confirms the un-flood direction: SMALLER effective k = more contained.

ONE-FOOTPRINT-BUDGET GEOMETRY (solve the length cohort together, not per-constant). The maximum field reach is bodyRadius + orbitRadius + satelliteRadius + the smin inflation, evaluated as ONE sum against the wrapper half-extent. At HEAD body 0.25 + orbit 0.35 + sat 0.13 = 0.73 reach in a 0.5 half-extent = ~1.46x the half-box BEFORE smin inflation. MECHANISM: treat the wrapper as the HARD bound and solve all four terms so the widest-orbit + trail excursion fits ~70-80% of the footprint — a single atomic re-derivation (the W15 keystone) so a future nudge to one constant cannot silently re-overflow.

BOUNDING-SPHERE EARLY DISCARD (the cheap pre-FBM clip + perf). IQ's SDF-bounding article: wrap the expensive field in a cheap bound and early-out. For the blob: a pre-FBM length(uv) > maxReach -> return transparent BEFORE the two 3-octave FBM evaluations + the OKLCh round-trip (the W16 perf trim, README:277). MECHANISM: maxReach must be PADDED by the smin inflation (IQ: 'inflate the sphere's radius to match' any outward-expanding op) — bound = bodyRadius + orbitRadius + satRadius + uSmoothK + noiseAmp, so the discard never clips a legitimately-merged limb. Reclaims the wasted FBM cost in the transparent oversize margin (2.56x the fragments at the 1.6x oversize).

HARD CLIP-TO-BOX via SDF intersection (the guaranteed-containment escape hatch). IQ distfunctions: opIntersection = max(d, dBox); opSmoothIntersection = -smin(-d, -dBox, k); sdRoundBox for a rounded boundary. MECHANISM: max(sceneDist, sdRoundBox(uv, halfExtent, r)) GUARANTEES the painted field never exceeds the box no matter how the geometry/mood drifts — a belt-and-suspenders clip the satellites smooth-intersect against the footprint. NOTE FOR OUR BLOB: this is a STRETCH/fallback, not the primary path — the design deliberately lets the orbit excursion overflow the wrapper (the 160% canvas, GooBlob.vue:201-213 contain:layout style with NO paint containment); a hard box-clip would amputate that intended overflow. Use it only if a re-flood regression must be structurally impossible.

ASPECT-CORRECT UV (circular field, no stretch). Codrops normalizes by min(resolution.x, resolution.y) so the field stays circular at any aspect. Our canvas is square (aspect-ratio:1 wrapper + 160% square canvas) so vUv-0.5 is already isotropic — but the velocity squash-and-stretch (sceneDist:172-179) is the ONE place an anisotropic basis is applied; its sa factor must stay volume-preserving (q=(dot/sa, dot*sa), already correct) so a fast flick stretches WITHIN the footprint rather than punching a limb through the edge.

CSS CONTAINMENT SEAM (the on-screen overflow contract). GooBlob.vue uses contain:layout style + content-visibility:auto but DELIBERATELY omits paint containment — paint/overflow:hidden would clip the intended satellite overflow; content-visibility applies paint/layout containment ONLY while offscreen-skipped, preserving on-screen overflow. MECHANISM: containment correctness is a TWO-LAYER property — the shader keeps the FIELD bounded (smin + geometry budget) AND the CSS keeps the LAYOUT bounded (the wrapper footprint) while allowing the designed canvas overflow. The two must agree: a contained field inside an oversized canvas inside a layout-contained wrapper.

2-AXIS MOOD MODEL (valence/arousal) feeding containment-safe parameters. The VAD/Russell circumplex (valence x arousal, dominance optional) is the SOTA affect model: derive the 11 MoodParams from 2 numbers — arousal -> speed/amplitude/smoothK-multiplier, valence -> warmth/squash-sign. MECHANISM FOR CONTAINMENT: when mood is a 1.0-centred MULTIPLIER on the absolute smoothK (W08 F0d) rather than an absolute distance, a high-arousal 'excited' preset widens the neck PROPORTIONALLY and cannot silently re-flood — the single absolute lives in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, mood only scales it. Adding a mood becomes 2 numbers, not 11, and every preset stays in the contained band by construction.

A half-migration re-floods. The ratified path is KEEP W08's POS_SCALE and budget the geometry on top of it.

THE STATIC GATE IS GREEN OVER A FLOOD. proof:blob-smin-normalized greps that the /0.22 + POS_SCALE fudges are GONE (the exact deletion that broke the render) and pure-math-sweeps k in isolation — it certified the regression green. SMIN INFLATION IS INVISIBLE TO A RAW-RADIUS BUDGET. body+orbit+sat sums UNDERSTATE the reach — the smin pulls the surface OUTWARD by ~k beyond the union of the raw circles (IQ: the kernel's inward-at-seam is an outward-of-union expansion of the merged isosurface). READBACK RETURNS 0 AGAINST THIS SUBSTRATE. preserveDrawingBuffer:false clears post-composite and the demand-loop parks — naive readPixels/drawImage returns 0. The gate MUST use a preserveDrawingBuffer:true test context (the W00 harness) or assert on the on-screen screenshot.

HARD BOX-CLIP AMPUTATES THE INTENDED OVERFLOW. max(d, sdRoundBox) guarantees containment but the blob DELIBERATELY overflows the wrapper (160% canvas, no paint containment) for the orbit excursion. A box-clip at the wrapper edge would chop the satellites the design wants to escape. Clip-to-box is a fallback, not the primary containment path.

PREMULTIPLIED-ALPHA EDGE FRINGE AT THE CONTAINMENT BOUNDARY. The blob outputs premultiplied (vec4(rgb*alpha, alpha), :379). At the contained edge, a bright lit/specular term added AFTER the *alpha premultiply double-darkens and fringes the boundary — the lit highlight MUST enter lin in LINEAR before the OETF and before *alpha (already correct at :351-374, must stay correct as the rim re-anchors on the contained body).

MOOD-AS-ABSOLUTE-DISTANCE SILENTLY RE-SCALES EVERY PRESET. If smoothK mood stays an absolute distance (lerp(0.16,0.32)) instead of a 1.0-centred multiplier, a future config retune re-scales every mood band off its hand-set value and a high-arousal preset re-floods. The single absolute must live ONLY in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.smoothK.

FILL-RATE IS QUADRATIC IN OVERSIZE. The 1.6x canvas = 2.56x the fragments, most transparent, early-returning AFTER the two FBM calls already ran. Trimming the oversize and adding the pre-FBM discard is a containment-ADJACENT perf win, but the discard threshold is a correctness hazard — too tight and it clips a wide-orbit satellite; pad it by the full reach + inflation.

notes.facet: Living-membrane surface detail — micro-noise, the breathing perimeter, avoiding the flat-fill dead look (WebGL2 metaball goo-blob; AX W08 un-flood + W15 contained-droplet + W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: IQ domain-warped fBM (fbm(p + 4*fbm(p + 4*fbm(p)))) — distort the sample COORDINATE with a low-frequency fBM of itself before evaluating, producing a flowing marbled membrane instead of an axis-aligned boil. The blob's fbmWarped already does ONE warp layer (the q offsets vec2(0,0)/vec2(5.2,1.3)); IQ's full recipe adds a SECOND layer (r offsets vec2(1.7,9.2)/vec2(8.3,2.8)) for richer organic complexity.

IQ fBM gain/H tuning (G = 2^-H) — the per-octave amplitude falloff (gain/persistence) is the ONE knob that decides liquid-smooth vs rocky-turbulent. Default G=0.5 (H=1) is the rocky/terrain look; a HIGHER gain (~0.42-0.5 with lacunarity ~1.8, i.e. H slightly >1) keeps more low-frequency energy and reads as a smooth liquid membrane. This is the exact mechanism behind W15's '~1.8 lacunarity / ~0.42 gain, liquid not rocky' target.

IQ analytic-derivative gradient noise (noised() → value in .x, exact gradient in .yz from ONE eval) — gradient noise reads as a marbled membrane, not blocky lattice cells, and hands the surface an EXACT field gradient for free (no 4-tap finite-difference). The blob already adopted this; the unexploited move is feeding noised()'s .yz gradient into the surface normal so the membrane's micro-bumps catch the light, not just displace the silhouette.

Rotated/detuned octaves (a fixed ~0.5rad 2x2 rotation OR replacing lacunarity 2.0 with 2.01/1.99 between octaves) — breaks the axis-aligned banding/grid artifacts that make procedural noise read as 'CG'. The blob's FBM_ROT already does this; keep it, and it is the reason the membrane never shows a visible grain grid.

Reuse of the intermediate warp values (q, r) as a SHADING/COLOR input — IQ's signature move: the q/r fBM vectors computed for the domain warp are reused to drive a color/lightness mix (mix on |q| and r.y). Free per-region marbled color variation across the membrane that is spatially COHERENT with the edge deformation (the high-warp zones tint differently), the single biggest 'alive not flat' upgrade after lighting.

Interleaved Gradient Noise dither (Jorge Jimenez, CoD:AW) — fract(52.9829189 * fract(dot(gl_FragCoord.xy, vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715)))) added at exactly 1/255 amplitude (with a -0.5/255 mean-correction) BEFORE the 8-bit quantize. Texture-free, ~3 lines, breaks up the OKLCh flat-fill banding that is the literal 'dead look' on a large smooth gradient body.

Ordered (4x4 Bayer matrix) dithering — a deterministic screen-space threshold pattern (Codrops Jun 2025), fully procedural/texture-free. An alternative to IGN with a more structured/retro grain; for a premium organic surface IGN's hash-noise stipple is the better fit, Bayer is the stylized option.

Blue-noise spatial dithering — the gold-standard banding break (perceptually flat, no low-frequency clumping). Requires a texture lookup or a precomputed tile; for a single-pass texture-free substrate, IGN is the pragmatic 90%-of-the-look substitute.

Multi-frequency summed-sine breathing (Σ aᵢ·sin(fᵢ·t + φᵢ) with incommensurate frequencies + phase offsets) — the canonical fix for the 'mechanical pulse' tell. A single sin() reads as a metronome; 2-3 detuned sines with phase offsets produce a quasi-periodic, never-exactly-repeating breath. Directly addresses W15's 'de-sync the single-sin breath pulse'.

Velocity-coupled warp amplitude (idle calm → motion turbulent) — ramp uNoiseAmp / uWarpAmp with |velocity| so the membrane is a calm living surface at rest and ripples/boils under interaction. Extends the existing FBM rather than replacing it; makes the membrane feel reactive without new geometry.

Fake subsurface / wrap-lighting translucency (Frostbite GDC 2011 'Approximating Translucency', Alan Zucconi port) — back-light = pow(saturate(dot(V, -(L + N·distortion))), p)·scale, lifting luminance where the body is THIN (light leaking through the rim). The blob already implements this (uSssScale/uSssPower); the SOTA note is it must default ON (low floor) for the wet-gel read, and it is what separates 'translucent jelly' from 'opaque sticker'.

Thickness-driven core glow + Fresnel-on-a-fake-3D-normal — the IQ tetrahedron/gradient normal lifts the 2D field to a pseudo-sphere (flat centre, steep rim); the Fresnel rim then lives on a CURVED edge and the core glows by -d thickness. Reads as a dimensional wet bead, not a flat-shaded silhouette. Already shipped in the blob, gated off by default — the keystone of 'avoid the flat-fill dead look'.

Warm-pearl iridescence via an IQ cosine palette in HUE space (a + b·cos(2π(c·t+d)), biased to a warm arc) — a thin-film-like rim sheen that shimmers gold→peach instead of the cold-blue default of generic liquid-glass libs. Keeps the membrane premium and on-brand (warm-cream) rather than garish. Already in the blob; default-off.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for OUR blob, mapped to the waves. W08 (un-flood, predecessor): does NOT touch the membrane — it only restores POS_SCALE on uSmoothK and re-tunes the composed smin band to ~0.03-0.08 effective so containment is even possible. Membrane work is meaningless on a flooded slab; it all lands in W15. W15 (the membrane wave): (1) Turn domain-warp ON by default — flip warpAmp from 0.0 to a calm ~0.3-0.4 floor; the blob's fbmWarped already implements IQ's single-layer warp, so this is a default flip, optionally adding IQ's 2nd warp layer (r) in watercolor-edges.glsl.ts for richer marbling. (2) Tune fBM gain/lacunarity toward the liquid band — set lacunarity ~1.8 and gain ~0.42 (currently hardcoded 2.0/0.5 in the fbm loop) so the membrane reads liquid not rocky; this is the G=2^-H mechanism. (3) De-sync the breath — replace the single sin(uPulsePhase) in metaball.frag.ts with a sum of 2-3 detuned sines with phase offsets (or drive uPulsePhase from a multi-frequency JS accumulator). (4) Raise noiseAmp from 0.025 to a perceptible-but-calm floor PROPORTIONAL to the new smaller body (W15 shrinks bodyRadius, so the absolute wobble must scale with it). (5) Flip lit/iridescence/sssScale/coreGlow to low ON-by-default floors (delete the 'zero regression' gating per the greenfield mandate) — this is the single biggest anti-flat-fill move; the dome luminance variance the gate asserts comes from here. (6) ADD an Interleaved Gradient Noise dither at 1/255 amplitude in metaball.frag.ts — CRITICAL placement: it must be added to the final sRGB color AFTER linearToSrgb() and BEFORE the *alpha premultiply / 8-bit output (the blob currently has NO dither, and a large OKLCh gradient body WILL band on an 8-bit panel — this is the literal flat-fill dead-look on a smooth fill). (7) OPTIONAL premium: reuse the warp q/r vectors as a per-region color/lightness mix so high-warp membrane zones tint subtly (IQ color-reuse) — coherent marbling for free. W16 (integration/README): the research-backed README documents this membrane stack (domain-warp + gain-tuned fBM + IGN dither + de-synced breath + lit/SSS/irid floors) as the canonical identity; the planned→landed sweep flips these from 'Planned' to shipped. The mood model (useBlobMood.ts) already routes arousal → noiseAmp/iridScale, so 'excited' boils the membrane and 'sleepy' calms it — keep that; W15 only re-checks the mood band has headroom above the new lit-default floor (so excited isn't over-saturated).
pitfalls: DITHER COLOR-SPACE TRAP — the IGN dither MUST be added in the OUTPUT (sRGB) space right before 8-bit quantize, AFTER linearToSrgb(), and BEFORE the *alpha premultiply. Adding it in linear space (pre-OETF) gives the wrong magnitude (1/255 of linear != 1/255 of display) and adding it after premultiply fringes the edge. This is adjacent to the blob's existing A5/A2 gamma trap that proof:blob-space-gamma guards.

DOUBLE-DITHER on 6-bit panels — never tune the dither amplitude to a guessed display bit-depth; 1/255 is correct and interferes minimally. Matching to a panel's hardware dither worsens it (frost.kiwi caveat). Keep it fixed at one 8-bit LSB.

NOISE-AMP MUST SCALE WITH THE SHRUNK BODY — W15 shrinks bodyRadius for containment; the membrane displacement (noiseAmp) and frequency (noiseFreq) are ABSOLUTE in UV space, so the same 0.025 reads as a bigger wobble on a smaller body and can overflow the ~70-80% footprint budget. Tie noiseAmp/noiseFreq to the new body scale or the silhouette deviation gate will fight the containment gate.

WARP AMPLITUDE OVER-COOK — IQ's full 3-layer warp at amplitude 4.0 is for fullscreen fractal art, NOT a small bounded droplet; a high warpAmp tears the membrane into spikes that clip the footprint and break the 'calm-but-living' read. Keep warpAmp at a low ~0.3-0.4 floor (the wave's 'calm default'); 2 layers max per the blob-digest two-layer-vs-three perf note (~33% cheaper, same look).

BREATH DE-SYNC CAN DRIFT THE REST POSE — summed incommensurate sines never return to exactly the same radius; under prefers-reduced-motion the useWebGLCanvas substrate paints ONE static frame and parks, so the breath must settle to a DETERMINISTIC rest pose (e.g. all sines at phase 0), not freeze mid-breath at a random amplitude. Same discipline the soft-body seeds carry.

FBM OCTAVE COST — domain warp at N layers multiplies fBM evals (each warp layer is 2 extra fbm calls, each fbm is up to 4 noised() octaves). The blob runs this PER PIXEL in sceneDist AND re-runs sceneDist 4x in surfaceNormal for the tetrahedron gradient. Adding a 2nd warp layer roughly doubles the membrane's per-pixel cost inside an already 5x-sampled field — measure on the DPR<=2 ceiling / half-res quality axis (W16) before shipping it ON by default.

GRAIN VS BANDING ARE DIFFERENT GOALS — a film-grain 'texture' look (visible stipple, higher amplitude) is a STYLE choice; banding-kill dither (1/255, sub-perceptible) is a CORRECTNESS fix. Don't conflate: the membrane wants the invisible 1/255 banding-kill by default; a visible grain tie-in to glass-ui's paper/disco-grain idiom is a separate, louder, opt-in amplitude.

LIT/SSS/IRID DEFAULTS RIDE THE CONTAINED NORMAL — the Fresnel rim and core glow read correctly ONLY when the normal/thickness are anchored on the CONTAINED body (W15 finding 1). If the geometry is still oversize/clipped, the dome highlight saturates flat and the 'lit default' looks worse than the flat fill. Containment (geometry) MUST land before/with the lit-default flip, not after — they are one cohesive re-derivation.

COLD-BLUE DEMO BINDINGS HIDE THE WARM IDENTITY — the three demo stories bind oklch(0.7 0.16 250) (cold blue); shipping the warm-pearl iridescence + warm-cream specular on a cold base reads muddy/garish. Re-point the demo color to the warm house identity (W15) or the membrane/sheen work will be evaluated against the wrong base.

STATIC-MATH GATES WON'T CATCH A FLAT MEMBRANE — the AW blob gate cohort (smin-normalized, gradient-unit-length, etc.) is pure-math and shipped GREEN over a totally broken render. A flat-fill / dead-membrane / banded body only fails a RENDERED-PIXEL gate (luminance variance, silhouette deviation). The membrane work must be validated on actual readback pixels with preserveDrawingBuffer:true, never naive readback against the parked demand-loop (returns 0).

notes.facet: Multi-blob / satellite orchestration — orbit dynamics, merge/split lifecycle, the wobbleScale/orbitSpeedScale mood knobs (W08 un-flood + W15 contained-droplet + W16 integration)
sotaTechniques: IQ 2024 NORMALIZED smin (k-as-distance-band) — premultiply k so the parameter maps DIRECTLY to the blend-thickness in distance units (quadratic: k*=4.0; circular: k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5))). This is the canonical un-flood lever: once k is a true distance, the composed upload (config.smoothK x mood-multiplier x POS_SCALE) is a single budget you can reason about, not a magic number. Our sdf-body.glsl.ts ALREADY ships this exact normalization — W08's job is to re-derive the three COUPLED inputs against it, not touch the shader.

Polynomial/circular smin over EXPONENTIAL smin — IQ's rigidity property: polynomial/circular smin returns EXACTLY min(a,b) outside the k-band (the CD/Clamped-Difference kernel family: g(-1)=g'(-1)=0), so the field is undistorted away from the seam. Exponential smin (the Codrops -log(sum(exp(-k*d))) form) distorts the SDF EVERYWHERE and hurts locality — it is the wrong tool for a contained droplet and a contributing flood class. Keep the quadratic/circular dispatch; do NOT adopt the exp form.

smin multiplicity over-merge correction (smish.dev) — the named root-cause of W08's flood at the math level: smin(a,a) != a, so where MANY fields coincide (body + N satellites + 15 trail spheres all overlapping at center) the smooth-min returns progressively MORE negative than any single field, bulging the interior to alpha=1. Mitigations: (1) keep k small relative to shape size, (2) cap simultaneous overlaps, (3) stagger satellite phases so all N never coincide at the core at once (our MERGE_STAGGER_MS already does this — it is also an over-merge guard, not just an aesthetic one).

smin material/color blend factor (IQ vec2 return) — the smooth-min can return BOTH the blended distance AND a blend weight m (vec2 smin(a,b,k){ h=1-min(|a-b|/(4k),1); w=h*h; ... return vec2(d, m); }). m interpolates material color at the seam. This is the SOTA path to give satellites a faintly distinct tint that melts into the body at the meniscus — a per-source palette-stop read at the merge band, instead of one flat field color. Directly enables the W11.b multi-stop palette to paint PER-SATELLITE rather than via the current screen-space color-noise hack.

Pointer-trail metaball chain (Codrops/Three.js droplet pattern) — the modern interactive-blob idiom: a fixed-length history buffer (trailLength=15) of pointer positions, each a smin-merged sphere with radius tapering along the tail (r -= baseR*i/N), uploaded as a compile-time-sized uniform array with a dynamic break. Our metaball.frag.ts TRAIL_N=15 + uTrailCount loop is a VERBATIM match of the current SOTA — confirms the W10 pseudopod is on the canonical path; W15 only needs to re-scale its radii against the smaller contained body.

Superposed-sinusoid / pseudo-Lissajous orbit (our orbitPos) — organic non-repeating orbits from an elliptical base (baseRadiusX != baseRadiusY for eccentricity) + two summed wobble sinusoids at incommensurate frequencies + independent X/Y perturbation sines with random phase. This is the standard procedural-orbit recipe (cheaper than physics, deterministic, seedable). orbitSpeedScale multiplies the angular sweep; wobbleScale multiplies the radial wobble amplitude — both are the mood->motion coupling knobs.

Circumplex (Russell valence-arousal) affect model — the academically-standard 2-axis emotion space (valence=pleasantness, arousal=activation). Our useBlobMood derives ALL MoodParams from one {valence,arousal} point via paramsFor() — arousal drives motion energy (orbitSpeedScale, wobbleScale, pulseFreq, smoothK), valence warms palette + pointer lean. This is exactly how SOTA affective-character systems map a continuous mood point onto expressive parameters; the five named moods as samples of one surface is the correct, non-overfit framing.

Volume-preserving squash-and-stretch (Thomas/Johnston 1st principle) — when stretched along motion axis by sa=1+|v|*k, the PERPENDICULAR axis MUST scale by EXACTLY 1/sa (not 1-amt, which loses area and shrinks the blob at speed). Our sceneDist() body-space anisotropic basis q=(dot/sa, dot*sa) is the textbook volume-preserving deformation — confirmed correct against the canonical principle.

FBM 1/f standard tuning (lacunarity 2.0, gain/persistence 0.5) + 'liquid not rocky' deviation — the industry baseline is lacunarity=2.0, gain=0.5. For a LIQUID membrane (vs rocky terrain) the W15 target lowers lacunarity toward ~1.8 and persistence toward ~0.42 so higher octaves contribute less high-frequency crinkle — a smoother, more fluid silhouette. Domain-warping the FBM (warpAmp) before sampling is the IQ marbling technique for an organic non-uniform edge.

WebGPU compute-marching metaballs (Nikoloff / Three.js TSL roadmap) — the next-substrate axis: run the metaball field + isosurface extraction in a GPUComputePipeline (marching squares/cubes), animate blobs that merge/split with selectable materials, instanced rendering for many sources. Relevant as the FORWARD path beyond the WebGL2 single-pass fragment evaluation — but NOT needed for our 2D contained droplet (a fragment-evaluated 2D field at canvas resolution is cheaper than a compute pipeline for a ~7rem accent). Document it as the scale-up door, not a near-term need.

Demand-scheduled rAF (event-driven over perpetual) — the SOTA perf pattern for idle organic UI: render only when something changes. The satellite phase-timer scheduler already knows when the next merge/orbit transition is due, so the loop can PARK at rest and wake() on the next scheduled phase + on pointer/mood activity. This is W16's quiescence signal — the single biggest battery lever after offscreen-park for an ambient accent blob.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD per wave. Target effective seam-pull ~0.03-0.08 (the pre-AW working 0.034). The multiplicity over-merge (smish.dev) is WHY the flood is so total — body + 3 satellites + up to 15 trail spheres all coincide near center; MERGE_STAGGER_MS is already a partial guard. W15 (contained droplet): solve bodyRadius+orbitRadius+satelliteRadius+smin-band as ONE footprint budget so the merged field at widest orbit fits ~70-80% of the wrapper (currently ~1.34x = over-budget). Keep W08's POS_SCALE regime (ratified). Lower FBM lacunarity->~1.8 / persistence->~0.42 for the liquid-not-rocky membrane; de-sync the single-sin breath. The orbitSpeedScale/wobbleScale knobs are correctly wired through orbitPos — just re-balance amplitudes against the smaller body so excited-arousal stays a contained droplet. CONSIDER the IQ vec2 material-smin so the W11.b palette stops paint per-satellite at the seam (a genuine SOTA upgrade over the current screen-space color-noise distribution). W16 (integration): the pointer-trail chain already matches the Codrops SOTA verbatim — no rework, only radius re-scale. Add the demand-scheduled quiescence (wake from the satellite phase scheduler) — the satellite system's existing phase timers are exactly the wake-source SOTA prescribes. The circumplex mood model is already the academically-correct framing; document it as such in the research-backed README.
pitfalls: EXPONENTIAL smin is a trap, not an upgrade. The Codrops droplet uses -log(exp(-k*a)+exp(-k*b))/k — elegant for a fully-fused water droplet but it distorts the SDF GLOBALLY (never returns exactly a or b) and destroys locality. Adopting it for a CONTAINED droplet would re-introduce a flood class and break the fwidth-AA edge + the surfaceNormal gradient (which assume a near-unit-gradient field). Stay on the polynomial/circular CD-kernel dispatch.

smin is NOT associative AND smin(a,a)!=a. Adding more satellites or more trail spheres MULTIPLIES the over-merge near the core (the smish.dev multiplicity bulge) — every coincident source pulls the interior more negative. Increasing satelliteCount without re-checking the footprint budget silently re-floods. The phase-stagger (MERGE_STAGGER_MS) is load-bearing as an over-merge guard, not just aesthetic — do not remove it for 'snappier' merges.

The composed uSmoothK is a PRODUCT of three terms (config x mood-multiplier x POS_SCALE) then x4 in-shader — a 5x change in any one term cascades. The original regression was exactly this: config dropped 0.22->0.12 but the mood lerp stayed 0.16-0.32 un-rescaled -> composed 0.216 -> effective 0.864. Re-solve all three TOGETHER as a budget; never nudge one. Reframing mood smoothK as a 1.0-centred multiplier (W08) is the structural fix that prevents recurrence.

POS_SCALE asymmetry is the silent second half of the flood. Every length-like uniform (bodyRadius, satRadius, pointer, velocity, noiseAmp) carries *POS_SCALE except uSmoothK at HEAD. A smin band that does NOT ride the same coordinate compression is a different unit than the geometry it merges — coherent only by restoring the multiply. Do not 'fix' this by removing POS_SCALE from the OTHER uniforms mid-wave (that is the W15-atomic-or-not decision; a partial migration re-floods across the wave seam).

FBM 'liquid' tuning is a taste cliff. Pushing lacunarity below ~1.7 or persistence below ~0.4 flattens the membrane into a featureless wobble (dead, not living); pushing them toward the 2.0/0.5 rocky default crinkles it into a spiky non-droplet. The ~1.8/~0.42 band is narrow — tune against the LIVE render, not a number target. Also tie noiseAmp to the NEW (smaller) body scale or the wobble reads disproportionate.

Volume-preservation is exact-1/sa or it's wrong. A '1-amt' squash (the naive form) loses area so the blob SHRINKS at speed — visibly deflating on a fast flick. The perp axis MUST be 1/sa. Our basis is correct; any 'simplification' to a linear squash breaks the principle.

The mood circumplex must not over-saturate the now-default-lit body. W15 flips lit/iridescence/SSS ON by default; the mood iridScale/arousal multipliers were tuned against a FLAT default. An 'excited' preset that was tasteful on a flat fill can blow out the highlight on a lit dome — re-check the mood band headroom after the lit-default flip (W15 explicitly calls this out).

WebGPU compute-marching is over-engineering for this surface. A ~7rem ambient 2D accent does NOT need a GPUComputePipeline + isosurface extraction — the fragment-evaluated 2D field is cheaper and simpler. Reaching for the compute substrate here is substrate-without-consumer; document it as the scale-up door only.

Quiescence false-park risk. The demand-scheduled park must NOT freeze a blob that SHOULD animate (mid-merge, active pointer, mood transition, non-zero click pulse). The wake predicate has to OR every active source; missing one (e.g. a satellite mid-emerge) produces a frozen-then-jerk artefact worse than the perpetual loop.

notes.facet: Accessibility of an animated organic shape — role/aria, decorative vs meaningful, motion sensitivity (as it applies to glass-ui's WebGL2 goo-blob, AX waves W08/W15/W16)
sotaTechniques: DECORATIVE-NON-TEXT classification (WCAG 1.1.1 + the WAI alt-decision-tree). A canvas with NO semantic role and an empty/absent accessible name is correctly ignored by AT. The mechanism: aria-hidden="true" on the <canvas> removes it from the accessibility tree so SRs never announce it. This is the SOTA-correct classification for the blob: it conveys NO information, so it is decorative-by-definition, not 'meaningful-but-unlabeled'. The blob already does this exactly right (GooBlob.vue line 161: aria-hidden="true" on the canvas).

WCAG 2.2.2 Pause-Stop-Hide (Level A) — the BINDING gate for an ambient blob. Exact normative thresholds: a pause/stop/hide control is required for content that (1) starts automatically, (2) lasts MORE THAN 5 seconds, AND (3) is presented in parallel with other content — unless the motion is essential. Mechanism: a user-reachable control that calls pause()/resume() on the render loop. This is a SEPARATE obligation from prefers-reduced-motion and must be available to ALL users (not gated behind PRM). The blob's auto-running metaball is the textbook 2.2.2 case: continuous, auto-start, >5s, non-essential, in-parallel.

WCAG 2.3.3 Animation-from-Interactions (Level AAA) — governs the pointer-follow / click-squish / pseudopod (W10 interaction). Exact wording: 'Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential.' The blob's lean-toward-cursor, velocity squash-and-stretch, and click bounce are ALL interaction-triggered non-essential motion — they fall under 2.3.3, a DIFFERENT criterion from 2.2.2 (which covers auto-started motion). Sufficient technique: collapse interaction motion to instant/no-op when prefers-reduced-motion:reduce. The blob conveys nothing by leaning, so it is never 'essential' — always disable-able.

prefers-reduced-motion = REDUCE, not REMOVE (the 2025-2026 refinement). The media keyword is `reduce` (not `none`); current guidance is to reduce/replace non-essential motion, NOT strip it. Safe-to-keep alternatives: opacity fades (<200ms), color transitions, a static composed pose. The SOTA pattern for an organic shape under reduce is a single deliberate static frame (a 'poster') rather than a hard blank — preserving the brand read while killing the vestibular trigger (panning/scaling large organic masses are named vestibular triggers).

Live-monitored PRM via matchMedia change listener (the substrate-owns-it pattern). A CSS @media reset cannot reach a WebGL rAF loop, so the substrate must own a JS matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') with a live `change` listener that freezes/unfreezes the loop without remount. glass-ui's useWebGLCanvas already implements this (per README/CLAUDE.md). SOTA-correct: ONE freeze gate, live-monitored, inherited by every surface on the substrate — interaction must hook the SAME gate, never a parallel motion path.

inert + role/name on a real button (the canonical clickable-decorative pattern). The hard trap: aria-hidden="true" MUST NOT wrap a focusable element (axe `aria-hidden-focus` / WCAG 4.1.2) — a keyboard user tabs into a node the SR ignores. SOTA: if the blob is genuinely interactive, the FOCUSABLE/named control is a real <button>/role="button" with an accessible name AROUND or BESIDE the canvas; the canvas stays aria-hidden and the button carries the name + keyboard activation (Enter/Space). The modern `inert` attribute (now all-major-browser) is the single-declaration way to neutralize a decorative subtree (hides from AT + blocks focus + blocks pointer) — cleaner than the old aria-hidden+tabindex=-1+pointer-events triple.

Anthropomorphic/emotion expression is NOT meaningful content unless it carries information (the emoji-accessibility analogue). The blob's mood (valence/arousal circumplex: idle/happy/curious/sleepy/excited) is AMBIENT affect, not conveyed information — like a decorative emoji that duplicates surrounding text, it needs NO text alternative and NO aria-live announcement. SOTA rule: only expose state via role="img"+aria-label (or aria-live) when the mood ENCODES information the user must act on (e.g. a status indicator). A purely expressive mascot stays decorative. (Contrast StatusDot in this same library, which emits role="img" ONLY when the consumer binds aria-label — the correct conditional pattern.)

Composed reduced-motion REST POSE (the 'poster frame', AW/AX planned). Instead of freezing on whatever random frame the rAF lands, paint ONE deliberately-designed static frame under PRM: peak roundness, satellites at a designed arrangement, the contained lit droplet at its most legible. This is the SOTA 'meaningful still' that satisfies reduce while preserving the brand mark. W15's contained-droplet geometry is the precondition (you can only pose a contained silhouette, not a flooded slab).

Demand-gated quiescence park (perf-as-accessibility). Beyond PRM, the SOTA substrate parks the rAF when nothing is changing (mood settled + pointer at rest + trail collapsed + no satellite mid-merge) and on offscreen (IntersectionObserver + content-visibility) / tab-hidden (document.hidden). This reduces sustained motion energy and battery/thermal load — an accessibility and sustainability win, and W16's named quiescence-signal work.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD per wave. W08 (un-flood smin): accessibility-neutral GEOMETRICALLY but a PRECONDITION — a flooded full-canvas slab cannot carry a 'composed rest pose' (there is no contained silhouette to pose), so un-flooding is what makes the PRM poster-frame achievable. Keep the aria-hidden canvas untouched. W15 (contained lit droplet + default-on lit/irid/SSS): two a11y obligations land here. (1) The composed reduced-motion REST POSE becomes designable — spec it as a named static frame (peak-round contained droplet, designed satellite arrangement), painted as the single PRM frame, replacing the 'random freeze'. (2) Turning lit/iridescence/SSS ON by default RAISES the contrast/legibility bar — W15 already calls for a 'min-contrast rim' so the first var(--primary) blob does not wash out in dark mode; frame that as a 1.4.11 non-text-contrast-adjacent concern (the rim is the silhouette read). The default-on sheen must not introduce a high-frequency shimmer that itself becomes a motion trigger — keep iridescence scroll slow (the README's 'subtle not maximal rainbow'). W16 (integration/interaction/perf/README): the DENSEST a11y wave. (a) RESTORE the pause()/resume() seam — today GooBlob.vue discards the renderer handle so blob.value.pause() is undefined: this is a LIVE WCAG 2.2.2 FAILURE (the documented DockBackgroundToggle integration is a runtime no-op). Capture `const { pause, resume } = useMetaballRenderer(...)` + re-expose, OR collapse to a v-model:paused prop the component owns. This is the single highest-priority a11y fix in the blob band. (b) The W10 interaction (pointer-lean/squish/pseudopod) is governed by WCAG 2.3.3 — verify ALL of it collapses to no-op under the SAME live-PRM gate the substrate owns (no parallel motion path); the README already asserts this but W16 should add the gate-coverage check. (c) The clickable mascot: if a consumer makes the blob a button (the README's 'wrap in a real <button>' note), the canvas stays aria-hidden and the <button> carries role+name+keyboard — DO NOT put aria-label on the canvas (it would need role=\"img\" and would wrongly promote decorative→meaningful). (d) The quiescence/demand-park signal is the sustained-motion reducer. For the README: the Accessibility section is already strong and research-backed — the W16 sweep should (1) flip the 'Planned (AW)' pause-seam language to 'shipped' once restored, (2) keep the decorative-canvas + 2.2.2 + 2.3.3 + PRM-live-monitor four-point structure, (3) add the composed-rest-pose as shipped (not planned) once W15 lands, (4) explicitly state mood is decorative-affect (no text alternative / no aria-live) so a consumer does not wrongly bolt an announcer on it. MOOD MODEL a11y note: the valence-arousal model is sound as pure expression; if a consumer ever maps mood to MEANING (e.g. error=sad), THAT consumer owns the text alternative on a real labeled element, not the blob.
pitfalls: LIVE WCAG 2.2.2 FAILURE TODAY: GooBlob.vue discards the renderer return, so the exposed pause()/resume() seam the DockBackgroundToggle docs wire to is undefined at the call site — the pause control is a runtime no-op. typecheck passes (the methods exist on the discarded return type) so vue-tsc misses it. This is the #1 fix (W16 slice-13 F0).

Do NOT add aria-label to the <canvas>. An aria-label on a bare canvas/span without role is ignored by many SRs (treated invalid), and adding role="img"+aria-label would WRONGLY promote the decorative blob to meaningful content requiring a maintained text alternative. The blob conveys nothing — keep aria-hidden="true" and name a real button if it becomes interactive.

aria-hidden + focusable conflict (WCAG 4.1.2 / axe aria-hidden-focus): if a consumer makes the blob clickable by adding tabindex to the aria-hidden wrapper, keyboard users tab into a SR-invisible control. The wrapper currently has @click but no tabindex (mouse-only — itself an a11y gap for keyboard users wanting the click-squish). The fix is a real <button> with name+Enter/Space, NOT tabindex on the hidden subtree.

PRM = reduce, not eliminate: a hard blank-on-reduce is a worse UX than a composed static poster. But the inverse pitfall is real too — leaving a 'reduced but still panning/scaling large organic mass' is itself a vestibular trigger. The safe target is a SINGLE static frame (no transform animation on the large blob body), optionally with a sub-200ms opacity fade-in, nothing more.

Default-on sheen as a NEW motion trigger: W15 turns iridescence/SSS on by default. A fast iridescent shimmer or high-frequency specular crawl is itself non-essential motion (2.2.2/2.3.3) and a potential photosensitive/vestibular irritant. Keep the iridSpeed slow and ensure the sheen FREEZES under PRM with everything else (it must ride the same uTime that the substrate stops, not a separate animation).

Two motion gates drifting apart: the auto-motion (2.2.2, the pause control) and the interaction-motion (2.3.3, the PRM no-op) are DIFFERENT criteria. A common error is wiring PRM to freeze the loop but leaving the click-squish impulse running on a separate path, or wiring the pause button but not the PRM freeze. Both must hook the substrate's single live gate; W16 should assert gate-coverage for the click impulse specifically (the impulse 'rides the renderer's single rAF' per GooBlob.vue, so under PRM-freeze it is a no-op — verify this holds after the pause-seam restore).

Fill-rate-as-accessibility regression: an idle on-screen blob burning full fps forever (no quiescence gate, W16 slice-13 F1: shouldContinue(){return !paused} defeats demand-park) is a sustained-CPU/GPU + battery + thermal cost that disproportionately harms low-end devices and is a sustainability/a11y concern, not just perf. The quiescence signal is the fix.

README planned-vs-shipped drift: the Accessibility + Interaction sections say 'Planned (AW)' for the pause seam and rest pose; once W16/W15 land these, the README must flip to shipped or it misleads consumers into thinking the WCAG-2.2.2 wiring is aspirational (the README sweep is explicitly in W16 scope, slice-13 F5 / slice-11 F2).

notes.facet: Performance budget for a ubiquitous WebGL2 metaball goo-blob — the per-frame cost ceiling, the smin distance regime that un-floods fill-rate, the tier cascade (when to drop to a static SVG/WatercolorDot), and the multi-instance WebGL-context budget. Feeds AX waves W08 (smin un-flood), W15 (contained lit droplet), W16 (integration + quality axis + multi-instance + README).
sotaTechniques: IQ-NORMALIZED QUADRATIC SMIN (k IS the band) — `k*=4.0; h=max(k-|a-b|,0)/k; min(a,b)-h*h*k*0.25`. After IQ's normalization the parameter k equals EXACTLY the max inflation/thickening of the blended shapes in distance units, so the uniform value is the neck-width you reason about directly (no hidden normalizer). Cheapest variant, never overestimates distance, gradient stays <=1 — keeping the SDF valid so the fwidth-AA and the 4-tap normal behave.

CIRCULAR SMIN (rounder menisci) — `k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5)); h=max(k-|a-b|,0)/k; min(a,b)-k*0.5*(1+h-sqrt(1-h*(h-2)))`. One sqrt (free on modern GPUs), perfect-circular blend profile. This is exactly the blob's `merge:'circular'` branch; the constant differs from quadratic's `*4.0` and MUST ride the same POS_SCALE compression.

FILL-RATE IS THE ONLY COST, QUADRATIC IN DPR — a fragment-bound full-screen quad pays per backing-store pixel, so cost scales with (cssW*cssH*dpr^2). The DPR<=2 clamp (AV_DPR_MAX) is the single biggest VRAM/fill lever: 3x retina is ~2.25x the fill of 2x for no perceptible gain on a soft organic surface.

BOUNDING / EARLY-DISCARD BEFORE EXPENSIVE ALU — a cheap analytic-circle pre-test (max body+orbit+sat reach) lets fragments outside the blob's possible extent `discard`/return transparent BEFORE the 3-octave FBM (run twice) + OKLCh round-trip + 4-tap normal. Scheduling the discard early skips the costly per-pixel work on the transparent border the oversize 160% canvas is mostly made of.

GATE THE 4-TAP TETRAHEDRON NORMAL BEHIND THE LIT/IRID PATH — `surfaceNormal()` calls `sceneDist()` FOUR extra times (each runs the full smin loop + FBM), so it ~5x's the field cost per pixel. It is only consumed by the lit/iridescence/SSS terms; a flat-fill blob should never pay it. Branch-coherent (all pixels take the same path when uLit is uniform-constant), so no warp divergence penalty.

HALF-RESOLUTION RENDER + BILINEAR UPSAMPLE (the quality:'half' axis) — render the metaball pass to a half-size FBO and bilinear-upsample to the canvas for ~4x fragment savings. The blob is the IDEAL candidate: the soft FBM edge + fwidth-AA hide the interpolation; box-down then bilinear-up avoids the half-pixel shift. This is the never-shipped `quality:'full'|'half'` axis W16 wires.

DEMAND-DRIVEN rAF PARK (quiescence gate) — the loop should park when the creature is genuinely at rest (mood settled + pointer rest + trail collapsed + no satellite mid-merge), woken by the satellite scheduler — not `shouldContinue(){return !paused}` which burns full fps forever on an idle onscreen blob. Pairs with the substrate's existing offscreen/tab-hidden/PRM park.

OFFSCREEN/HIDDEN PARK (already shipped, SOTA-correct) — IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 200px warm band) + content-visibility:auto (`contentvisibilityautostatechange`) + document.hidden ORed onto the rAF gate via the compositor thread, so an offscreen/backgrounded blob attaches ZERO frames. This is the canonical battery/jank discipline; keep it.

TIER CASCADE — WebGL2 SDF (interactive hero) -> WatercolorDot (cheap CSS/SVG dot, the existing sibling) -> static poster frame. The blob and WatercolorDot are a DELIBERATE pair: route static/ambient instances to WatercolorDot, reserve the per-pixel-shaded GooBlob for the ONE interactive hero. SVG goo (feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix) is the classic cheap metaball but is itself a fill-rate/filter cost at size and offers no per-pixel lighting — it is a fallback tier, not a peer.

MULTI-INSTANCE WEBGL-CONTEXT BUDGET — browsers hard-cap ~16 live WebGL contexts per tab (OffscreenCanvas only 4); the oldest is force-lost past the cap (the prior context-cap incident). N independent GooBlobs = N contexts. SOTA fix: a single shared scissored context drawing all instances, OR strict tiering (one GooBlob context + WatercolorDot for the rest). Always release via WEBGL_lose_context on teardown.

BREATHING/IDLE CADENCE + 2-4 CORE MOODS (design-grounded budget) — game/Rive idle references put a relaxed breathing cycle at ~15-25 breaths/min (~0.25-0.4 Hz) and recommend 2-4 core states (idle/success/error/celebration) layered on a state machine. This corroborates the blob's pulseFreq:0.3 default and the 5-mood cross-fade; a designed REST POSE (peak roundness + satellites at a composed arrangement) is the correct PRM/pause static frame, not a random freeze.
notes.applicability: W08 (smin un-flood — the blocker): the IQ article is the authoritative confirmation that after `k*=4.0` the uniform k IS the blend band in UV distance units. The live bug is that the W9.a normalization changed k's semantic regime but left the config default (0.12), the mood lerp, and the MISSING POS_SCALE multiply un-reconciled — composed uSmoothK~=0.21 -> effective k~=0.84 in a 1.0-wide UV (~6x the working band), so the smin floods the field negative across the whole canvas (84% coverage) into a clipped color slab. The fix is purely a SCALE re-derivation, NOT a shader rewrite (the lit rim + iridescence render correctly on the visible edge). Concrete path: (a) restore `*POS_SCALE` on the uSmoothK upload — the smin band is a length and must ride the same 0.625 compression as uBodyRadius/satRadius/uPointer/noiseAmp (verified asymmetric at useMetaballRenderer.ts:438-439); (b) re-tune the composed band to ~0.03-0.08 effective for a tight wet meniscus; (c) keep mood smoothK as a 1.0-centred MULTIPLIER (already done at :439). The circular branch constant `1/(1-sqrt(0.5))` differs from quadratic's `*4.0`, so re-tuning must hold for BOTH merge variants under the same POS_SCALE. W15 (contained lit droplet): solve bodyRadius+orbitRadius+satelliteRadius+smin-band so the whole merged field fits ~70-80% of the wrapper, express every length in wrapper-normalized units (the POS_SCALE-disposition decision: either keep W08's regime or bake 0.625 into all constants ATOMICALLY with proof:blob-render as the lock — never a partial re-flood). The contained silhouette is the keystone — it resurfaces the lit/iridescence/SSS that already ships but paints nothing because thickness saturates flat on the oversize body. The breathing reference grounds the lit warm-cream droplet as the DEFAULT identity (delete the off-by-default 'zero regression' flag-gating per greenfield). W16 (integration + perf + README): (1) the multi-instance context cap (~16/tab) is the hard ceiling — route ambient blobs to WatercolorDot, reserve GooBlob for the interactive hero, or share one scissored context; (2) wire the quality:'half' half-res-FBO axis for ~4x fragment savings on weak GPUs; (3) the oversize-canvas trim = pre-FBM analytic-bounding discard + gate the 4-tap surfaceNormal behind uLit; (4) a genuine quiescence signal feeding shouldContinue so the idle onscreen blob throttles. The README 'Performance notes' section already gestures at most of these as '(Planned — AW)'; this research moves them from planned to research-backed, and the SVG-breakdown thresholds (~3-5k SVG elements) justify the tier framing in prose.
pitfalls: RE-FLOODING ACROSS THE WAVE BOUNDARY — if W15 deletes POS_SCALE but leaves the smin band W08 just compressed, the SDF re-floods. The POS_SCALE excision (if done at all) MUST be one atomic re-derivation of the ENTIRE length cohort (body/sat/orbit/smin/noise) in a single wave with proof:blob-render locking it — never a partial migration. This is the §4-note-13 contradiction and the no-1-shrug precept.

k MUST RIDE BOTH MERGE CONSTANTS — quadratic uses `k*=4.0`, circular uses `k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5))~=3.41`. The re-tuned composed band has to land in the working window for BOTH, since uMerge switches the in-shader normalizer; tuning only against quadratic mis-scales the circular menisci.

DPR^2 FILL TRAP — cost is quadratic in devicePixelRatio. Removing/raising the AV_DPR_MAX=2 clamp on a 3x display ~2.25x's the fragment work for no visible gain. The clamp is load-bearing; a consumer over-authoring size or a missing clamp is the silent perf regression.

THE 4-TAP NORMAL IS ~5x THE FIELD COST — surfaceNormal() evaluates sceneDist() (full smin loop + 3-octave FBM) four extra times. Leaving it un-gated when uLit=0 pays a flat-fill blob the full lit cost. Gate it behind the lit path; ensure uLit is effectively uniform-constant per draw so the branch stays warp-coherent (no divergence penalty).

CONTEXT-CAP EXHAUSTION IS A HARD WALL, NOT A SLOWDOWN — past ~16 contexts/tab the browser force-loses the OLDEST context (a different live blob silently goes blank), and SPA route churn that doesn't WEBGL_lose_context on teardown leaks toward the cap. A grid of independent GooBlobs is the failure mode; this is why ambient instances MUST route to WatercolorDot or share one context.

HALF-RES UPSAMPLE NEEDS CORRECT PIXEL ALIGNMENT — box-down then bilinear-up shifts the image half a pixel if the grids aren't aligned; the soft FBM edge hides MOST artifacts but a mis-aligned upsample crawls on the rim. Use the aligned down/up convention (Bart Wronski) and only enable on the quality:'half' tier.

PAUSE/RESUME SEAM IS A RUNTIME NO-OP TODAY — GooBlob.vue discards the renderer handle, so blob.value.pause() is undefined at every call site (the documented DockBackgroundToggle integration silently does nothing; typecheck passes because the methods exist on the discarded return type). W16 must capture `const {pause,resume}=useMetaballRenderer(...)` and re-expose, OR collapse to a declarative v-model:paused — this is the blocker hiding behind a green typecheck.

notes.facet: Modern goo/blob design systems — organic shapes (Stripe/Linear/Apple), restraint, the arresting-not-distracting balance, and the SOTA WebGL2 metaball technique that backs glass-ui's W08 un-flood / W15 contained-lit-droplet / W16 integration waves
sotaTechniques: IQ NORMALIZED quadratic smin (the un-flood math, W08 root). `k *= 4.0` rescales the polynomial smin so `k` is a TRUE blend band in DISTANCE units (the 4.0 = 1/g(0), g(0)=1/4 the kernel value at the origin = max thickening when shapes are equidistant). MECHANISM CONFIRMED against IQ's 2024 rewrite — the form glass-ui ships in sdf-body.glsl.ts is verbatim correct. The flood is NOT the shader; it is the COUPLED INPUT: an uploaded k that is large RELATIVE TO THE BODY RADIUS subtracts a near-body-radius offset from `min(a,b)` and pushes the whole composite SDF negative (inside) → alpha=1 everywhere. The fix is a SCALE re-derivation (k must be a small fraction of bodyRadius), exactly as W08 specs.

IQ circular smin variant (the wetter meniscus, already wired as `merge:'circular'`). `k *= 1.0/(1.0-sqrt(0.5))` normalizes the circular CD kernel to the SAME blend-band units as quadratic, so swapping merge mode does NOT re-scale k. Confirmed verbatim. Gives a true quarter-circle fillet at the seam — the rounder/wetter premium-droplet read; a candidate W15 default once the field is contained.

Smin stays a CONSERVATIVE SDF (|∇f| ≤ 1) REGARDLESS of k (IQ). This is the load-bearing proof that the W08 flood is a TUNING bug, not a structural one: the field is always a valid bounded SDF, so a correctly-scaled k yields a contained droplet with no architecture change. It also validates the W16 perf trim (a pre-FBM `length(uv) > maxReach → discard` bounding cull is SAFE because the gradient is ≤1, so distance cannot be underestimated past the cull radius).

Codrops 2025 droplet pattern — the COORDINATE-SCALE lesson (the W08/W15 keystone). The canonical premium-metaball reference uses `k = 7.0` BUT in a tiny coordinate space (`baseRadius = 8e-3`), i.e. k is ~875× the sphere radius in raw units yet contained because the WHOLE scene is sub-unit. The takeaway for glass-ui: k is meaningless in isolation — it must be re-derived AS A RATIO against the body/satellite radii in OUR UV space (half-extent 0.5). This is precisely why W08 reframes mood-smoothK as a 1.0-centred MULTIPLIER and solves the band as one budget against bodyRadius.

Codrops pointer-trail pseudopod (the W15 interaction-legibility model, already wired in metaball.frag.ts uTrail). 15 historical pointer positions, each spawning a sphere with TAPERING radius (`radius - baseRadius*i`, newest=largest at the cursor, oldest=smallest), all smin-merged → a stretchy elastic limb that snaps back. glass-ui's TRAIL_N=15 + `r *= 1 - i/N` taper is the SAME mechanism. The W15 insight is correct: the trail is already built and sound; it is INVISIBLE only because the oversized field has no contained silhouette to deform — containment resurfaces it.

SDF-gradient surface normal (the lit dome, W15 default-ON). The gradient of the distance function IS the surface normal (IQ distgradfunctions2d / Codrops both). glass-ui derives it via the 4-tap tetrahedron of the COMPOSITE sceneDist (correct — the normal must ride the field the alpha is cut from, not a clean circle) and lifts a pseudo-3D z via a unit half-sphere profile (`z = sqrt(1-(1-interior)^2)`) so the highlight rolls across a believable sphere. This is the SOTA-correct fake-3D-from-2D-SDF approach; W15 re-anchors it on the CONTAINED body so the Fresnel rim lives on a curved edge inside the footprint.

Fast/fake subsurface scattering — wrapped lighting + Fresnel back-light (Alan Zucconi / John Austin; the W15 translucent-gel read). Fake SSS = a Fresnel-masked back-light: where the light faces the camera THROUGH a thin rim, light travels a shorter path so the edge glows (`pow(saturate(dot(V, -(L + N*distortion))), power)`). glass-ui's sceneDist-thickness ramp (`-d/bodyR`) feeding a `coreGlow` (thick=bright core) + an SSS back-light (`1-thickness` weighted) is the textbook fast-SSS. This is the single highest-value term for making the blob read as a translucent GEL not a flat sticker — W15 turns it ON at a low floor.

Glass tone-crush, NOT bloom (Codrops `pow(color, vec3(7.0))`; intensity≈2.3). The premium glass read comes from a TONE COMPRESSION that suppresses darks and accentuates highlights — a cheap per-pixel ALU curve, no second pass, no bloom. glass-ui's analog is the warm-cream specular tint (L≈0.97, C≈0.03, hue≈85° routed through the SAME OKLCh matrices, NOT hardcoded white — pure white reads cheap-CG) added in LINEAR before the OETF. The named-white-is-cheap rule is the load-bearing detail for the warm-cream fit.

OKLCh perceptual color perturbation + hue-preserving gamut clamp (Ottosson; the in-family color identity). Perturbing L/C/h in OKLCh (vs raw sRGB/HSV) is why the blob stays in-family and never bands or goes muddy — the perceptually-uniform space the whole AV.W2 shared chunk speaks. The hue-preserving chroma-bisection clamp keeps an out-of-gamut perturbation in-hue. This is the correct, already-shipped color architecture; W15 leverages it for the warm-token default palette (deriveBlobPalette → 2-4 in-family stops).

Domain-warped FBM membrane with 'liquid-not-rocky' constants (IQ warp/fbm; the W15 living edge). The organic silhouette = an analytic-gradient gradient-noise FBM displacing the SDF edge, wrapped in ONE domain-warp pass (`fbm(p + W*fbm(p))`). The liquid-vs-rocky character is in the FBM constants: lacunarity ~1.8 / persistence ~0.42 reads as a marbled liquid membrane; the default ~2.0/0.5 reads rockier. W15 tunes toward the liquid band + de-syncs the single-`sin` breath so the membrane never reads mechanical. Gradient noise (not lattice value noise) is the SOTA choice — marbled, not blocky.

Apple Liquid Glass restraint doctrine — 'present, but not distracting' (WWDC25 §219 / createwithswift). The canonical SOTA design principle for the mood model + ambient use: ambient UI layers SUPPORT focus rather than compete for it; large surfaces do NOT flip light↔dark because the transition would be distracting; motion is organic and lightweight, responding to touch. This is the 'arresting not distracting' balance codified — the blob must be a calm, weightless, on-palette ambient mark, NOT a busy attention-grab. Drives the W15/W16 'keep it calm by default' tuning (small pulseAmp, slow cycles).

Stripe/Linear ambient-gradient discipline — controlled sophistication + computation restraint. Stripe's hero gradient: exactly 4 cohesive stops, a SLOW drift (not frenetic), constrained to a section (intentional, not full-bleed-dominating), disabled via a scroll/visibility observer when offscreen (compute restraint), and a minimal WebGL impl. The design philosophy is 'controlled sophistication' — vibrant but legible, premium via DISCIPLINE not maximalism. This is the exact posture for the blob: few stops, slow, on-palette, paused when not visible (the substrate's offscreen-park is the same instinct made structural).

Calm-tech / WCAG-2.2.2 motion governance (the W16 integration backbone). Premium ambient motion is OBLIGATED to: respect prefers-reduced-motion (vestibular disorders affect ~35% of adults over 40 — paint one static frame then park, substrate-owned via live matchMedia since CSS can't reach a JS rAF); carry a user-reachable pause control for any >5s auto-starting non-essential background (WCAG 2.2.2 Level A, available to ALL users not just PRM); and quiesce/park offscreen for battery. glass-ui's useWebGLCanvas already owns the PRM freeze + offscreen park; W16 makes the DockBackgroundToggle pause SEAM real (the dead-defineExpose bug) and adds the onscreen-idle quiescence gate — the calm-tech compute discipline made structural.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD, mapped to the three waves. W08 (un-flood): the IQ smin math is the EXACT root-cause proof — k is normalized correctly in the shader (`k*=4.0` is right, leave sdf-body.glsl.ts alone), so the flood is purely the COUPLED INPUT (uploaded k ≈0.216 → effective ≈0.864 in a 0.5-half-extent space, ~6.3× the working band) plus the missing POS_SCALE on the smin upload. The Codrops k=7-in-tiny-units lesson is the conceptual key: re-derive smoothK AS A RATIO of bodyRadius (target effective seam-pull ~0.03-0.08, default smoothK ~0.04-0.05, mood as a 1.0-centred multiplier), restore `* POS_SCALE` so the band rides the same coordinate compression as every other length. The conservative-SDF property (|∇f|≤1 regardless of k) PROVES this is a tuning fix, not an architecture change. W15 (contained lit droplet): solve body+orbit+satellite+smin as ONE footprint budget (~70-80% of the wrapper) — the Codrops droplet is contained because the whole scene is sub-unit; ours must be re-derived DOWN against the half-box. Then flip the SOTA features ON by default (lit dome via SDF-gradient normal, low fast-SSS back-light + coreGlow for the gel read, low warm-pearl iridescence, warped-FBM liquid membrane at ~1.8/~0.42, warm-cream specular tint NOT white) — the W9/W10/W11 work all ships but paints nothing under the oversized field; containment resurfaces it AND makes the already-wired pointer-trail/squash legible (re-scale magnitudes against the smaller body, no new code). Derive the DEFAULT palette from glass-ui warm tokens (OKLCh, in-family) so the un-themed blob belongs to the cream-glass system — the cold-blue demo bindings are the wrong identity. The MOOD MODEL: anchor it in the Apple restraint doctrine — moods are a calm valence/arousal swing on a few scalars (smoothK multiplier, pulse, iridescence intensity), never a busy attention-grab; 'excited' is a subtle lift, 'sleepy' a subtle settle, all on-palette. W16 (integration/perf): the calm-tech governance is the spine — make the DockBackgroundToggle pause seam REAL (v-model:paused, the recommended declarative shape, binding the existing renderer pause()/resume()), give shouldContinue a genuine at-rest quiescence predicate (park when mood settled + pointer at rest + trail collapsed + no merge, wake from the satellite scheduler) so an idle ambient blob does not burn 60fps (the Stripe scroll-observer discipline made structural), bound the multi-instance WebGL-context cap (route the static register to the WatercolorDot sibling; reserve GooBlob for the ONE interactive hero), and add the half-res quality axis for weak GPUs. The research-backed README: state the fidelity bar (single-pass WebGL2 SDF metaball, OKLCh in-family color, restraint-first ambient accent), cite the SOTA lineage (IQ smin/normals/warp, Codrops droplet, Zucconi SSS, Apple/Stripe restraint, Ottosson OKLCh, WCAG 2.2.2), and a planned→landed sweep with a defineExpose-currency gate.
pitfalls: FILL-RATE is the cost and it is QUADRATIC in DPR — the substrate's 2× DPR clamp is load-bearing (Retina is already 4× the fragment work). The fragment runs FBM×3 octaves TWICE per pixel + a full OKLCh round-trip; W15 turning lit/SSS/iridescence ON by default ADDS the 4-tap surfaceNormal sceneDist (which QUADRUPLES the field cost per pixel). W16 MUST gate the 4-tap behind the lit/iridescence/SSS path only, add the pre-FBM bounding discard, and trim the oversize margin — or the contained-lit default ships a fill-rate regression on the very surfaces it improves.

Re-flooding across the W08→W15 wave seam (the POS_SCALE trap). W08 takes the MINIMAL un-flood (restore POS_SCALE on smin, re-tune the band). The ratified disposition is W15 KEEPS W08's POS_SCALE regime and re-derives geometry ON TOP of it — NOT a partial migration to raw-normalized units that re-floods what W08 just compressed. If a full re-expression is ever ratified it MUST be ONE atomic re-derivation of the ENTIRE length cohort (body/sat/orbit/smin/noise) in a single wave with proof:blob-render as the regression lock. Never split the coordinate-system decision across the seam.

The static-math gate false-green (the cardinal AX lesson). proof:blob-smin-normalized shipped GREEN while the blob was a canvas-filling slab — it grep'd the fudge-deletion that BROKE the render + a pure-math k-sweep in ISOLATION; it never composed config.smoothK × mood/DEFAULTS against the body radius, never rendered a pixel. EVERY blob gate (gradient-unit-length, spec-premult, space-gamma, mood-resolved, tempo-suppression) is static. The ONLY trustworthy close is a rendered-pixel readback (proof:blob-render) + a live multi-viewport light/dark audit. Do not trust source-string gates for a visual defect.

WebGL readback returns 0 against this substrate. preserveDrawingBuffer:false clears post-composite AND the demand-loop parks, so naive readPixels/drawImage reads black. The gate MUST use a preserveDrawingBuffer:true test context (the W00 harness) or assert on the on-screen screenshot. A born-RED gate authored against a naive readback would itself be false.

Linear-in-without-an-OETF-out ships ~2.2× too dark (the named A5/A2 trap). The lit/SSS/iridescence terms enter `lin` in LINEAR space BEFORE linearToSrgb AND before the *alpha premultiply — a post-OETF apply double-gammas the highlight and fringes the premultiplied edge. proof:blob-space-gamma locks it. Any new surface term W15 adds must enter in linear, before the mandatory OETF.

value.js parseCSSColor CANNOT parse var(--token) and THROWS once per frame (the confirmed AW.W13 live bug). A token color must be DOM-cascade-unwrapped to a concrete rgb() before the ColorResolver sees it. The fix is ONE resolveTokenColor leaf with getComputedStyle appearing exactly ONCE (W16) — currently duplicated in BOTH GooBlob.vue and useMetaballRenderer.ts, leaking DOM into the supposed-DOM-free renderer seam.

The multi-instance WebGL-context cap (~8-16/page in Chromium; commit 9427536 hit it live). Each GooBlob grabs its own context; IntersectionPause stops the rAF but does NOT release the context. A blob GRID exhausts the cap and the Nth blob silently blanks. Route the static/decorative register to the CSS/SVG WatercolorDot sibling — a thumbnail does not need its own GL context. Reserve the GL blob for the one interactive hero.

Restraint is the design failure mode, not a nice-to-have. Apple explicitly dials motion DOWN; Stripe constrains its gradient to a section and pauses it offscreen. A blob with fast cycles, large pulseAmp, garish maximal-rainbow iridescence, or many stacked large instances reads CHEAP and becomes a vestibular trigger. Keep pulseAmp ≤~0.012, cycles slow, iridescence a warm-pearl SHEEN not a thin-film rainbow, and the palette few-stop and on-palette. The blob is an ambient accent that supports focus, never competes for it.

The dead-but-documented integration seam (the W16 headline). GooBlob.vue discards the renderer return so pause/resume are never exposed; the README documents them and the optional-chain `?.` SILENTLY swallows the undefined — a consumer gets a WCAG-2.2.2 pause button that does nothing with zero error. The declarative v-model:paused shape makes the seam structurally un-droppable. Never add a fallback pause path 'just in case' — the ?.-swallow IS the anti-pattern.

The onscreen-idle perpetual loop. shouldContinue(){return !paused} reschedules the rAF forever even at rest — a 7rem ambient accent burns full 60fps (FBM×3 twice + OKLCh round-trip per pixel) indefinitely. The README's 'parks aggressively' claim covers ONLY offscreen/hidden/PRM, never onscreen-idle. The quiescence predicate (park at rest, wake from the satellite scheduler) is the biggest battery lever after offscreen-park — the calm-tech compute discipline.

Demo bindings carrying the WRONG identity. The three blob stories bind cold-blue `oklch(0.7 0.16 250)` — not the warm-cream house identity the README claims. A var(--primary) blob can ALSO wash out in dark mode without a foreground-aware min-contrast rim guard. Re-point the demos to warm and guard the dark wash, or the storybook advertises a cold bubble the library is not.

notes.facet: Reference surveys — Inigo Quilez SDF articles, the Shadertoy metaball canon, soft-body game-dev techniques applicable to UI
sotaTechniques: IQ 2024 normalized smooth-minimum (the keystone for W08 un-flood): the 2024 smin rewrite reframes every smin as `b - k*g(x)` with x=(b-a)/k and a per-variant NORMALIZATION factor so k is a real distance-units blend band (k = the exact max inflation/thickening the two shapes undergo). The blob's sdf-body.glsl ALREADY ports this correctly (`k*=4.0` quadratic, `k*=1/(1-sqrt(0.5))` circular). Mechanism: with normalization, a uSmoothK of 0.2 reads as a ~0.2-unit meniscus measurable against the SAME UV scale as bodyRadius/satRadius/orbitRadius. This is the exact diagnostic the W08 flood needs: the math is normalized but the COMPOSED k (~0.21) + the missing POS_SCALE upload land an effective in-shader band ~6x the working width in a 1.0-wide UV.

IQ CD-family 'rigid + conservative + local' selection criteria: the article classifies smins by Rigid (no distortion outside the blend band), Local (effect confined), Conservative (never overestimates distance — raymarch-safe), Associative (order-independent for N inputs). Quadratic and circular are Rigid+Conservative; exponential/root/sigmoid are NOT rigid (they distort the shape everywhere, even far from the seam). Mechanism: IQ's stated default is quadratic ('fast, close enough to circular, never overestimates'); circular is the choice ONLY when you want a true quarter-circle fillet (the rounder/wetter premium-droplet seam).

IQ 2D distance-gradient = free fake normal (the lit-droplet keystone): the gradient of a 2D SDF is the outward surface direction; lifted to pseudo-3D via a dome-height z = sqrt(1-(1-interior)^2) it gives a per-pixel normal for Blinn-Phong + Fresnel WITHOUT raymarching. The blob's surfaceNormal() already does this via the IQ 4-tap tetrahedron gradient on the COMPOSITE field (the normal must ride the same smin/FBM field the alpha is cut from, not a clean circle) with a screen-space epsilon (~1.5px/resolution.y) so it tracks pixel size at any zoom.

Barre-Brisebois/Bouchard fast translucency (GDC 2011, via Alan Zucconi) for the SSS mood-axis: a cheap back-light term `pow(saturate(dot(V, -(L + N*distortion))), power) * scale * thickness` fakes light transmitted THROUGH a thin translucent body, using an SDF-estimated thickness (here `-d/bodyR`). The blob already ships this (uSssScale/uSssPower/distortion-by-N*thickness). SOTA mood mapping: drive scale/power off the arousal axis (excited shimmers, sleepy is flat) — already wired via iridScale.

Russell circumplex affect model (valence x arousal) for the mood model: a 2-axis continuous core where each named emotion is a POINT, so moods read off ONE principled surface instead of being hand-tuned in isolation. The blob's useBlobMood already implements this exactly (MOOD_AVA points + paramsFor() deriving all 12 MoodParams from {valence, arousal}; arousal -> motion energy, valence -> palette warmth + pointer lean). This is the canonical, research-correct framing — keep it; the SOTA refinement is to also map arousal onto smin (gooier when energized) and the squash magnitude.

Volume-preserving squash-and-stretch from velocity (the soft-body shortcut, no sim): the classic Disney principle re-expressed as an anisotropic UV basis q=(dot/sa, dot*sa) with sa=1+|v|*k and EXACTLY 1/sa on the perpendicular axis (preserves area — `1-amt` shrinks the blob at speed). The blob already does this in sceneDist(). This buys ~80% of the JellyCar/World-of-Goo soft-body FEEL for zero Verlet/mass-spring cost — the correct UI-grade tradeoff (full soft-body physics is overkill for a decorative accent).

Pointer-trail pseudopod (the reach-toward-cursor limb): a fixed-size array of decaying-radius spheres (newest at index 0, radius tapering r*=1-i/N) smin-merged into the body so an elastic limb stretches toward the cursor and snaps back. The blob ships this (TRAIL_N=15, dynamic break on uTrailCount). This is the SAME mechanism as the canonical Codrops droplet reference's uPointerTrail — confirmed current-SOTA.

fwidth-derived anti-aliased SDF edge: `aa = max(fwidth(d), 1e-6); alpha = 1 - smoothstep(-aa, aa, d)` derives the smoothstep half-width from the SDF's screen-space gradient so the edge stays ~1px at any zoom. The blob ships this — and it is STRICTLY AHEAD of the canonical Codrops reference, which uses fixed-epsilon thresholds with no adaptive AA.

Interleaved Gradient Noise dither (Jimenez, CoD:AW 2014) to kill OKLCh/warm-cream banding: `fract(52.9829189 * fract(dot(p, vec2(0.06711056, 0.00583715))))` is a cheap (dot+fract) low-discrepancy dither added at ~1/255 amplitude pre-quantization to break the 8-bit banding that smooth OKLCh gradients + the warm-cream core glow produce. Aurora already ships this; the blob README flags it as planned to land with the W15 surface finish — it should be ON by W15 for the lit warm-cream default (the gradient most prone to banding).
